title: Non-Driver ID Card
body:
Need something else? [Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02056) for information or complaints about DMV offices or employees If you do not have a driver license, you can apply for a non-driver photo ID card (also known as a New York State ID). Individuals of all ages can apply. You need to complete form "MV-44" and provide proof of identity and birth date (birth certificate and Social Security Card) to apply. You must apply for an original non-driver ID in a DMV office. This cannot be done online, by mail, or by phone. If you have a disability and are not able to go in person, email [accessibility@dmv.ny.gov](mailto:accessibility@dmv.ny.gov) to request an accommodation. You can also get information on how to renew a photo ID or how to report a lost or stolen photo ID. Online [Visit the DMV website.](https://dmv.ny.gov/) [Learn about DMV transactions that can be done online.](https://dmv.ny.gov/transactions/online-license-and-id-transactions) [Learn how to apply for or renew a non-driver ID card.](https://dmv.ny.gov/non-driver-id/get-a-non-driver-id) [Find out what documents you need to apply for or renew non-driver ID.](https://process.dmv.ny.gov/documentguide/dmv_license/DisplayPages/pwizlicensePermitNDID.cfm) [Get the application for a driver license, learner permit, or non-driver ID card.](https://dmv.ny.gov/forms/mv44.pdf) [Make a reservation.](https://public.nydmvreservation.com/) By Phone
Agency: New York State Department of Motor Vehicles
Division: Department of Motor Vehicles Call Center
Phone Number: (800) 698-2931
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 4 PM
Staff is available through the automated phone system during business hours except for holidays. Automated assistance is available 24/7, including in Spanish. Call volume is often high. If you don't get through, call back later.
Enhanced ID vs. REAL ID
After May 7, 2025, only Enhanced or REAL ID driver licenses, permits, or non-driver IDs will be accepted to get on a domestic flight, enter certain federal buildings or military bases (unless you have a Passport). If you plan to travel, it is recommended you upgrade before May 7, 2025. Both Enhanced and REAL IDs:  Are Federal REAL ID compliant Can be used for photo identification purposes Can be used to board a domestic flight (within the U.S.) Can be used to enter a federal building or military base Show your full legal name (first, middle, last) Show your residential address (where you live) Require an office visit to prove your: Identity - if your name has changed bring in marriage certificate(s), divorce decree(s) or court order document(s) NY State residency U.S. citizenship Date of birth Social Security status An Enhanced license, permit, or non-driver ID: Can be used to cross a U.S. border coming from Canada, Mexico, and some Caribbean countries (it is not acceptable for air travel between these countries) Costs an additional $30 on top of the regular transaction fees Has an American flag displayed on the document A REAL ID license, permit, or non-driver ID: Does not have additional cost, but all regular transaction fees will apply Has a star displayed on the document [Schedule an appointment with the DMV.](https://public.nydmvreservation.com/)
Mobile ID (MiD)
New York State residents can download the MiD App on their smartphone. The app is a secure digital version of your state-issued driver’s license, permit or non-driver ID. [Learn more about the Mobile ID (MiD).](https://dmv.ny.gov/id-card/mobile-id-mid)
DMV Office Locations
Reservations are recommended when visiting a Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) location. Bronx Bronx Terminal Market 610 Exterior Street, Level 6 Monday - Friday: 7:30 AM - 5 PM LIMITED SERVICES ONLY Bronx License Center 1350 Commerce Avenue (between Waterbury Avenue and Halsey Street) Monday - Friday: 7:30 AM - 5 PM LIMITED SERVICES ONLY Brooklyn Coney Island Office 2875 West 8th Street (between Sheepshead Bay Road and Surf Avenue) Monday - Friday: 7:30 AM - 5 PM Atlantic Center Office 625 Atlantic Avenue, 2nd Floor (between Fort Greene Place and 6th Avenue) Monday - Friday: 7:30 AM - 5 PM Manhattan Harlem Office 5 West 125th Street, 2nd Floor (between Malcolm X Boulevard and 5th Avenue) Monday - Friday: 7:30 AM - 5 PM Midtown Manhattan Office 366 West 31st Street (between 8th and 9th Avenues) Monday - Friday: 7:30 AM - 5 PM Lower Manhattan Office 11 Greenwich Street (at Battery Place) Monday - Friday: 7:30 AM - 5 PM  ***Please note that the License Express DMV office, located at 145 West 30th Street, is closed until further notice.*** Queens College Point Office 30-56 Whitestone Expressway (between Downing Street and 31st Avenue), Flushing Monday - Friday: 7:30 AM - 5 PM Springfield Gardens Office 168-35 Rockaway Boulevard (between 148th Avenue and 175th Street), Springfield Gardens Monday - Friday: 7:30 AM - 5 PM Jamaica Office 168-46 91st Avenue, 2nd Floor (between 168th and 169th Streets), Jamaica Monday - Friday: 7:30 AM - 5 PM Queens Hall (License Express DMV) 65-21 Main Street, Room 130 Monday - Friday: 7:30 AM - 5 PM Staten Island Richmond Office 1775 South Avenue, Suite 2 (at Spencer Street) Monday - Friday: 7:30 AM - 5 PM

Point and Insurance Reduction Program (PIRP)
The Point and Insurance Reduction Program (PIRP) is also known as the Defensive Driving Course or Motor Vehicle Accident Prevention Course. Private companies and organizations throughout New York State offer this course. Completing an approved course will: Refresh your driving knowledge Help to prevent you from losing your license in the event you accrued 11 or more points on your driving record Reduce the base rate of your auto and motorcycle insurance premiums 10% each year for three years Completing a course does not : Prevent a mandatory suspension or revocation Eliminate your responsibility to pay a driver responsibility assessment Give you a way to reduce future driver violation points [Learn more about PIRP and find an approved course.](https://dmv.ny.gov/points-and-penalties/pirp-and-ipirp)

You can download the complaint form online. [Download the Driver Training Programs Complaint Form.](https://dmv.ny.gov/forms/dtp201.pdf) Send the completed form: By Mail New York State Department of Motor Vehicles Driver Training Programs 6 Empire State Plaza, Room 327  Albany, NY 12228 By Fax (518) 473-0160

title: Police Officer Complaint
body:
Call 911 Call 911  to report criminal activity or serious misconduct by an on-duty or off-duty police officer or civilian member of the New York City Police Department.
Need something else? [City Agency Record or FOIL Request](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01021) to request police officer records [City Agency or Worker Feedback](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01662) to file a complaint against a civilian employee of the NYPD (such as a crossing guard, 911 agent, or traffic agent) You can report police officer misconduct involving a member of the NYPD to the Civilian Complaint Review Board (CCRB), including: Force  Abuse of authority, such as threats or improper searches and seizures Discourtesy, such as profanity or crude gestures Offensive language regarding race, ethnicity, sexuality, gender identity/gender expression, etc. CCRB will investigate the complaint, and if it finds that misconduct occurred, they will recommend discipline to the Police Commissioner.
You can file a police officer misconduct complaint by contacting CCRB. Online [Report police officer misconduct.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/ccrb/complaints/file-a-complaint/file-online.page) [Learn more about the CCRB and how complaints are investigated.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/ccrb/about/about.page) In Person or By Mail Civilian Complaint Review Board  100 Church Street, 10th Floor  New York, NY 10007 Hours: Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM (No appointment necessary) By Phone
Agency: Civilian Complaint Review Board
Division: Complaints Unit
Phone Number: (800) 341-2272
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Leave a message after hours and you'll get a call back.
Other Ways to File a Complaint You can also file complaints with a [City Council Member](https://council.nyc.gov/districts/) in your borough or in person at any police precinct. To find your local precinct, go to the [Police Precincts and PSAs](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01027) page.
Check the Status of a Complaint
You can check the status of your complaint online. You will need to provide the Complaint Tracking Number that was issued to you by CCRB. [Check the status of your complaint using your CCRB case number.](https://apps.nyc.gov/ccrb-status-lookup/)
Civilian Complaint Mediation
You can request mediation through the CCRB as an alternative way to resolve disputes with a police officer. Mediation is an opportunity for the complainant and the police officer to meet voluntarily to attempt to resolve their dispute without discipline.  You cannot request mediation for cases involving property damage or an allegation of excessive force that resulted in serious injury. [Learn more about the CCRB's mediation program.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/ccrb/mediation/mediation-process.page)
Business Card Received During a Police Stop
If you were stopped by an NYPD police officer, they may have given you a business card to identify themselves.  The Right to Know Act, in effect as of October 19, 2018, requires police officers to identify themselves by providing their name, rank, command, and shield number to civilians at the beginning of certain interactions, and to provide this information on a business card. The business card also has information about: How to request Body-Worn Camera footage How to request police stop information How to submit a comment or complaint about the police encounter The Right to Know Act also requires police officers to explain that searches will not be conducted if a person refuses to provide consent to the search, and that these requests must be documented. You can get more detailed information about the Right to Know Act and your rights under this law.  [Learn more about the Right to Know Act.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/ccrb/complaints/file-a-complaint/right-to-know-act.page) To get information about requesting a Stop Report or the release of body camera footage, go to the [Police Stops](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02531) page. Reporting a Violation of the Right to Know Act You can submit a comment or complaint about your interaction with the NYPD if you feel the police officer did not follow these guidelines. CCRB will investigate the report, and if it finds that misconduct occurred, they will recommend discipline to the Police Commissioner.  Online [Report police officer misconduct.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/ccrb/complaints/file-a-complaint/file-online.page) In Person or By Mail Civilian Complaint Review Board  100 Church Street, 10th Floor  New York, NY 10007 Hours: Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM (No appointment necessary) By Phone
CCRB does not investigate complaints against civilian members of the New York Police Department (NYPD), Department of Correction (DOC) Officers, or Port Authority Police Officers. You can submit [City Agency or Worker Feedback](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01662) if you have a complaint about: Civilian members of the NYPD DOC Officers Crossing Guards Traffic, Parking, or School Safety Agents 911 Operators
Agency: Civilian Complaint Review Board
Division: Complaints Unit
Phone Number: (800) 341-2272
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM

title: Electronics Disposal
body:
Need something else? [Lithium-Ion Battery Safety](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03565) [Special Waste Disposal](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01973)  [Waste Disposal for Businesses](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01787) for e-waste disposal rules for businesses [Battery Recycling](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02078) [Recycling Rules](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02013) [Residential Trash Rules](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02086) [Illegal Dumping](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02097) to report electronics that were illegally dumped on a sidewalk Some electronics contain hazardous materials, including lead, mercury, arsenic, and cadmium. You cannot  dispose of these electronics, also called e-waste, with your regular trash or recycling. E-waste includes: Computers and Computer Accessories Cables, cords, and wiring permanently fixed to a device Desktop towers and monitors Keyboards, mice, and pointing devices Laptops Printers and document scanners Servers (small-scale only) TV and Video Equipment Cable boxes, cable/satellite receivers, antennas, and digital converter boxes Cables, cords, and wiring permanently fixed to the TV TVs, VCRs, DVD players, and DVRs (digital video recorders) Portable Electronic Devices Cell phones Digital cameras Tablets (ex: iPads) and e-readers Portable music devices/digital music players (iPod, mp3 player, Walkman) Home Electronics Electronic keyboards Fax machines Video game consoles
If you need to dispose of an item not listed above, use the [How to Get Rid of Lookup](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/index.page#how-to-get-rid-of) online tool to learn how to dispose of it.
Disposal Options City residents have several options to dispose of e-waste. You can: [Donate](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/donate/site/) them if in working condition Enroll your apartment building to get pickups through the [ecycleNYC](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/what-we-do/programs/ecyclenyc.page) program Bring them to a [Special Waste Disposal](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01973) site or other electronics drop-off locations Return them to the manufacturer or retailer for recycling Tenants must appropriately discard their electronics. It is not the landlord's responsibility to take or mail back items for reuse or recycling. [Learn more about electronics disposal.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/collection/get-rid-of/electronics.page#disposal-options)
Donate
You can search for places in your neighborhood and throughout the City where you can donate working electronics on the donateNYC website. [Visit donateNYC.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/donate/site/)
Pickup for Apartment Buildings
Apartment buildings with 10 or more units can participate in ecycleNYC, a free and convenient in-building service to remove and recycle unwanted electronics. Service options include: Room clean-outs for buildings with 10 or more units Storage bins for buildings with 100 or more units Building events for buildings with 250 or more units Buildings, management companies, or residents can apply to enroll in ecycleNYC online. If you're not sure if your building is already enrolled in this program, check with your building manager. [Learn more and apply for ecycleNYC.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/what-we-do/programs/ecyclenyc.page)  Pickups If your building is enrolled in ecycleNYC, a building manager or staff member can request pickup of unwanted electronics. Pickup is guaranteed within 5 business days.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Drop-Off Locations
City Drop-Off Locations You can drop off electronics for free at Special Waste Sites or seasonal SAFE Disposal Events. Learn more on the [Special Waste Disposal](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01973) page. Other Locations [View a map of electronics drop-off locations](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/collection/get-rid-of/e-waste-drop-off-sites.page) or contact the following businesses or organizations to drop off, recycle, or donate your electronics. Please note that some sites charge fees or don't accept certain items. Check the location’s website or contact them to confirm before you drop off the items. Best Buy [Visit Best Buy's website.](https://www.bestbuy.com/site/services/recycling/pcmcat149900050025.c)
Agency: Best Buy
Phone Number: (888) 237-8289
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Goodwill [Visit Goodwill's website.](https://www.goodwillnynj.org/donate-goods)
Agency: Goodwill Industries of Greater New York and Northern New Jersey
Phone Number: (718) 728-5400
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Salvation Army [Visit Salvation Army's website.](https://satruck.org/)
Agency: Salvation Army
Phone Number: (800) 728-7825
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Staples [Visit Staples' website.](https://www.staples.com/sbd/cre/marketing/sustainability-center/recycling-services/electronics/)
Agency: Staples
Phone Number: (800) 333-3330
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Take-Back Programs
You can return unwanted electronics to manufacturers for recycling or disposal for free. Electronic manufacturers, such as Samsung, Sony, or Toshiba, must accept electronics from residents at no cost. Cell phones can also be dropped off at any store that sells service plans. You can find more information about recycling electronics at the store where you purchased the item or at any store that sells the item. You can also call the manufacturer or check your brand's website. The NY State Department of Environmental Conservation (NYSDEC) keeps a list of registered electronics manufacturers and information about their e-waste acceptance programs on its website. [Find e-waste acceptance programs.](https://www.dec.ny.gov/chemical/82084.html) Store or Manufacturer Complaints You make a report to the NYSDEC Tip Line about a: Electronics manufacturer that doesn't accept their products for recycling Store that sells electronics but doesn't have information about electronics recycling The NYSDEC Tip Line only takes complaints. It does not provide recycling or disposal locations.
Agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
Division: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation Tip Line
Phone Number: (800) 847-7332
Business Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week
Schools
Electronics cannot go in regular recycling or trash. Schools must follow specific guidelines for disposal. For more information on electronics disposal for New York City Public Schools, you can email your question to [WasteSupport@schools.nyc.gov](mailto:WasteSupport@schools.nyc.gov).

title: Tire Disposal
body:
It is illegal to place car tires in the trash. However, you can set out bicycle tires with your trash. You can bring tires to any business that sells them. New York State law requires businesses that sell tires to take back used tires for recycling. These businesses include: Tire shops Auto parts stores Vehicle repair shops New car dealerships The Department of Sanitation will accept up to four tires from passenger vehicles at Special Waste Sites. Learn more on the [Special Waste Disposal](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01973) page. DSNY District Garages will also accept up to four car tires Monday through Saturday, 10 AM - 5:30 PM, except holidays.  [Get a list of DSNY District Garages.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/about/about-dsny/garage-locations.page) DSNY facilities will accept tires from NYC residents with a valid New York State driver's license and a valid New York State vehicle registration both with New York City addresses. No commercial vehicles are allowed. Tires do not have to be removed from rims.

title: NYC311 Feedback
body:
Need something else? [City Agency or Worker Feedback](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01662) [Service Request Status](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01066) We believe government works best when everyone's voice can be heard. We'd love to hear what you think about the service we've provided.
Feedback About Service Requests
When you file a service request (SR) with NYC311, it is automatically forwarded to the appropriate City agency for investigation and resolution. NYC311 sends survey offers when the agency closes SRs. Survey offers are emailed or texted using the contact information provided in the SR. Anonymous SRs do not receive offers. Please note that this survey data is used to broadly measure and improve City services, not to address individual SRs. If you’d like to provide direct or detailed feedback about the way a City agency handled an SR you filed, use the [City Agency or Worker Feedback](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01662) page. If the SR you're providing feedback about has been closed but the issue remains unresolved, you should also refile the SR.
Submit Other NYC311 Feedback
You can submit a complaint or compliment about NYC311, including comments about customer service, language accessibility, and your general experience. You can give feedback about the following NYC311 channels: NYC311 Website NYC311 Call Center NYC311 App NYC311 Open Data NYC311 Social Media NYC311 Text [Send feedback about NYC311.](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/submit-feedback/) Please note that the feedback form above is not monitored 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.  If this is an emergency, call 911 immediately.  For non-emergency inquiries or requests, call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to speak with a representative who will be able to assist you. NYC311 is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
File Service Requests
If you want the City to address a specific problem at a particular location, search NYC311 Online's [Report Problems](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/report-problems/#pills-all-by-category) page for the problem you want to report. You can also [contact us](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/about-nyc-311/#contact-us) through one of our other channels.

title: Medical Waste Disposal
body:
Need something else? [Special Waste Disposal](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01973) for medicine or prescription drugs [Loose Syringes](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02475) to report loose syringes or medical needles on public property The City does not collect medical trash, except for syringes used in a residence. Sharps Disposal You can bring properly packaged and labeled used syringes and lancets (also known as "sharps") to any hospital or nursing home in New York State. NY hospitals and nursing homes are required by law to act as collection centers. You should contact the hospital or nursing home first for specific drop-off days and times. Many local pharmacies and healthcare providers who provide sharps also participate in the voluntary sharps collection program. [View a map of pharmaceutical and sharps drop-off locations.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/collection/get-rid-of/pharmaceutical-sharps-drop-off.page) You can also drop off sharps at a SAFE Disposal Event. If you aren't using a sharps disposal program: Place the sharps in a leak-proof, puncture-resistant container. When the container is full, seal the lid securely, tape it closed, and label the container “Home Sharps - not for recycling." Place the container with trash for regular trash collection. Don't put syringes or lancets or sharps containers with recycling. [Learn more about used syringe and lancet disposal.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/collection/get-rid-of/medical-waste.page#sharps-residents) Other Medical Waste [Learn how to dispose of medical waste other than syringes and needles.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/collection/get-rid-of/medical-waste.page) You can also hire a licensed carter. [Get a list of licensed and registered carting companies.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/bic/industries/carter-information.page) Medicine Printed materials that come with prescription medication should be referred to for specific disposal instructions. Most prescription drugs should be mixed with an undesirable substance (such as used coffee grounds or kitty litter) and put in impermeable, non-descript containers (such as empty cans or sealable bags) before throwing them out in the trash. COVID-19 Test Kits Throw out COVID-19 test kits with your regular trash. These test kits are not considered medical waste.
SAFE Disposal Events
You can dispose of your special waste at SAFE Disposal Events (Solvents, Automotive, Flammable, Electronics). SAFE Events are usually held in the fall. Only residential waste from New York City is accepted. You must bring a valid ID and proof of NYC residency, such as a phone or utility bill. Commercial waste and commercial vehicles are not  allowed at SAFE Events. [Learn more about SAFE Disposal Events.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/what-we-do/programs/safe-disposal-events.page) Upcoming SAFE Events There are no SAFE Disposal Events scheduled at this time. Check back in Fall 2026 for more information. Items Accepted Automotive products Antifreeze Car batteries Gasoline Motor oil Transmission fluid Batteries Cleaning products Corrosive liquids Cosmetics or beauty products Hair developer Nail polish Electronics Computers and computer accessories TV and video equipment [Additional items](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02385) Fire extinguishers Flammable liquids Gas, helium, oxygen, or propane tanks Ink or toner cartridges Lawn and garden care products Light bulbs (compact fluorescent or tubes) Medical waste Medication Sharps (syringes, lancets) ​Paint Paint cans Spray paint Thermometers and thermostats Items Not Accepted Appliances with [CFC or Freon](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01792) Air conditioners Dehumidifiers Refrigerators or freezers Asbestos Commercial waste Cooking oil or grease Tires Waste generated from outside New York City
Report Improper Disposal
You can report improper syringe or sharp disposal.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Hospital Refusing Sharps
You can file a complaint against a hospital that does not accept syringes or lancets for safe disposal.
Agency: New York State Department of Health
Division: Hospital Complaints Hotline
Phone Number: (800) 804-5447
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8:30 AM - 4:45 PM
Nursing Home Refusing Sharps
You can file a complaint against a nursing home that does not accept syringes or lancets for safe disposal.
Agency: New York State Department of Health
Division: Nursing Home Complaint Hotline
Phone Number: (888) 201-4563
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 4:45 PM
Staff is available during business hours, except State and Federal Holidays. Leave a message after hours and you'll get a call back.

body:

Medicaid Buy-In Program for Working People with Disabilities
Working people with disabilities, age 16 to 64, may be eligible for Medicaid health care coverage. You may be eligible even if your income is over the Medicaid limit. [Learn more about the Medicaid Buy-in Program for Working People with Disabilities.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/mbi-wpd.page)

Individuals Who Have Medicare
The Health Insurance Information Counseling and Assistance Program (HIICAP) offers free counseling about health benefits to disabled individuals who have Medicare.  You must make an appointment for in-person assistance. [Learn more about HIICAP.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dfta/services/health-insurance-assistance.page)

body:
Need something else? [Special Education](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03011) to find other services for public school students with disabilities You can get information about programs and services available for students who are blind or have low vision and for students who are deaf or hard of hearing.
Blind or Low Vision Student Assistance
New York City Public Schools (NYCPS) offers Education Vision Services (EVS), which serves blind and low vision students ages 5 to 21. The program is part of Special Education District 75. EVS Referrals NYCPS places students in EVS programs by referral only. Students usually come to the program in one of three ways: A parent or teacher refers the child to the school Committee on Special Education (CSE). The child is then evaluated by the specialized CSE for the Hearing Handicapped and Visually Impaired (HHVI). A parent calls EVS to make inquiries and is referred to HHVI. An eye doctor refers a child to the State Commission for the Blind, which in turn asks the parent to contact HHVI. Students must have a report from an eye doctor to enter the program. EVS Curriculum The EVS curriculum is built for the specialized needs of students who are blind or low vision.  Students get Resource Room (Supplemental Instruction) Services to help them participate fully in a regular classroom. The EVS curriculum follows the National Agenda for Children and Youth with Visual Impairment. Jobs for EVS Students EVS arranges community-based work experiences for students. It places students in the Summer Youth Employment Program and the Training Opportunities Program, gives school-to-work transition plans, and provides ongoing training inside and outside the classroom.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Additional Resources You can also learn about other services and programs for blind or low vision students through the Mayor’s Office for People with Disabilities (MOPD). [Get information about educational support for students who are blind or low vision.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/mopd/resources/disability-specific-blind-low-vision-schools.page)
Deaf or Hard of Hearing Student Assistance
New York City Public Schools offers Hearing Education Services (HES) that focus on bringing deaf and hard of hearing students into the mainstream educational environment.  HES evaluates students, places them in appropriate learning environments, and provides support services. You can get more information about HES. Types of Support Provided by HES​ HES provides educational support through: Audiology Speech therapy Sign language interpreting Note-takers Counseling Tutoring Transition services Work-study programs HES has three parts: The Related Service Program  provides auditory training, speech reading, receptive and expressive language development, speech and academic support. The Resource Room Program  provides additional help for students in need. The Self-Contained Program  provides instruction in a separate setting with a smaller student to teacher ratio.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Additional Resources You can also learn about other services and programs for deaf or hard of hearing students through the Mayor’s Office for People with Disabilities (MOPD).  [Get information about educational support for students who are deaf or hard of hearing.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/mopd/resources/deaf-education.page)

title: Sidewalk Cleaning
body:
Need something else? [Dirty Sidewalk](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01803) to report a sidewalk or gutter, including 18 inches into the street, that is not clean [Sidewalk Washing Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01937) to report someone washing a sidewalk outside of permitted hours Property owners must clean the sidewalks next to their property and 18 inches from the curb into the street. The Department of Sanitation (DSNY) inspects sidewalks during specific times of the day. Sidewalk cleaning enforcement times depend on the type of property.
Residential Properties
DSNY agents can only issue violations for dirty sidewalks next to residential properties from 8 AM to 9 AM and from 6 PM to 7 PM, 7 days a week.
Commercial Properties
Commercial property enforcement times are limited to two 1-hour periods per day. The exact times depend on the Sanitation section the address is located in. When businesses are closed they must arrange to have the area maintained.
[Look up commercial enforcement routing times for a specific address.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dsny/forms/enforcement-routing-times)
Mixed-Use Properties
Mixed-use properties are used for both commercial and residential purposes. Enforcement times depend on the use of the first floor of the building where the violation occurs. If the business on the first floor is operating, DSNY can issue violations during commercial routing times for the address.
[Look up commercial enforcement routing times for a specific address.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dsny/forms/enforcement-routing-times)
If the business on the first floor is permanently closed or vacant, DSNY can issue violations only during residential routing times. Residential routing times are 8 AM to 9 AM and 6 PM to 7 PM, 7 days a week.

title: DOB NOW
body:
DOB NOW is the Department of Buildings'(DOB) self-service online tool for Owners, Design Professionals, Licensees, and Filing Representatives. You can submit applications, make payments, schedule appointments, check application or inspection status, pull permits, and file renewals. [Learn more about DOB NOW.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/industry/using-dob-now.page) [Check upcoming DOB NOW Training sessions.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/dob/upcoming-events.page) [Access archived DOB NOW Training sessions.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/industry/dob-now-training.page) NYC.ID Account Starting on June 3, 2024, all existing and new DOB NOW users are required to have an NYC.ID account. Users will complete a one-time process of creating an NYC.ID account An NYC.ID account is required to access DOB NOW: Build Safety BIS Options Licensing DOB NOW: Inspections and eFiling account registration is not changing and will not require an NYC.ID account [See NYC.ID announcement.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dobnow_login_sn.pdf) Visit [nyc.gov/dobnowtips](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/industry/dob-now-registration-tips.page) to learn more.
DOB NOW: Build
You must use DOB NOW: Build to submit plumbing, sprinkler, and fence filings to the Department of Buildings (DOB) if you're a: Professional Engineer Registered Architect Licensee Special Inspector Progress Inspector Filing Representative Owner You must be registered with eFiling to log into DOB NOW: Build. [Submit job filings, register for DOB NOW: Build, or get additional information.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/industry/dob-now-build.page) [Get help with Department of Buildings Self-Service Tools.](https://a810-efiling.nyc.gov/eRenewal/dobNowHelp.jsp) Additional assistance is available: By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
DOB NOW: Inspections
Licensed professionals and building owners must use the Department of Building's DOB NOW: Inspections portal to submit requests for development inspections of: Electrical Signs Fire Suppression Boilers Construction Cranes and Derricks Elevators Builders Pavement Plans (BPP) Oil Burning Equipment Sustainability High Rise Initiative Plumbing [Submit inspection requests, register for DOB NOW: Inspections, or get additional information.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/industry/dob-now-inspection.page) [Get help with Department of Buildings Self-Service Tools.](https://a810-efiling.nyc.gov/eRenewal/dobNowHelp.jsp) Additional assistance is available: By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
DOB NOW: Licensing
Licensed professionals must use DOB NOW: Licensing to submit new applications, reissuances, and renewals for the following: Master Plumber Master Fire Suppression Piping Contractor Welder Master Electrician Special Electrician [Submit license filings, register for DOB NOW: Licensing, or get additional information.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/industry/dob-now-licensing.page) [Get help with Department of Buildings Self-Service Tools.](https://a810-efiling.nyc.gov/eRenewal/dobNowHelp.jsp) Additional assistance is available: By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
DOB NOW: Safety
Licensed professionals must use DOB NOW: Safety to submit compliance filings for boilers and façades to the Department of Buildings (DOB). [Submit compliance filings, register for DOB NOW: Safety, or get additional information.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/industry/dob-now-safety.page) [Get help with Department of Buildings Self-Service Tools.](https://a810-efiling.nyc.gov/eRenewal/dobNowHelp.jsp) Additional assistance is available: By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
DOB NOW: BIS Options
You can request drawings, plans or documents for properties located in New York City, by submitting a Record Request online in DOB’s Building Information System (BIS) via DOB NOW: BIS Options. The following requests can be submitted in DOB NOW: BIS Options: Certificate of Correction Review Requests Civil Penalty Review Requests (L2) New License Applications License Renewal Applications Record Requests If you already have a DOB eFiling account, you can log into DOB NOW and select the BIS Options portal. [Log into DOB NOW.](https://nyc.gov/dobnow) You can create a new eFiling account.  [Register with eFiling.](https://a810-efiling.nyc.gov/eRenewal/loginER.jsp) For step-by-step directions, see the [Record Requests in DOB NOW guide.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/records_request_user_guide.pdf) Requests can be made for folders, plans, microfilm, docket books, reels, index/I-cards, and curb cut cards. Download [Record Requests in DOB NOW guide.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/records_request_user_guide.pdf) If Building Plans are in DOB’s inventory, once a record request is submitted in DOB NOW, an email notification is sent to the requestor when the records are available for pick up at the borough office where the property is located.

title: Water and Sewer Bill
body:
Need something else? [Water and Sewer Bill Payment](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02462) to make a payment, find out your current balance and payment due dates, and learn how your water bill is calculated [Water and Sewer Rate](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02465) for rate information [Water and Sewer Bill Dispute](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02461) to dispute charges on your bill or make complaints about water and sewer rate increase You can get information and assistance with your annual, semi-annual, and quarterly Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) water and sewer bills.   You can: Change the name on your water bill Arrange for a final meter reading Get assistance if you have received a Water Shutoff Notice letter Get information about financial assistance programs Online [Learn more about water and sewer bills.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/pay-my-bills/water-sewer-bills-frequently-asked-questions.page) If you sign up for a My DEP Account you can: View and pay your bill online Sign up for autopay and monthly billing Schedule appointments Submit requests online for: Billing disputes Refunds And more [Register or login to My DEP Account.](https://nyc.gov/mydep) By Email [customerservice@dep.nyc.gov](mailto:customerservice@dep.nyc.gov) By Phone
Agency: Department of Environmental Protection
Division: Bureau of Customer Services Water Meter Services and Billing
Phone Number: (718) 595-7000
Business Hours: Monday: 8 AM - 7 PM; Tuesday - Friday: 8 AM - 6 PM; Saturday: 9 AM - 12 PM
Payment Agreement
To enter into a payment agreement, contact DEP's Collection Unit at (718) 595-7890, Monday to Friday from 9 AM to 5 PM or email [collectionsunit@dep.nyc.gov](mailto:collectionsunit@dep.nyc.gov). To get more information about water shut offs, email [watershutoff@dep.nyc.gov](mailto:watershutoff@dep.nyc.gov).
Financial Assistance Programs
Two- and three-family owner-occupied properties that are facing foreclosure and are in the lien sale may be eligible to have their open water and sewer charges on the property temporarily set aside until the property is sold or refinanced. If you are experiencing difficulty paying your mortgage and other carrying costs, such as water and sewer charges, DEP has launched the Water Debt Assistance Program in conjunction with the New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development’s Mortgage Assistance Program. Qualified customers are offered immediate, temporary relief from water and sewer debt. To learn more about the Water Debt Assistance Program, use the [Water and Sewer Lien Sale](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02464) page.
Exemptions
Certain qualifying organizations may be entitled to an exemption from water and sewer charges. Eligibility depends on several factors and interested parties should review and complete the exemption application. All supporting documentation and required forms must be mailed or delivered to the address provided in the general instructions on the form. [Download the DEP Application for Exemption from Water and Sewer Charges.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dep/downloads/pdf/pay-my-bills/customer-service/application-for-exemption-from-water-and-sewer-charges.pdf) [Learn more about exemptions from water and sewer charges.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/pay-my-bills/how-we-bill-you.page)
Current Usage and Billing Information
The MY DEP ACCOUNT section of the DEP Website can provide current usage and billing information. The property owner can view their current account balance and calculate their consumption and charges. [Register or login to My DEP Account.](https://nyc.gov/mydep)
Account Information Update
The water and sewer account must remain in the name of the property owner. The owner can request their water and sewer bill to be sent to an alternate person, or for a copy of the bill to be sent to another interested party such as the tenant. Contact information for the owner, such as the mailing address, telephone number, and email address, can be updated by completing the Customer Registration Form and mailing it to the City's Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) at: NYC Department of Environmental Protection Attn:  Registration Unit 59-17 Junction Boulevard, 7th Floor Flushing, NY 11373 The Customer Registration Form is available: Online [Download form to register a new water and sewer account or to update owner contact information.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dep/downloads/pdf/pay-my-bills/customer-service/customer-registration-form.pdf) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to request a copy.
Final Water Meter Reading When Selling Property
You can request a Property Transfer Meter Reading (also known as a Title Read or Final Read) prior to the sale of your property. The current property owner should request the title read be done at least 30 days in advance of the closing. There is a $25 charge for this reading. An inspection will be scheduled if needed. This does not shut off water and sewer service to the property. When you sell or transfer a property, remember to take care of the following items for your water bill/account: Request a title water meter reading from DEP prior to closing Stop automated bill payments option on-line if enrolled Cancel Service Line Protection Program if enrolled Un-enroll from MY DEP on-line account access DEP does not shut off water or sewer services for property sales.

Division: Bureau of Customer Services Water Meter Services and Billing

title: Parade or Sound Permit
body:
Need something else? [Events](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01892) for information about upcoming street activities
Permits are required for local or large parades and protests. A local event is defined as an event with fewer than 1,000 expected participants that is not located on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan. A large event is defined as an event with more than 1,000 expected participants,  or  any event on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan. You must submit a notarized permit application at least two weeks before the event. You can mail the application if there is enough time, or you can drop it off Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 4 PM, at the following address: Investigation Review Section 300 Gold Street, Room 305 Brooklyn, NY 11201 If your event requires a loud speaker, megaphone, or other sound device, you will also need a Sound Device Permit. Submit the Sound Device Permit application at the local precinct where the event will take place. The fee for the Application for Sound Device Permit starts at $45 but varies based on the number of days you need it. Application forms and additional information for parade,and sound device permits are available online and in person at any police precinct. Online [Learn more about parade and sound permits and get application forms.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/services/law-enforcement/permits-licenses-permits.page) In Person
[Find a precinct or police service area (PSA) by address or zip code.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/bureaus/patrol/find-your-precinct.page) [Find a precinct by name.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/bureaus/patrol/precincts-landing.page) [Find a PSA by name.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/bureaus/transit-housing/housing.page)

title: Street Light Complaint
body:
Call 911 Call 911 to report a downed power line.
Need something else? [Street Light Installation or Relocation Request](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02491) to request a new street light or to have an existing street light relocated [Traffic Signal Complaint or Request](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01404) [Pedestrian Signal Complaint or Request](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01047) [Electrical Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01048) to report dangling or hanging power lines [Light from Parking Lot Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02259) You can report a problem with a street light to the Department of Transportation (DOT). You must provide a location of the street light condition. You do not need to leave contact information. If you provide an e-mail address, you will receive a service request confirmation email.
Report Street Light Conditions
Street lights turn on at dusk. You can report street light conditions on all City roadways and pathways, including: Highways Streets Paths in parks Playgrounds Parking lots in public parks Golf courses Street light conditions include: On during the day Burned out Flickering/cycling on and off Leaning pole Exposed electrical wires in the base of the street light DOT responds to most street light conditions within 10 days. Street light outages due to nearby construction, ConEd power issues, an obstruction in the base, or where a new street light or traffic foundation is needed may take longer to resolve.
File a Complaint or Check Status Use the  [Street Lighting Repair Form](https://service.nyctmc.org/service4/main2.asp)  to report a streetlight condition or to check the status of a street light service request.
Orange Light Over Luminaire Orange lights over luminaires designate the location or intersection with fire or police alarm call boxes. Follow Up on Street Light Outages To get information about a street light that has been out for more than 90 days, contact the appropriate [Borough Commissioner Office](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/contact/contact.shtml#bc).
Sneakers or Foreign Objects Hanging
Sneakers or other hanging objects do not obstruct the operation of a street light. DOT does not accept reports of objects hanging from a street light.

title: Water and Sewer Bill Payment
body:
Need something else? [Water and Sewer Bill](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02459) for general information about water and sewer bills and how to make account updates [Water and Sewer Rate](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02465) for rate information [Water and Sewer Bill Dispute](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02461) to dispute charges on your bill or make complaints about water and sewer rate increase You can pay your Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) water and sewer bill online, by phone, by mail, or in person. Protect yourself from fraud by using only the official payment methods listed below for your transactions. [Learn more about utility scams.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/whats-new/beware-of-utility-scams.page)
Pay Online
You can pay your water and sewer bill online, 24 hours a day, 7 days per week with a My DEP Account. If you sign up for a My DEP Account you can: Make a payment Set up recurring payments Enroll for automatic bill payments Manage multiple properties View and print your current bill or retrieve and print past bills View payment history Receive email confirmations for transactions Submit requests for: Billing disputes Refunds And more [Register or login to My DEP Account.](https://nyc.gov/mydep) You can make payments using a credit card, debit card or through Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) using a checking or savings account. Payments authorized after 9 AM weekdays may not post to your account until the following day. Payments authorized on the weekend may not post until Tuesday. [Learn more about about paying a water and sewer bill online.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/pay-my-bills/how-to-pay.page) [Pay your water and sewer bill online.](https://nyc.gov/mydep)
Pay By Phone
You can pay your water and sewer bill over the phone, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. You can make a payment by debit card, most credit cards, and through electronic funds transfer (EFT) using a savings or checking account. There is a 2.25% processing fee for credit and debit card payments. There is no fee for EFT transactions. Payments authorized after 9 AM weekdays may not post to your account until the following day. Payments authorized on the weekend may not post until Tuesday.
Agency: Department of Environmental Protection
Division: Bureau of Customer Services Automated Bill Payment
Phone Number: (866) 622-8292
Business Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week
Staff is available through the automated phone system at all times. Automated assistance is also available in Spanish.
Pay By Mail
You can pay your water and sewer bill using a check or money order. Cash is not accepted by mail. Make the check or money order payable to "NYC WATER BOARD"   Write the account number on the check or money order Enclose your bill stub and payment in a stamped envelope Mail to: NYC Water Board P.O. Box 11863 Newark, NJ 07101-8163
Pay In Person
You can pay your water and sewer bill at any Department of Environmental Protection Borough Office. You can make the payment by personal check, certified check, or money order, payable to "NYC Water Board". Cash is not accepted. You must write the water and sewer account number on the check. You can also use Internet kiosks and customer service telephones at the Borough Office to make payments using electronic fund transfers (EFT) or debit or credit cards. NYC [Department of Finance Business Centers](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01015) accept payments in person by cash, check, or money order. (Please note: Business Centers accept payments only. They do not have Water and Sewer Bill account information. If you have any issues or questions, you should visit a DEP Borough Office instead.)
DEP Borough Offices Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) Borough Offices are open Monday - Friday, from 9 AM to 5 PM. Customers can receive service at any Borough Office regardless of their Borough of residence. Walk-in services are provided.

title: Water and Sewer Lien Sale
body:
Need something else? [Water and Sewer Bill Payment](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02462) for water bill payment options All overdue water and sewer charges are considered a lien against your property. New York City has the authority to sell this lien to a third party, or lienholder, when the charges have been delinquent for more than a year. When the City sells the lien it is not selling the property. The new lienholder does not take title to the property. The lienholder purchases the right to collect the money that was previously owed to the City. If the property owner does not pay what is owed, the lienholder can begin formal foreclosure proceedings. Water and sewer liens will be included in the 2025 Lien Sale. [Learn more about the lien sale.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/property/property-lien-sales.page)
Agency: Department of Environmental Protection
Division: Bureau of Customer Services Water Meter Services and Billing
Phone Number: (718) 595-7000
Business Hours: Monday: 8 AM - 7 PM; Tuesday - Friday: 8 AM - 6 PM; Saturday: 9 AM - 12 PM
Lien Sale Eligible Properties
Properties eligible for the lien sale include: Tax Class 1 – Mixed use, two- and three-family homes with $3,000 or more in water and sewer charges outstanding for a year or more. Tax Class 2 - Multi-family homes, including condos and HDFC rentals, with $1,000 or more in water and sewer charges outstanding for a year or more. All commercial properties with $1,000 or more in water and sewer charges outstanding for a year or more.
Payment Agreement Terms
Payment agreements may be available to customers whose property is to be included in an upcoming Lien Sale. Down payments can be as little as 0% down, and monthly payments can be spread out to a maximum of 10 years. The current annual interest rates are based on your property's assessed property value and can be either Low - 6%, Medium - 9% or High - 16%.  Please note that these interest rates are subject to change annually.
Properties Exempt from the Lien Sale
The Tax Lien Sale excludes: Disabled Homeowners' Exemption properties (DHE) Single-family properties State Personal Income Tax (PIT) Circuit-Breaker Tax Credit properties Senior Citizen Homeowners Exemption properties (SCHE) HDFC Coops and condos (Housing Development Fund Corporation) Accounts with an Active Bankruptcy petition Active Duty military personnel  Veterans Accounts in current payment agreements Accounts in the Water Debt Assistance Program
Water Debt Assistance Program (WDAP)
The Department of Environmental Protection's (DEP) Water Debt Assistance Program (WDAP) can help homeowners who are at risk of foreclosure. You may prevent the sale of your water and sewer debt in an upcoming Lien Sale if you meet all of the following requirements:  You own and live in your home. Your property is on the 90-Day Lien Sale Listing or you receive a pre-lien warning notice You are currently at least 30 days delinquent in paying your mortgage. You are not currently in bankruptcy. Your home is classified as a: B0-B9: Two family residence C0: Three family residence S0: One family over two stores S1: One family over one store S2: Two family over one store You get water and utility bills in your name at your home address and have a valid New York State ID. All water and sewer charges were issued after you purchased the property. To determine your eligibility, you must visit any DEP borough office or DEP's Central Office with a valid government-issued photo identification, proof of mortgage delinquency and proof of residency to complete a Water Debt Assistance Customer Participation Form and sign a Program Agreement. Eligibility for this program can only be determined by DEP. You can get this form: Online [Learn more about DEP's Water Debt Assistance Program and download Customer Participation form.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/pay-my-bills/water-debt-assistance-program.page) In Person Visit your local DEP borough office to get a copy of this form. title: Water and Sewer Rate
body:
Need something else? [Water and Sewer Bill Payment](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02462) to make a payment, find out your current balance and payment due dates, and learn how your water bill is calculated  [Water and Sewer Bill](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02459) for general information and water and sewer bills and how to make account updates [Water and Sewer Bill Dispute](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02461) to dispute charges on your bill or make complaints about water and sewer rate increase The New York City Water Board is responsible for establishing rates and charges and collecting user payments from customers for services provided by the water and wastewater utility systems of the City of New York. Water consumption is determined by the amount of water that flows through the meter. The sewer rate is set at 159% of the water charges. As of July 1, 2025, water costs $5.05 per 100 cubic feet (748 gallons) and the combined cost of water and sewer is $13.07 per 100 cubic feet. The minimum water and sewer charge per metered household remains at $1.27 per day. If the property is billed through the Multi-Family Conservation Program, the annual charge per unit is $1,332.65. If you have any questions or need additional information, assistance is available: Online [Learn more about the water rate increases.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/pay-my-bills/how-we-bill-you.page) By Email [customerservice@dep.nyc.gov](mailto:customerservice@dep.nyc.gov) By Phone

Division: Bureau of Customer Services Water Meter Services and Billing

Reason for Increase
The Department of Environmental Protection's budget is funded by the money it collects through water and sewer rates. As the agency begins or continues several major projects over the next few years, including the ongoing construction of Water Tunnel No. 3, repairs to the Delaware Aqueduct, and major upgrades and repairs to treatment plants, sewers and other water infrastructure, budgetary needs will be great. Most of these projects are mandated by Federal or State regulators, and all will ensure that the health of the City’s waterways continues to improve and that the department continues to provide clean, safe water to New Yorkers into the future.

Exemptions
Certain qualifying organizations may be entitled to an exemption from water and sewer charges. Eligibility depends on several factors and interested parties should review and complete the exemption application. All supporting documentation and required forms must be mailed or delivered to the address provided in the general instructions on the form. [Download the DEP Application for Exemption from Water and Sewer Charges.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dep/downloads/pdf/pay-my-bills/customer-service/application-for-exemption-from-water-and-sewer-charges.pdf) [Learn more about exemptions from water and sewer charges.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/pay-my-bills/how-we-bill-you.page)
New York City Water Board

Customers with an Automated Meter Reading (AMR) device installed will also be able to monitor their consumption through their My DEP Account.
Filing a Dispute
To dispute a water and wastewater bill, you must first file a written dispute to the Bureau of Customer Services [Download the Dispute Resolution Process Overview.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dep/downloads/pdf/pay-my-bills/customer-service/dispute-resolution-process-overview.pdf) [Download the DEP customer dispute form.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dep/downloads/pdf/pay-my-bills/customer-service/customer-dispute-form.pdf) Online Submit the dispute form online using your [My DEP Account](https://nyc.gov/mydep). By Email Email your dispute form to [customerservice@dep.nyc.gov](mailto:customerservice@dep.nyc.gov) with the subject line "Dispute". By Mail Mail your dispute form to: Department of Environmental Protection Bureau of Customer Services P.O. Box 739055 Elmhurst, NY 11373-9055
Initial Appeal
You may appeal the decision or resolution of a previous written dispute by making an appeal to the Deputy Commissioner within 120 days after the date DEP provides a written response. Online Submit the appeal online using your [My DEP Account](https://nyc.gov/mydep). By Email Email your initial appeal to [customerservice@dep.nyc.gov](mailto:customerservice@dep.nyc.gov) with the subject line "Initial Appeal". By Mail Mail your initial appeal to: Deputy Commissioner Department of Environmental Protection Bureau of Customer Services 59-17 Junction Boulevard, 13th Floor Flushing, NY 11373-5108
Final Appeal
If you disagree with the decision rendered by the Deputy Commissioner, you may make a final written appeal to the Executive Director of the New York City Water Board within 60 days of the date of the determination by the Deputy Commissioner. By Email Email your final appeal to [nycwaterboard@dep.nyc.gov](mailto:nycwaterboard@dep.nyc.gov) with the subject line "Final Appeal" By Mail Mail your final appeal to: Executive Director New York City Water Board 59-17 Junction Boulevard, 8th Floor Flushing, NY 11373

title: Flammable Liquid Disposal
body:
Highly flammable liquids, such as gasoline, heating oil, and lighter fluid, should never be disposed of in the New York City municipal waste stream. This includes: Gasoline Heating oil Lighter fluid Never pour these liquids down the drain or in a sewer. Contact a hazardous material or chemical waste disposal company to get rid of highly flammable liquids. You can also take them to a SAFE Disposal Event.
SAFE Disposal Events
You can dispose of your special waste at SAFE Disposal Events (Solvents, Automotive, Flammable, Electronics). SAFE Events are usually held in the fall. Only residential waste from New York City is accepted. You must bring a valid ID and proof of NYC residency, such as a phone or utility bill. Commercial waste and commercial vehicles are not  allowed at SAFE Events. [Learn more about SAFE Disposal Events.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/what-we-do/programs/safe-disposal-events.page) Upcoming SAFE Events There are no SAFE Disposal Events scheduled at this time. Check back in Fall 2026 for more information. Items Accepted Automotive products Antifreeze Car batteries Gasoline Motor oil Transmission fluid Batteries Cleaning products Corrosive liquids Cosmetics or beauty products Hair developer Nail polish Electronics Computers and computer accessories TV and video equipment [Additional items](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02385) Fire extinguishers Flammable liquids Gas, helium, oxygen, or propane tanks Ink or toner cartridges Lawn and garden care products Light bulbs (compact fluorescent or tubes) Medical waste Medication Sharps (syringes, lancets) ​Paint Paint cans Spray paint Thermometers and thermostats Items Not Accepted Appliances with [CFC or Freon](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01792) Air conditioners Dehumidifiers Refrigerators or freezers Asbestos Commercial waste Cooking oil or grease Tires Waste generated from outside New York City
Motor Oil Disposal
You can bring motor oil to any service station that changes oil, or any retailer that sells oil. Such locations are required by law to accept up to five gallons of oil per day, per person, for free.  To report a used oil take back program refusing to accept oil, send an email to [info.sqg@dec.ny.gov](mailto:info.sqg@dec.ny.gov). Make sure to include the name, location, and any other relevant details about the refusal or other issues (such as charging fees for acceptance, no signage, etc.). You can also drop off your motor oil at a Special Waste Site or a SAFE Event. Learn more on the [Special Waste Disposal](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01973) page.

title: Propane Tank Storage and Disposal
body:
You can learn about propane tank storage and disposal rules in New York City.
Storage
The NYC Fire Code allows one- or two-family properties to store a maximum of two 20-pound propane cylinders outdoors. For all other residential properties, including apartment building roofs and terraces, storage and use are limited to a single small disposable 16.4-ounce cylinder. Outdoor barbecue grills can be installed, operated, and maintained on any residential premises if they are: Designed to use charcoal or electricity Have a total grate area of no more than 10 square feet Are not installed or operated within 10 feet of any flammable waste or material [View the Fire Code.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fdny/codes/fire-code/fire-code.page)
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) if you need more help.
Disposal
The Department of Sanitation (DSNY) does not collect propane tanks, such as those used by gas barbecues, because they are pressurized and may explode when compressed in the garbage truck.  You can drop off the tanks at a SAFE Disposal Event. Events are held every spring and fall. Learn more on the [Special Waste Disposal](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01973) page. You can also:  Exchange a used tank when buying a new tank Bring a tank to a hardware store or private propane dealer for reuse or recycling Bring a used tank to a scrap metal dealer for recycling
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) if you need more help.

title: Vehicle Disposal
body:
You can legally dispose of your vehicle by taking it to a motor vehicle wrecker or junk dealer. If you dispose of a vehicle improperly, you may get a summons with a fine of up to $1,000. [Learn about motor vehicle disposal.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/what-we-do/cleaning/derelict-vehicles.page#vehicle-disposal) [Learn about bike disposal.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/what-we-do/cleaning/derelict-vehicles.page#bicycle-disposal)
Required Documents for Proper Disposal
When turning over a vehicle to an auto wrecking firm, the title form (or registration on vehicles manufactured before 1974) needs to be completed. The name of the auto wrecking firm should appear on the title as the new owner of the vehicle. The auto wrecking firm is responsible for providing a receipt stating: The car's make and model Vehicle identification number Date of transaction The auto wrecker's name The receipt is proof that the car was disposed of legally and should be saved.
Disposing of Auto Parts
Metal car parts not containing oil or other hazardous substances can be put out with metal recyclables. Parts that contain hazardous substances, automotive batteries and tires should be brought to a [Special Waste Disposal](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01973) location.
Donations
The City does not accept vehicles donated by citizens. If you are interested in donating a vehicle, you should contact individual charitable organizations about donations.

title: Landscaper Waste Requirements
body:
Need something else? [Littering](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01673) to report landscapers chronically dispersing yard waste in or around the sidewalk, curb, or street [Curbside Composting](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02030) Landscapers must collect and dispose of any yard waste that they generate at a permitted composting facility. Yard waste generated by landscapers cannot be set out for collection or dispersed in or around the curb or street. [Learn more about landscaper waste requirements.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/businesses/setup-operations/commercial-landscapers.page)
Disposal Exception If you receive written notice that there isn't enough room at permitted composting facilities within City (or within 10 miles of the borough where yard waste was generated), you may dispose of yard waste at any permitted solid waste facility.
Lack Of Compliance
Landscapers who do not dispose of generated waste properly will be fined. The amounts are: $250 for the first violation $1,000 for the second violation within a 12-month period after the first violation $2,500 for the third or following violation within a 12-month period after the first violation You can file a [Littering](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01673) complaint against landscapers for improper disposal if you witnessed the violation more than once, occurring on a specific day of the week at a regular time.  Complaints for one-time occurrences are not accepted.

title: Recycling Theft
body:
You can report a vehicle that removed a large amount of recyclable materials which had been placed out for collection for the Department of Sanitation (DSNY). Do not use the Recycling Theft Tip Form to report individuals on foot scavenging small quantities of recyclable material. [Report stolen recyclable materials taken with a vehicle.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dsny/forms/recyclable-material-theft-observation)
Removing Other Residents' Trash or Recycling
You can't remove items, materials, or bags that other residents have placed out for pickup. Only authorized employees or agents of the Department of Sanitation may collect them.

title: Public Recycling Bin Complaint
body:
Need something else? [Litter Basket Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02143) Department of Sanitation (DSNY) public recycling bins collect metal, glass, plastic, milk or juice cartons, and paper. They are made of metal and can be all one color or silver with a colored lid. You can report a problem with a public recycling bin.
Overflowing
You can report a public recycling bin that’s completely full or overflowing. What You Need Please describe in your complaint if: Trash is blowing into the street or onto the sidewalk There is trash or trash bags on the ground around the bin
Report an overflowing public recycling bin.
Used for Household or Commercial Waste
Public recycling bins are for pedestrians to throw away metal, glass, plastic, milk or juice cartons, and paper. The bins can’t be used to dispose of household or commercial waste. Businesses are required by law to dispose of waste by contracting with a private carter or by hauling their own waste to an authorized disposal site. You can report people or businesses who are misusing public recycling bins. What You Need Your report must include: Address where the materials are coming from Bin location Name of the business if the bin is in front of a business Type of materials being thrown out Timeframe and days when the bin is misused
Report misuse of a public recycling bin.
Broken Bigbelly Can
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to report a broken or malfunctioning Bigbelly solar trash can.

title: Plastic Bag Ban and Paper Bag Fee
body:
Need something else? [Plastic Bag Recycling](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02080) The New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (NYSDEC) began enforcement of the plastic bag ban on October 19, 2020. New York State’s law banning plastic carryout bags took effect on March 1, 2020. In New York City, businesses are required to collect a non-taxable 5-cent fee from customers on paper carryout bags, with some exceptions. You can avoid paying the paper bag fee by bringing your own reusable bags to stores. Stores are required to allow the use of reusable shopping bags. The plastic bag ban and paper bag fee are efforts to reduce the use of wasteful single-use bags and their negative impact on the environment. Stores may choose not to switch to paper and may only have reusable bags for purchase. The City and State does not set prices for reusable bags. You can get more information about the plastic bag ban from NYSDEC. Online [Learn more about the plastic carryout bag ban for consumers and businesses.](https://dec.ny.gov/environmental-protection/recycling-composting/bag-waste-reduction-law) You can also send an email to [plasticbags@dec.ny.gov](mailto:plasticbags@dec.ny.gov). By Phone
Agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
Division: Bureau of Waste Reduction and Recycling
Phone Number: (518) 402-8706
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Businesses Covered by the Law
All businesses that are required to collect New York State sales tax are subject to the plastic carryout bag ban. Examples include, but are not limited to: Clothing stores Convenience stores Drug stores Green carts Grocery stores Hardware stores Liquor stores Office supply stores Pharmacies The plastic carryout bag ban  does not apply to businesses or other establishments that are not required to collect NYS sales tax.
Bag Exemptions
The following types of bags are exempt from both the plastic bag ban and the paper carryout bag fee. "Exempt bag" means a bag that is: Used only to contain or wrap uncooked meat, fish, seafood, poultry, other unwrapped or non-prepackaged food, flower, plant, or other item for the purpose of separating it from other items to avoid contamination, prevent damage from moisture, or for sanitary, public health, or environmental protection purposes Used only to package items from bulk containers, including: fruits vegetables grains candy small hardware items (such as nuts, bolts, and screws) live insects fish, crustaceans, mollusks, or other aquatic items requiring a waterproof bag Used only to contain food sliced or prepared to order Used only to contain a newspaper for delivery to a subscriber Sold in bulk quantities to a consumer at the point of sale that were specifically prepackaged in a manner to allow for bulk sale (for example, quantities of bags prepackaged in individual pre-sealed boxes) or prepackaged in individual boxes or containers for sale to a customer Sold as a trash bag Sold as a food storage bag, such as those in snack, sandwich, quart, and gallon sizes Used as a garment bag, such as over-the-hanger bags or those used by a dry cleaner or laundry service Made of plastic provided by a restaurant, tavern or similar food service establishment, as defined in the New York state sanitary code, to carry out or deliver prepared food Provided by a pharmacy to carry prescription drugs
Paper Bag Fees
The New York State Bag Waste Reduction Act authorizes counties and cities to impose a 5-cent paper carryout bag reduction fee on paper carryout bags. In addition to this 5-cent fee, stores may charge for their cost of a paper bag as a taxable retail sale. Only SNAP and WIC customers are exempt from the 5-cent paper carryout bag reduction fee. However, if a store is charging more than 5 cents for a paper bag, SNAP and WIC customers must still pay the remaining taxable charge for the bag. You can get more information or make a complaint about this fee. You can also get information online about exemptions related to the 5-cent paper carryout bag reduction fee and other information for businesses, such as collecting, reporting, and remitting the fee. Online [Learn more about the paper carryout bag reduction fee.](https://www.tax.ny.gov/bus/st/paper-carryout-bag-fee.htm) By Phone
Agency: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
Division: New York State Tax Information Center
Phone Number: (518) 485-2889
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Plastic Bag Complaints
Enforcement of the plastic carryout bag ban began on October 19, 2020. You can report a business providing plastic carryout bags. Online [Report a plastic bag law violation.](https://www.dec.ny.gov/form/report-a-plastic-bag-violation) By Phone
Agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
Division: Bureau of Waste Reduction and Recycling
Phone Number: (518) 402-8706
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM

title: Christmas Tree Disposal
body:
Need something else? [Wood Disposal](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01800) to learn how to get rid of lumber, tree branches, shrubs, and firewood [Trash, Recycling, and Compost Collection Schedule](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01801) [Missed Trash, Recycling, or Compost Collection](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01788)  The NYC Department of Sanitation (DSNY) collects live Christmas trees and wreaths at the curb as part of [Curbside Composting](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02030) service. You do not need to make an appointment to have your tree or wreath collected. Curbside composting is collected every week on your recycling day. Make sure to remove all stands, lights, ornaments, and tinsel before placing a tree or wreath at the curb. Do not put trees or wreaths in bags.  Trees and wreaths that still have items attached cannot be composted. Live trees are collected, chipped, mixed with leaves, and turned into rich compost for NYC's parks, institutions, and community gardens.
Artificial Trees
Take apart your artificial tree to recycle the base and trunk (pole) with metal, glass, plastic, and cartons on your recycling day. Make sure to remove all lights, ornaments and tinsel before placing at the curb. Otherwise, set it out as trash on a regular collection day.
