title: Identity Theft
body:
You can report identity theft and the fraudulent use of personal information, including: Social security Credit card Bank account numbers You can also report phone scams. Contact your local police precinct to make the report. Officers will respond when they are not handling emergency situations.
[Find a precinct or police service area (PSA) by address or zip code.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/bureaus/patrol/find-your-precinct.page) [Find a precinct by name.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/bureaus/patrol/precincts-landing.page) [Find a PSA by name.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/bureaus/transit-housing/housing.page)
Prevention Tips
You can learn how to prevent and respond to identity theft. Online [Get identity theft prevention tips for consumers.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/consumers/scams.page#idtheft) [Get identity theft prevention tips for businesses.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/businesses/tips-for-business.page#idtheft) By Mail You can get a copy of the Identity Theft Prevention Guide by mail.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to request a copy.
Paper Shredding
To help prevent identity theft, you should shred papers that have personal information before placing them out for recycling. Personal information includes your: Social Security Number Birth date Contact information Signature Bank and credit card account numbers Password or PIN information Shredding Events The NYPD or elected officials may hold free paper-shredding events in your community. Check with your [local police precinct](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01027) or [elected official's office](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01223).
Credit Report Fraud Alert
If your personal information has been stolen, the Federal Trade Commission recommends that you contact the three nationwide consumer reporting companies and request that an initial fraud alert be placed on credit reports. These companies are Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. They can be contacted online or by phone. Online [Visit the Equifax homepage.](https://www.equifax.com/personal/) [Visit the Experian homepage.](https://www.experian.com/) [Visit the TransUnion homepage.](https://www.transunion.com/) By Phone

title: Water Meter
body:
Need something else? [Water Meter Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02137) You can learn about water meter installation, replacement, or operation in residential or commercial buildings in New York City from the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP). Online [Get general water meter information.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/pay-my-bills/water-meter-faqs.page) By Phone
Agency: Department of Environmental Protection
Division: Bureau of Customer Services Water Meter Services and Billing
Phone Number: (718) 595-7000
Business Hours: Monday: 8 AM - 7 PM; Tuesday - Friday: 8 AM - 6 PM; Saturday: 9 AM - 12 PM
Automated Meter Reading (AMR) Upgrade 2024-2027 Starting in December 2024, DEP will be working to upgrade Automated Meter Reading (AMR) devices across all five boroughs. This upgrade is: Free Mandatory To replace devices that have reached the end of their useful life No appointment is necessary since most AMR devices are located outside the property. Property owners will receive an email or a letter from DEP, notifying them when they expect technicians to be in the area. (If DEP does need access to your property to reach the AMR device, they will reach out to you separately.) [Learn more about the Automated Meter Reader (AMR) Upgrade Program.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/news/120224/automated-meter-reader-upgrade-program)
Automated Meter Reading (AMR) Installation
The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) installs devices for automated meter reading (AMR) of water meters throughout New York City. The devices automatically transmit water meter readings directly to DEP for more accurate billing, and will assist in ending the need for estimated bills.   If you're not home when the contractor or inspector visits, you will find a notice with instructions for scheduling a future installation. If your home hasn't been visited, you can schedule an appointment for an installation. title: School Tax Relief for Homeowners (STAR)
body:
Homeowners may be eligible for a School Tax Relief (STAR) credit. The STAR Credit is offered by New York State in the form of a rebate check. The STAR Exemption is offered by New York City and appears on your property tax bill. You can’t receive both at the same time. New STAR applicants must apply for the benefit with the State. If you are receiving the STAR Exemption but your income goes over $250,000, you must apply for the STAR Credit. The STAR Credit may offer a greater benefit than the STAR Exemption because the amount of the credit will increase in the future, but the value of the exemption will not.
STAR Income Verification Request Letter
The New York State Department of Taxation and Finance may request income verification from some STAR property owners, requesting income verification. You can report your income to the NYS Tax Department online, by phone, or in person. Online Use the [STAR Income Worksheet](https://www8.tax.ny.gov/INWF/inwfStart) (no account required) or log in to (or create) an Individual Online Services account to use the [Homeowner Benefit Portal](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pit/property/homeowner-benefit-portal.htm) (no Property Key required). By Phone If you do not have Internet access, call the New York State Tax Department (not your local assessor). You can provide your income information over the phone directly to NYS Tax Department representatives or request that they mail you a STAR Income Worksheet.
Agency: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
Division: New York State School Tax Relief Program
Phone Number: (518) 457-2036
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8:30 AM - 4:30 PM
In Person NYS Tax Department may host STAR income worksheet events. [See if there are scheduled STAR events.](https://www.tax.ny.gov/star/events/#where-when)
STAR Credit
New School Tax Relief (STAR) applicants must apply for the benefit in the form of a credit check with New York State. If you are receiving the STAR Exemption but your income goes over $250,000, you must apply for the STAR Credit. Eligibility To apply for STAR, at least one owner must use the property as their primary residence. There are two forms of STAR: Basic and Enhanced. Enhanced STAR (E-STAR) offers a larger tax savings than Basic STAR. You can’t receive both at the same time. Basic Star and E-STAR have different eligibility requirements. Basic STAR To be eligible for the STAR Credit: You must own your home and it must be your primary residence. The total household income of all owners and spouses living on the property must be $500,000 or less. There is no age restriction. Enhanced STAR To be eligible for the E-STAR Credit: You must be 65 or older by December 31 of the year when the credit will begin. For jointly-owned property, only one spouse or sibling must be 65 or older. The total household income of all owners (residents and non-residents) and any owner’s spouse who lives on the property must be $110,750 or less For purposes of Basic STAR and E-STAR, total household income is defined as adjusted gross income (AGI) minus any taxable IRA distributions. Application Information Online [Learn more and apply for the STAR Credit.](https://www.tax.ny.gov/star/) By Phone
Agency: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
Division: New York State School Tax Relief Program
Phone Number: (518) 457-2036
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8:30 AM - 4:30 PM
STAR Exemption
New York City’s STAR Exemption program is no longer accepting applicants. If you don’t currently receive STAR, you should apply with NY State for the STAR Credit. If you currently receive the STAR Exemption, you can: Remove the STAR Exemption so you can apply for the STAR Credit with the State The STAR Exemption doesn't need to be renewed. Exemption Amounts New York State sets the rates for STAR and Enhanced STAR. The amount of your exemption credit is based upon: Your property's assessed value or transitional assessed value. Your prior year savings. E-STAR has an annual inflation rate adjustment. The STAR Credit may offer a greater benefit than the STAR Exemption because the amount of the credit will increase in the future, but the value of the exemption will not. State law sets limits on the maximum savings amount for properties receiving STAR or E-STAR. The limit is based on the type of property you own. The approximate benefit for the STAR Exemption is $293. The approximate benefit for the Enhanced STAR Exemption is $650. For more information on how your exemption was calculated, contact the State. [Visit the Department of Taxation and Finance website.](https://www.tax.ny.gov/)
STAR Exemption or Credit for Past Due Taxes
A new law requires that any property with unpaid property taxes that are past due for more than one year cannot continue receiving the Basic STAR Exemption or Credit. New York State will mail letters to homeowners that are at risk of losing their STAR Exemption or Credit. If you receive a letter you have until May 25 to pay the past due property taxes that you owe or enter into a payment agreement or PT AID agreement to keep the STAR Exemption or Credit. For the purposes of determining STAR eligibility property taxes are considered past due when: Property taxes remain unpaid more than  one year after the due date. If you have a payment agreement or PT AID agreement you have not made the required payments and have defaulted on that agreement. Properties receiving Enhanced STAR are not affected. Other non-property tax charges on the tax bill are not included. Some properties may be exempt from this law. If you receive a notice from NYS and you fit either of these categories you should contact DOF prior to May 25: You receive the Senior Citizen Homeowner’s Exemption (SCHE), Disabled Homeowner’s Exemption (DHE), or Veterans Property Tax Exemption in the current tax year you are eligible to continue receiving Basic STAR. If you have a payment agreement or PT AID agreement and you are up to date with payments you are eligible to continue receiving Basic STAR. If you receive a notice and the information in the notice is incorrect or you do not owe past due property taxes you must appeal to New York State within 45 days of the notice.   Paid or Unpaid Taxes Paid If you pay your past due property taxes in full or enter into a payment agreement/PT AID agreement by May 25, you will continue to receive the STAR Exemption or Credit.   Unpaid If you do not pay your past due property taxes or enter into a payment agreement/PT AID agreement by May 25 you will lose the STAR Exemption or Credit for the current tax year. If you currently receive the STAR Exemption it will be removed from your October property tax bill, retroactive to July 1. If you currently receive the STAR Credit, you will not receive a check this year. If you pay the past due property taxes after May 25 but within the next tax year you can apply for the STAR Credit through NYS and receive the credit for this year retroactively. Once the STAR exemption is removed from your property you must apply for the STAR credit.
Upgrade to Enhanced STAR
There are two forms of the STAR Exemption: Basic and Enhanced. Enhanced STAR (E-STAR) offers a larger tax savings than Basic STAR. You can’t receive both at the same time. If you receive the Basic STAR Exemption and meet E-STAR eligibility guidelines, you will no longer need to take any action to upgrade to the Enhanced STAR exemption or credit. The NYS Department of Taxation and Finance will automatically notify you when you become eligible for Enhanced STAR. Eligibility To be eligible for E-STAR: All owners must be 65 or older in the calendar year in which you are applying. If the owners are spouses or siblings, only one must be 65 or older. The total household income of all owners (residents and non-residents) and any owner’s spouse living on the property must be: for tax year 2026/2027 $110,750 or less. For purposes of STAR and E-STAR, income is defined as adjusted gross income (AGI) minus any taxable IRA distributions. If you are enrolled in E-STAR, your income eligibility will be verified automatically each year by the NYS Department of Taxation and Finance. You don't need to do anything.
Remove STAR Exemption to Get STAR Credit
The STAR Credit may offer a greater benefit than the STAR Exemption because the amount of the credit will increase in the future, but the value of the exemption will not. If you are currently receiving STAR or Enhanced STAR as a property tax exemption, and want to receive STAR as a credit rebate check, you must request that the NYC Department of Finance remove the STAR Exemption from your property first. You can then reapply for STAR or Enhanced STAR with the State. If you choose to remove the STAR exemption in order to receive the STAR credit you will owe more in property taxes.
Online You can complete the application and upload your documents online. You'll need to log in or create an account first. Filing online will allow you to: Save your progress so you can come back to a partially completed application later View the status of submitted applications Get electronic notifications when your application is submitted, received, and processed or if additional information is required Submit additional documents [Apply online.](https://a836-pts-efile.nyc.gov/SmartFile/) By Mail
You can get the Property Tax Exemption Removal Form online or by mail. All owners must sign, date, and provide their Social Security numbers on the form. If an owner has died, a copy of the death certificate must be included. Mail the form and any required documents to: NYC Department of Finance Homeowner Tax Benefits P.O. Box 311 Maplewood, NJ 07040-0311 Online [Download the Property Tax Exemption Removal Form.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/finance/downloads/pdf/property/exc-0728.pdf) By Mail
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to request a copy.
Appeal a Removal
You can appeal if New York State removed your exemption. A property’s benefits may be revoked if: An owner died The property transitioned to a new owner The owner is no longer eligible You can appeal the decision with the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance. Online [Learn more about STAR Credit appeals.](https://www.tax.ny.gov/star/) By Phone
Agency: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
Division: New York State School Tax Relief Program
Phone Number: (518) 457-2036
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8:30 AM - 4:30 PM
Benefit Status
You can get information about your property tax benefits, including: Application status Current benefit amounts Proposed benefit for the upcoming tax year Co-op owners should contact their management office for assistance. STAR Exemption Benefit Status Online [Get property tax benefit information.](https://a836-pts-access.nyc.gov/care/forms/htmlframe.aspx?mode=content/home.htm) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
STAR Credit Benefit Status Online [Learn more and apply for the STAR Credit.](https://www.tax.ny.gov/star/) By Phone

Division: New York State School Tax Relief Program
Phone Number: (518) 457-2036
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8:30 AM - 4:30 PM
Get Help

title: 911 Surcharge
body:
Need something else? [Business Tax Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02602) for help with payment issues, copies of filed returns, audits, and notices of unpaid taxes. Landline, and Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) telecommunications service providers are required to collect the 911 surcharge from their customers and send it to the City. Wireless telecommunications service providers are required to collect the 911 surcharge from their customers and send it to New York State. Information on filing and paying are on the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance website.
Tax Rates
The monthly surcharge is: Landline - $1.00 per line Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) - $1.00 per device
Filing and Paying
Providers must turn over the collected fees, minus a 2% administrative fee, and file Form NYC-E-911 Surcharge to report the surcharge amounts billed and collected. [Learn more about the 911 surcharge and get the NYC-E-911 form.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/business/business-e911-surcharge-for-telecommunications-services.page) You can file the forms and pay online through Business Tax e-Services or send the documents and payment by mail. Online You can file and pay the tax through Business Tax e-Services. You can pay by: Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) withdrawn directly from your bank E-check Credit card (American Express, Master Card, VISA, and Discover) Debit card (VISA and Master Card debit cards that don’t require the entry of a PIN number to complete a transaction) There is a 2% convenience fee for paying by credit or debit card. There is no convenience fee for paying by EFT or e-check. If there is a debit block on the bank account and you wish to pay online or by using software, the number needed to release the block is 6136400434. [Access Business Tax e-Services.](http://nyc.gov/eservices) By Mail You can file the tax forms by mail. If there's a balance due, you can also send a payment by mail. For all returns, except returns claiming a refund, mail the tax form to: NYC Department of Finance P.O. Box 5564 Binghamton, NY 13902-5564 Don't send payments or requests for extensions to this address. After you have mailed the form, if you owe a payment, mail the check and the payment voucher to: NYC Department of Finance P.O. Box 3933 New York, NY 10008-3933 If you are claiming a refund, mail the form to: NYC Department of Finance P.O. Box 5563 Binghamton, NY 13902-5563
Deadline
Returns and taxes are due by the 25th of each month.
Interest Rate
If you don't file your return or pay the tax by the deadline, you will be charged interest. From April 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026, the interest rate is 10%.
Refunds
You can request a refund for overpayment of the 911 surcharge by completing an amended NYC E-911 form. The Department of Finance doesn't pay interest on refunds for this tax. [Learn more about the 911 surcharge and get the NYC-E-911 form.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/business/business-e911-surcharge-for-telecommunications-services.page)
Ways to Get Help
You can get answers to questions about the tax or help with filing and paying through your eServices account. Log in to your [E-Services](https://nyc.gov/eservices) account.

title: Abortion
body:
Abortion Is Legal and Protected in New York In New York State, abortion is: Safe Legal Available to all [Learn more about abortion and your rights.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/abortion.page)
Abortion is legal and protected in New York. You can get counseling and abortion care at many health centers in New York City. If you are a teenager, you can get sexual health services, including abortion care, at a clinic without your parents' permission or knowledge. Services are confidential, free or very low-cost, and open to all. You will be helped regardless of your immigration status. You can find abortion providers online or by phone. Online [Find an abortion provider.](https://www.nychealthandhospitals.org/services/obstetrics-gynecology/#accordion-abortion-surgery) By Phone
Agency: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
Division: New York City Abortion Access Hub
Phone Number: (877) 692-2482
Business Hours: Monday - Saturday: 8 AM - 8 PM
Telehealth Services
You can get confidential, on-demand abortion care from the comfort of your home through NYC Health + Hospitals’ [Virtual ExpressCare](https://expresscare.nyc/abortion-care/). You can access services: By video or phone 9 AM to 9 PM, 7 days a week Without an appointment In over 200 languages Services At your visit, you will talk with a licensed health care provider. They can offer: Screening and assessment Options counseling Prescriptions for medication abortion and delivery in 1 to 4 business days Connections to in-person care or procedures Follow-up after abortion Eligibility To be eligible for Virtual ExpressCare, you must be: Pregnant 15 years of age or older In NYC at the time of the visit In NYC when taking abortion medication You don’t need to show proof of residency or immigration status. Parental consent isn’t required. Learn More Online [Learn more about Virtual ExpressCare.](https://expresscare.nyc/abortion-care/) By Phone
Agency: NYC Health + Hospitals
Division: Virtual ExpressCare
Phone Number: (718) 360-8981
Business Hours: Daily: 9 AM - 9 PM
Financial Assistance
Health insurance, including Medicaid, may cover the cost of an abortion. Contact your health insurer to find out what your plan covers. You may be eligible for New York State Medicaid to cover your abortion procedure if you do not have other coverage. Pregnant New Yorkers can qualify for Medicaid at higher income levels. If you need help paying for your appointment, visit: [National Abortion Federation](https://prochoice.org/patients/find-a-provider/), or call its hotline at (800) 772-9100 [New York Abortion Access Fund](https://www.nyaaf.org/), or call its hotline at (212) 252-4757 [National Network of Abortion Funds](https://abortionfunds.org/) If you need help with travel or lodging costs related to your appointment: [Brigid Alliance](https://brigidalliance.org/) provides help with travel expenses. You can make an appointment at one of their partner clinics to access this help. [Haven Coalition](http://www.havencoalition.org/) provides help with overnight lodging for those who have to travel to New York City for an abortion.
Abortion Providers Outside of NYC
To find an abortion provider outside of New York City, visit: [National Abortion Federation](https://prochoice.org/patients/find-a-provider/) [Ineedana.com](https://www.ineedana.com/) [Abortion Finder](https://www.abortionfinder.org/)

body:
Need something else? Get application or case assistance with: [SNAP](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01018) [Cash Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03115) [EBT cards](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02340) [Medicaid](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02861) [Fair Fares NYC](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03181) [CityFHEPS Rental Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03172) [HEAP Energy Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02529) [HEAP Cooling Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02552) [Child Support](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01038) The Human Resources Administration (HRA) has a website and free mobile app, Access HRA. You can use these resources to: Apply for benefit programs Recertify for benefit programs Submit documents View case information You must create an ACCESS HRA account to: Apply or recertify for benefits View sensitive case information Your username and password are the same for both the website and mobile app. [Visit the ACCESS HRA website.](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/) [Download the ACCESS HRA mobile app.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page) [Download the ACCESS HRA Child Support mobile app.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/childsupportmobile.page) [View instructional videos that shows you how to use ACCESS HRA.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/access-hra-resources.page) [Read the ACCESS HRA User Guide for helpful tips on how to use the ACCESS HRA website and mobile app.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hra/ACCESSHRA/pdf/announcements/welcome_english.pdf) You can email [ACCESSHRASuppapp@dss.nyc.gov](mailto:ACCESSHRASuppapp@dss.nyc.gov) if you have problems using ACCESS HRA.
Features Specific to the ACCESS HRA Website
The ACCESS HRA website lets you submit the following items online after you set up your ACCESS HRA account: Application for SNAP or Cash Assistance Recertification for SNAP or Cash Assistance  Periodic report for SNAP Application for Emergency Cash Assistance, also known as a One Shot Deal Application for Medicaid for people age 65 and older, disabled, or blind Application for Medicare Saving Programs (MSP) for people with Medicare Renewal for Medicaid for people age 65 and older, disabled, or blind Renewal for CityFHEPS Application for Regular Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP) Application for Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP) Cooling Assistance Application for Child Care in Lieu of Cash Assistance (CILOCA) Application or renewal application for the Fair Fares NYC discount You can also use the ACCESS HRA website to request: Changes to your Cash Assistance case, including requests for child care Changes to your SNAP case Closure of your SNAP or Cash Assistance case Emergency grants for your Cash Assistance case ACCESS HRA allows you to print a prepopulated Medicaid Renewal form.
Features Specific to the ACCESS HRA Mobile App
You can download the free ACCESS HRA mobile app onto a mobile device, such as a: Smartphone Tablet You must have or create an ACCESS HRA account to use the mobile app. You can use the same login information as the website. You can use the app to: Upload required documents on the My Uploads page by taking a picture or choosing an image from your gallery Enroll to receive push notifications related to your case, such as appointment reminders and messages, directly on a mobile device
Features Specific to the ACCESS HRA Child Support Mobile App
The free ACCESS HRA Child Support mobile app makes it easier to access child support services and can be downloaded onto a mobile device, such as a smartphone or tablet.  You must have or create an ACCESS HRA account to use the mobile app. You can use the same login information as the website.  You can use the app to: Submit a child support referral or enrollment Make a payment for child support by credit or debit card or PayPal Maintain your contact information View upcoming appointments Enroll for child support debt reduction Challenge an enrollment action
ACCESS HRA Website and Mobile App Shared Features
You must have or create an ACCESS HRA account and link it to your HRA case to use the features described below. You can use the website and mobile app to see your: Application or case status EBT Card Balance Recent payments Upcoming appointments Documents that HRA received and added to your case List of required documents that HRA still needs for your case HRA notices Mailing address, phone number, and email address on file You can also use the website and mobile app to:  See the next steps required to complete your application or recertification Request a budget letter Update your mailing address, phone number, and email address Sign up to go paperless and receive notices electronically Sign up for text alerts about upcoming appointments Link your HRA case Profile to a Partner Organization

title: Accessible Taxi Dispatch
body:
Need something else? [Taxi Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01241) to report a problem with a taxi driver or vehicle [City Agency or Worker Feedback](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01662) to give the Taxi Limousine Commission (TLC) feedback about the Accessible Dispatch program You can get a wheelchair accessible taxi anywhere in the five boroughs. To schedule a pickup: Call the Accessible Taxi Hotline and choose the e-hail app a company of your choice. Note, the app companies offer an upfront price and may ask for payment information. Passengers may also hail an accessible taxi on the street and use the meter to determine the price for the fare. Dial 711 for Relay service. When you book through Accessible Taxi Hotline, the meter starts when you are secured in the vehicle. At the end of the trip, you pay the standard metered fare with cash or a credit card. You can pick a vehicle type based on your need or preference. There is no passenger limit if they legally fit in the vehicle. There is no additional charge based on the number of people. Online [Find an Accessible Ride.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/passengers/find-an-accessible-ride.page) By Phone
Agency: Taxi and Limousine Commission
Division: Accessible Taxi Hotline
Phone Number: (646) 599-9999
Business Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week
Wheelchair Accessible Taxi Description
Wheelchair accessible taxis have manual ramps that the driver lowers to the ground so a wheelchair can roll into the taxi. Inside the taxi, the wheelchair is secured in place. The firmly fixed securements meet the requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act. Drivers are trained to help the passenger and properly secure the wheelchair. You can file a complaint on the [Taxi Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01241) page if there is an issue with a driver.

title: Adopt an Animal
body:
You can adopt an animal at the Animal Care Centers of NYC (ACC). The Care Centers are located in Manhattan, Queens, and Staten Island. ACC also holds weekly off-site adoption events. To adopt an animal, you must: Be 18 years old or older Have a photo ID Show proof of your current residence Show proof you are allowed to have animals in the residence if you rent your apartment or house ACC counselors will help you choose the animal that is best for your lifestyle. If you have children living in your home, they must come to the Care Center and be part of the adoption process. Adoption of any animal is on a first-come, first-served basis. It's also based on your specific qualifications. Adoption fees are on a sliding scale ranging from $25 to $400, depending on the animal that is being adopted. Cash, checks, and credit cards are accepted. You can get more information about adoption and fostering of available animals. Online [Learn more about animal adoption.](https://www.nycacc.org/adoption/process/) [Learn more about fostering an animal.](https://www.nycacc.org/foster/) [View photos of animals up for adoption.](https://www.nycacc.org/) [Learn about upcoming adoption events.](https://www.nycacc.org/adoptionevents) By Email [adopt@nycacc.org](mailto:adopt@nycacc.org) In Person Manhattan Animal Care Center 326 East 110th Street (Between 1st and 2nd Avenues) [Check hours of operation.](https://www.nycacc.org/about/locations) Queens Animal Care Center 1906 Flushing Avenue, Ridgewood, NY 11385 [Check hours of operation.](https://www.nycacc.org/about/locations) Staten Island Animal Care Center 3139 Veterans Road West (Route 440 South to Exit 1N - Arthur Kill Road. At stop sign, make left onto Veterans Road West) [Check hours of operation.](https://www.nycacc.org/about/locations) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Holiday Closures
ACC offices are closed on the following holidays: New Year's Day Martin Luther King Jr. Day Lincoln's Birthday Washington's Birthday Memorial Day Independence Day Labor Day Thanksgiving Day Christmas Day

title: Adult Day Care
body:
New York City has social adult day care programs and medical adult day care programs. You can find out about social and medical adult day care programs and services provided and locations in your area.
Social Adult Day Care Programs
Social adult day care programs serve adults of all ages with functional impairments, including but not limited to physical frailness, dementia, and Alzheimer’s disease. They are structured programs that provide supervised group activities, including:  Socialization  Recreation Meals  Transportation (in some instances) Social adult day care programs do not provide medical services. For older adults, they may be a good option for individuals seeking socialization and other services whose needs cannot be met at an [Older Adult Center](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02353).  Online [Learn more about social adult day care.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dfta/community-partners/social-adult-day-care.page) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Medical Adult Day Care Services
Medical adult day care services are for older adults with more medical needs. They are typically found in nursing homes. Access to on-site clinic services is available. Medical staff can help with administering medications.  [Learn more about medical adult day care services.](https://www.health.ny.gov/health_care/medicaid/program/longterm/addc.htm)
Complaints and Comments
Medical Adult Day Care Feedback Complaints or comments about medical adult day care providers must be directed to the [New York State Department of Health.](https://www.health.ny.gov/contact/doh800.htm) Social Adult Day Care Feedback You can make a complaint or comment about: Social adult day care programs operating within New York City Services provided by those programs Online [Make a complaint or comment about a social adult day care program.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dfta/community-partners/social-adult-day-care-sadc-inquiry-form.page) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: Adult Vaccination and Immunization
body:
Need something else? [Coronavirus (COVID-19) Vaccine](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03360) [Flu Shot and Prevention](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02735) [Monkeypox (MPV)](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03484) [Polio](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03499) [Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03608) You can find clinics that offer vaccinations and immunizations for a variety of diseases and travel shots. You can also get materials in multiple languages, including an FAQ sheet and a self-screening checklist.
Clinics
You can get referrals to vaccine clinics. Eligibility may depend on your age and risk of disease.  Vaccines Offered Hepatitis A - for high-risk adults ages 19 to 59 Hepatitis B - for high-risk adults ages 19 to 59 HPV (Human Papillomavirus) Meningococcal - for 18-year-olds MMR (Measles, Mumps, Rubella) Polio Pneumococcal vaccine Shingles (Zoster) Td (Tetanus, Diphtheria) Tdap (Tetanus, Diphtheria, Pertussis) Varicella (Chickenpox) - for 18-year-olds Find a Clinic
[Find a clinic.](https://a816-health.nyc.gov/NYCHealthMap/ServiceCategory)
NYC Health Clinics accept all types of insurance. If you have insurance, the clinic will bill your plan but won’t collect payments from you. If you don’t have health insurance, you will still get services. You will be asked to pay a sliding scale fee. The fee may be based on clinic type and your age, family size, and income. [Learn more about clinic billing.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/services/allclinics.page)
Travel Shots
The City does not provide travel shots such as vaccinations against typhoid or yellow fever. The [Centers for Disease Control and Prevention](https://www.cdc.gov/) website offers information and resources to find clinics for travelers.
Adult Vaccination Health Bulletin
You can get materials with information about the vaccines that help keep adults and their loved ones healthy.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to request a copy.
Frequently Asked Questions Sheet
The Adult Vaccination: Frequently Asked Questions sheet gives adult patients answers to some of the most frequently asked questions about vaccines for adults. The sheet also addresses vaccine effectiveness, safety, and other topics. This sheet is available in: English Spanish Russian Traditional Chinese Simplified Chinese [Download the FAQ sheet.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/doh/downloads/pdf/csi/adult-vaccine-faq.pdf)
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to request a copy.
Patient Self-Screening Form
The Patient Self-Screening Form is a checklist for adult patients to use while waiting for a visit with a healthcare provider. It can be used to determine what vaccines may be recommended based on: Age Lifestyle Health conditions Job Other factors Healthcare providers can then review and discuss the completed form with you to recommend and administer any needed vaccines. This form is available in: English Spanish Russian Traditional Chinese Simplified Chinese [Download the Patient Self-Screening Form.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/doh/downloads/pdf/csi/adult-vaccination-patient-screening-form.pdf)

title: HEAP Cooling Assistance
body:
Need something else? [Cooling Centers](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02663) [Cool It! NYC](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03323) [Essential Plan Cooling Program](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03679) The Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP) helps eligible New Yorkers afford an air conditioner or fan to stay cool during the summer months. The application period for the 2025-2026 Cooling Assistance Component opened on April 15, 2026. Eligible applicants are given one benefit per household for the purchase and installation of air conditioner or fan. If an air conditioner cannot be safely installed, a fan will be provided. Installation for a window, portable air conditioner or fan cannot exceed $800. For an existing wall sleeve unit, installation cannot exceed $1,000. No additional HEAP cash benefits are available. You can apply online, by phone, or in person.
Eligibility
You may be eligible for a HEAP Cooling Assistance Component benefit if your household meets the HEAP benefit gross monthly income guidelines and other eligibility requirements. [Learn more about the HEAP Cooling Assistance Component benefit.](https://otda.ny.gov/programs/heap/#cooling-assistance) [Determine if you may be eligible for other HRA programs on ACCESS NYC](https://access.nyc.gov/).
How to Apply
You can apply for the HEAP Cooling Assistance Component benefit online, by phone, or in person at a local HRA Benefits Center. When you apply by phone or in person, you can get help with: Eligibility Application process Required documentation Online Use the [ACCESS HRA website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/) from anywhere and at any time to apply for HEAP Cooling Assistance benefits. You can submit documents using the Document Upload feature on the [ACCESS HRA Mobile App](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page). Online submissions will require the selection of two HEAP participating vendors who can install an air conditioner. [Visit the OTDA website for a list of HEAP participating vendors.](https://www.heapoil.com/admin/reports/OTDA_ParticipatingDealersReport.jsp) By Phone You must speak to an agent during business hours to apply by phone.
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.
In Person You can apply in person by visiting certain HRA Benefits Access Centers or community outreach site near you. [Find a location near you.](https://otda.ny.gov/programs/heap/contacts/default.asp?county=32#result)
HEAP Application Status
The Human Resources Administration has 30 business days from the date your application is reviewed to make a decision on your application. A notice is mailed to you when a decision is made on your application. ​You can check your Cooling Assistance application status online or by phone. Online Visit the [ACCESS HRA website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/) or the [ACCESS HRA Mobile App](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page) from anywhere and at any time and log into your ACCESS HRA account. By Phone
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.
Air Conditioner Maintenance
You are responsible for maintaining the air conditioner. This includes: Removing, covering, and storing it during the winter Reinstalling it the next summer If there is a problem after installation, contact the company who makes the air conditioner or the vendor who installed it. If you do not have the vendor’s information, you can request it from HEAP.
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.

title: Air Conditioner Installation Guidelines
body:
Need something else? [CFC and Freon Removal](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01792) to schedule an appointment to dispose of an air conditioner [HEAP Cooling Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02552) to see if you qualify for an air conditioner or fan You do not need a work permit or equipment use permit to install a common window air conditioner (AC) unit. AC units exceeding three tons or 36,000 BTU per hour require a permit. [Get air conditioner installation tips.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/installing-air-conditioning-units.page)
Equipment Use Permit Information
An Equipment Use Permit (PW-4) is required to install an air conditioner unit over three tons or 36,000 BTU per hour. Application information is available on the Department of Buildings (DOB) website. [Learn about air conditioner installation permits.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/installing-air-conditioning-units.page)
Installation Guidelines
These are the guidelines you should follow when installing an air conditioner: Follow the manufacturer's instructions included with the A/C unit. Make sure the A/C is installed securely. Support it from underneath or firmly fasten it from inside with angles. You can use metal brackets and mounting rails for safe installation. Supporting metal brackets and interior angles must be structurally fastened to the building envelope and strong enough for the size and weight of the A/C unit. Objects used to adjust the position of the A/C unit must have an independent source of fastening or attachment. Secure leveling objects in order to prevent movement and shifting due to vibration or weather conditions. Install the A/C so that it remains in place when the window is opened and affix it so that the window cannot be opened accidentally. Do not use loose objects, such as wood blocks, bricks, or telephone books to level an air conditioner. Do not place anything on top of an air conditioner. Tilt the unit slightly to provide water drainage but do not over tilt.

title: After School Program
body:
You can find New York City after school programs for elementary, middle school, and high school students. Some after school programs require enrollment, while for others, preregistration is not required. These programs are offered without any cost to parents or children.
Department of Youth and Community Programs
The New York City Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD) offers after school programs for young people in all 5 boroughs of New York City. Online [Learn about DYCD after school programs.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dycd/services/after-school.page)
[Find an after school program.](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/site-finder/?type=After%20School%20Program) Call the program for more information.
By Phone
Agency: Department of Youth and Community Development
Division: Community Connect
Phone Number: (800) 246-4646
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
If the call fails to connect, you can call again later or email communityconnect@dycd.nyc.gov.
Police Department Youth Programs
The City provides information about programs for children and young adults run by the New York Police Department (NYPD). To get information about programs in the neighborhood, contact a Youth Officer at your local police precinct. You can also get information about The Police Athletic League (PAL) programs offered in the City. The City's Police Department and PAL work in partnership to provide communities with needed summer and after school recreational and educational activities throughout all 5 boroughs.
In Person Contact a Youth Officer at your local police precinct.
[Find a precinct or police service area (PSA) by address or zip code.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/bureaus/patrol/find-your-precinct.page) [Find a precinct by name.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/bureaus/patrol/precincts-landing.page) [Find a PSA by name.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/bureaus/transit-housing/housing.page)
By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Department of Parks Programs
The NYC Parks Afterschool Program provides children ages 6 to 13 the opportunity to enjoy a wide range of activities. This free program takes place Monday through Friday from 3 PM to 6 PM. Registration is required. The programs offers: Academic enrichment Arts and cultural programming Healthy snacks Special events Sports and fitness Supervised computer use Team-building activities Trips around New York City You can get more information online, including registration requirements and program locations. [Learn more about NYC Parks Afterschool Program.](https://www.nycgovparks.org/programs/recreation/afterschool)
Ranger Conservation Corps Program Through New York City’s Ranger Conservation Corps program, high school students can work on environmental conservation and restoration projects. The Ranger Conservation Corp program environmental internship is run by the Urban Park Rangers. Online [Get information about the Ranger Conservation Corp.](https://www.nycgovparks.org/programs/rangers/conservation-corps) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Public Schools Athletic League
Through the Public Schools Athletic League (PSAL), NYC high school students can participate in summer sports, fitness, and recreation programs. PSAL is open to all NYC students entering grades 9–12 in Fall 2025 with an OSIS number, including Charter school students. Registration is first come, first served and will remain open until each activity reaches capacity. [Learn more about the Public Schools Athletic League.](https://www.psal.org/events-and-standings/summer.aspx) [Register for the Public Schools Athletic League.](https://www.psal.org/psalapps/summer/#/registration)
Complaints
You can make a complaint about an after school program.

Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM

title: Alcohol License
body:
Need something else? [Alcohol License Check](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02556) for complaints about an establishment serving alcohol without a license [Alcohol Sale Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02223) to report the sale of alcohol to a minor or an intoxicated person, or at more than half off, or to-go, or outside of approved hours [Liquor License Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02557) You can get information about liquor license fees and eligibility from the State. Various licenses and permits are available within two general categories: wholesale and retail. Online [Visit the New York State Liquor Authority website.](https://sla.ny.gov/) By Phone
Agency: New York State Liquor Authority
Phone Number: (518) 474-3114
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8:30 AM - 4:30 PM
Sale of Alcoholic Beverages
Off-premises (supermarket or grocery stores) beer sales are permitted at all times. Off-premises (liquor store or retailer) liquor and wine sales are prohibited between midnight and 8 AM, and Sundays between 10 PM and 10 AM. On-premises (bar or lounge) sales are prohibited on weekdays between 4 AM and 8 AM, and Sundays between 4 AM and 10 AM.
Restaurant or Bar Selling Alcohol To-Go
As of April 12, 2022, bars and restaurants may sell wine and/or liquor to-go or for delivery only if it is ordered along with a “substantial food item.” Substantial food items include sandwiches, soups, salads, wings, hotdogs, or other foods of similar quality and substance. A bag of chips, bowl of nuts, or candy alone are not considered substantial food. Bars and restaurants may only continue to sell beer, cider, and mead to-go or for delivery without the purchase of a substantial food item.  [Learn more about the Drinks To-Go Law.](https://sla.ny.gov/lawsla-guidancefaq-sale-wine-and-liquor-go-premises-retail-licensees) Report a Violation You can report a restaurant or bar selling alcohol (other than beer, cider or mead) to-go or for delivery without the required food purchase. Obvious efforts to avoid the law, for example an unreasonably small portion of soup, a serving of canned beans, a handful of lettuce, or charging a small extra fee for an alcoholic beverage instead of a food item not actually ordered or delivered, will be treated as a violation of the law. [Send your complaint, including photos, to the State Liquor Authority.](https://slacomplaints.ny.gov/clientapp/)

Business Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week
Transportation Options
You can get information about traveling to and from Port Authority Airports.
Agency: Port Authority of NY and NJ
Division: 800-AIR-RIDE
Phone Number: (800) 247-7433
Business Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week
Air Travel Security Guidelines
You are allowed to carry on containers that are 3.4 ounces (100 ml) or smaller, and all containers must fit inside a one-quart, clear, plastic, zip-top bag. This applies to any liquid, aerosol, gel, cream or paste. Only one quart-sized bag is allowed for each passenger and in each screening bin. You may carry on more than 3.4 ounces of prescription medication, baby formula or milk. These items are not required to be in the zip-top bag and must be declared for inspection at the checkpoint. The 3.4-ounce container and quart-sized bag rules are security measures that limit the total volume of liquid you can bring onto an airplane. If you are unsure about the size or amount of your containers of liquid, put those items in your checked luggage. You can learn more online. [Visit the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) website.](https://www.dhs.gov/)
Air Travel Service Complaints or Comments
You can submit a complaint or comment online about service you received or requested from an airline or ticket agent that does not relate to airline safety or security. This may include, but is not limited to, topics such as: Flight delays and cancellations Overbooking Disability Tarmac delays Baggage Discrimination Refunds Ticketing practices Family seating Frequent flyer programs Charter flights Privacy Air ambulance service Before you contact the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) for help with an air travel problem, you should give the airline a chance to resolve it.  If you can’t resolve the problem at the airport, you may want to file a complaint with the airline.  DOT requires airlines to acknowledge consumer complaints within 30 days of receiving them and to send consumers written responses addressing these complaints within 60 days of receiving them.  DOT also requires airlines to let consumers know how to complain to them. It’s often best to email or write to the airline’s consumer office at its corporate headquarters.  If you feel that the airline does not resolve the issue to your satisfaction, you may want to file a complaint with DOT.  You may also file a complaint with DOT if you feel that you experienced unlawful discriminatory treatment in air travel by airline employees or the airline’s contractors on the basis of disability or on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex (including gender identity and sexual orientation), religion, or ancestry.  For complaints about airline safety, visit the [Airline Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01114) page instead. Online [Submit an air travel service complaint or comment.](https://www.transportation.gov/airconsumer/file-consumer-complaint) By Mail Send a letter, including your full address, phone number, and details of the issue with your trip, to: Office of Aviation Consumer Protection U.S. Department of Transportation 1200 New Jersey Avenue, SE Washington, DC 20590
Airport Facility Complaints or Comments

title: Liquor License Tax
body:
Need something else? [Business Tax Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02602) for help with payment issues, copies of filed returns, audits, and notices of unpaid taxes. The Retail Beer, Wine and Liquor License Tax must be paid by all businesses licensed by the New York State Liquor Authority that sell beer, wine, or liquor at retail or for consumption on or off premises, within New York City. [Learn more about the Retail Beer, Wine and Liquor License Tax.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/business/business-retail-beer-wine-and-liquor-license-tax.page)
Tax Rate
The tax is 25% of the annual license fees imposed on retailers under the New York State Alcoholic Beverage Control Law. If the license is issued after June 1st, the beginning of the tax year, the tax is pro-rated to account for the remainder of the tax year.
Filing and Paying
When the State Liquor Authority issues a new alcohol license, it notifies the NYC Department of Finance (DOF). DOF then bills the address listed on the license. A new bill or return will be sent each year.  The return is considered filed when payment is made.
Online You can file and pay the tax through Business Tax e-Services. You can pay by: Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) withdrawn directly from your bank E-check Credit card (American Express, Master Card, VISA, and Discover) Debit card (VISA and Master Card debit cards that don’t require the entry of a PIN number to complete a transaction) There is a 2% convenience fee for paying by credit or debit card. There is no convenience fee for paying by EFT or e-check. To pay online, you will need the notice number from your bill (first 13 digits) plus the billing zip code. If there is a debit block on the bank account and you wish to pay online or by using software, the number needed to release the block is 6136400434. [Access Business Tax e-Services.](https://a836-btseservices.nyc.gov/production/eservices/_/)
By Mail To pay by mail, follow the instructions on the notice and mail your payment along with the detached voucher. Returns should be mailed to: NYC Bill Payment Processing Center 711 Executive Boulevard, Suite H  Valley Cottage, NY 10989 Payments should be mailed to: NYC Payment Processing Center 711 Executive Boulevard, Suite H Valley Cottage, NY 10989
Deadline
The tax period starts June 1 and ends May 31 of the following year. The due date is June 26th. New license holders must pay the tax by the 25th day of the month after the month the license was issued.
Interest Rate
If you don't file your return or pay the tax by the deadline, you will be charged interest. From April 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026, the interest rate is 10%.
Ways to Get Help
You can get answers to questions about the tax or help with filing and paying. By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
By Email If you're unable to speak with a representative by phone, you can email the Department of Finance. [Contact the Department of Finance.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-us.page)

title: Baby Care and Safety
body:
If you are a new parent, you can get information about how to keep your new baby safe.
Safe Sleep for Babies
The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) has some advice on how to safely place your baby to sleep. Babies sleep safest: On their backs Until their first birthday, babies should be placed on their backs for all sleep times, including naps. Babies can breathe better on their backs than on their stomachs or sides. Babies who sleep on their sides can more easily roll onto their stomach, making it harder for them to breathe and increasing their risk of suffocation.   In an empty crib Keep soft objects, loose bedding, or any other items that could increase the risk of suffocation out of the baby’s sleep area. Do not place pillows, blankets, toys, or bumper pads anywhere in your baby’s sleep area. If one of those items gets on the baby’s face, your baby may not be able to move their face away and can suffocate.   Alone Avoid sharing a bed with your baby. Your baby should not sleep in an adult bed, on a couch, or on a chair, with you or anyone else during the day or night. The baby may suffocate if another person accidently rolls on top of them or covers their nose and mouth. The baby could also get trapped in bedding or suffocate under blankets or pillows. [Learn more about safe sleeping for babies.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/pregnancy-sleep-safety.page)
Talk to Your Baby
Talking to your baby is one of the most important ways you can help the development of your baby's brain. A texting program led by the NYC Health Department provides parents and caregivers of young children with once-a-week texts offering coaching tips and information relating to language development. Online [Learn about tips for talking to your baby.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/talktoyourbaby/index.page) By Phone Text “talk” to 55676 to begin receiving weekly coaching tips.

title: ApprenticeNYC for Advanced Manufacturing
body:
The City's ApprenticeNYC for Advanced Manufacturing helps New Yorkers develop in-demand skills in a high-growth occupation. You will be trained for and placed in roles such as CNC Machinist Welder, and Industrial Mechanic.  [Learn more about training in the industrial field.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/sbs/careers/industrial-training.page) The apprenticeship opportunity consists of two phases of full-time training. During the Pre-Apprenticeship phase, you will interview with employers to be considered for the apprenticeship. This phase includes four weeks of independent and instructor-led online training, culminating with a chance to earn a Manufacturing Certification (CMfgA). During the Apprenticeship phase, you will receive twelve weeks of paid, in-person training. The training will focus on practical learning and technical skills followed by 40 weeks of paid on-the-job training with an employer.  You would be considered an ideal candidate if you: Are 18 years and older A New York City resident Meet Federal Selective Service requirements (if applicable) Earn $50,000 or less (annually) Are committed to a long-term career in the Advanced Manufacturing sector Are comfortable with math and computers Like making things and working with your hands Can stand for long periods of time No experience is necessary to apply. You will receive a weekly stipend of $325 during the four weeks of pre-apprenticeship and a portion of your job search if you are not selected for the apprenticeship.  If you are selected, you will be paid a minimum of $18 per hour at a full-time scheduled by your employer. As you gain more skills, you receive several merit-based pay increases. By the end of the one-year apprenticeship, your hourly pay will be at least $21. [Learn more about ApprenticeNYC for Advanced Manufacturing.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/sbs/careers/construction.page)

title: Become a City Marshal
body:
City Marshals are appointed by the Mayor to enforce court orders according to fees set by State law. Marshals do not earn a City salary or pension, and they are not peace officers. You can get the application and learn about the qualifications and responsibilities for the position of City Marshal.
Minimum Qualifications
The minimum qualifications are: United States citizen Resident of New York City, or New York Counties, or Nassau, Westchester, Suffolk, Orange, Rockland, or Putnam Counties. Submission of background and financial information to DOI Satisfactory completion of approved training program Demonstrated ability to obtain required bond, currently $100,000 Recommendation by the Mayor's Committee on City Marshals (which is attained by submitting the application) [Get the complete list of City Marshal qualifications.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/marshals/marshals/qualifying-criteria.page)
Application Process
You can get an application online or in person at the Department of Investigation (DOI). Applications will not be made available by mail or fax. DOI cannot answer any questions regarding the application. Online [Learn how to become a City Marshal and download an application.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/marshals/applicants/applicants.page) In Person Department of Investigation 80 Maiden Lane, 17th Floor (between Gold and William Streets) Manhattan Walk-in Hours: Monday to Friday, 9 AM - 5:30 PM
Application Deadline There is no deadline for filing applications to become a City Marshal. Review of applications will be ongoing. Applicants will receive written confirmation of their filing.

title: Banking Corporation Tax
body:
Need something else? [Business Tax Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02602) for help with payment issues, copies of filed returns, audits, and notices of unpaid taxes. The Banking Corporation Tax (BCT) is a tax on banks and the companies they control. Examples include commercial and savings banks, savings and loan associations, and bank trust companies. Corporations that have to pay BCT are corporations defined under New York State law or under the laws of other states, the US, or other countries as authorized to do banking business. These corporations include:  Banking corporations Commercial and savings banks Savings and loan associations  Bank holding companies Trust companies Certain subsidiaries of banks that are owned by a bank or bank holding company [Learn more about the Banking Corporation Tax (BCT).](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/business/business-banking-corporation-tax-bct.page)
Who Doesn't Have to Pay
The following do not have to pay BCT: Corporations that have to pay General Corporation Tax (GCT) Trust companies of 20 or more savings banks organized under NYS law owning all capital stock Real Estate Mortgage Investment Conduits (REMICs) Corporations taxed as insurance companies under NYS Tax Law Article 33 (other than savings and insurance banks)
Filing and Paying
You must use one of the following forms to file the Banking Corporation Tax. NYC-1 NYC-1A [Get BCT forms.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/business/business-banking-corporation-tax-bct.page) You can file the forms and pay online through Business Tax e-Services or send the documents and payment by mail. The Department of Finance participates in the IRS Federal and State 1120 Corporation Tax e-file program. This program allows NYC businesses to file federal and NYC business tax returns together. Electronic filing is required for tax preparers and businesses that self-file 100 or more NYC returns.
Online You can file and pay the tax through Business Tax e-Services. You can pay by: Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) withdrawn directly from your bank E-check Credit card (American Express, Master Card, VISA, and Discover) Debit card (VISA and Master Card debit cards that don’t require the entry of a PIN number to complete a transaction) There is a 2% convenience fee for paying by credit or debit card. There is no convenience fee for paying by EFT or e-check. To pay online, you will need the notice number from your bill (first 13 digits) plus the billing zip code. If there is a debit block on the bank account and you wish to pay online or by using software, the number needed to release the block is 6136400434. [Access Business Tax e-Services.](https://a836-btseservices.nyc.gov/production/eservices/_/)
By Mail You can file the tax forms by mail. If there's a balance due, you can also send a payment by mail. For all returns, except returns claiming a refund, mail the tax form to: NYC Department of Finance P.O. Box 5564 Binghamton, NY 13902-5564 Don't send payments or requests for extensions to this address. After you have mailed the form, if you owe a payment, mail the check and the payment voucher to: NYC Department of Finance P.O. Box 3933 New York, NY 10008-3933 If you are claiming a refund, mail the form to: NYC Department of Finance P.O. Box 5563 Binghamton, NY 13902-5563
Deadline
BCT must be filed annually. Calendar year taxpayers must file on March 15 of the following year. Fiscal year taxpayers must file by the 15 day of the third month after the close of their fiscal year. If a due date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or a legal holiday, the deadline is the next business day. When paying estimated taxes, if the preceding year's tax is more than $1,000, the first installment must be 25% of this tax and be paid when filing either the preceding year's tax return or a request for an extension.
Extension Request
You can request an extension of filing time, but not an extension of time to pay. Extensions can be filed online through e-Services or by mail. Online [Access Business Tax e-Services.](https://a836-btseservices.nyc.gov/production/eservices/_/) Mail To request a filing extension by mail, you must complete the extension request form. [Download the extension request form.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/finance/downloads/pdf/25pdf/business_tax_forms/nyc-ext_2025.pdf) Mailed extension requests should be sent to the address on the form.
Interest Rates
If you don't file your return or pay the tax by the deadline, or if you overpay, you will be charged interest. From April 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026, the current interest rates are: 10% for underpayments 5% for taxes that remain or become overpaid
Refunds
You must file for a refund within three years of when the return was filed or two years of when the tax was filed and paid, whichever is later. If no return was filed, you must file within two years from the time the tax was paid. Refunds can be requested by filing an amended return. If the refund is based on changes made by the IRS or New York State, use Form NYC-3360B. You can't get a refund based on "Net Operating Loss Carryback." The Department of Finance has 90 days from the due date, extended due date, or filing date (whichever is later) to issue a refund without interest. [Get BCT forms.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/business/business-banking-corporation-tax-bct.page)
Ways to Get Help
You can get answers to questions about the tax or help with filing and paying. By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: Beaches
body:
Call 911 Call 911  to report an emergency.
Need something else? [Beach Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02229) New York City beaches are closed for the season. During the off-season, you can sit, stroll, or jog on beaches, but you cannot swim or wade in the water. Beaches will open for the season on May 23 and will remain open through September 13, 2026. During beach season, lifeguards are on duty daily from 10 AM to 6 PM. You are allowed to swim only when lifeguards are on duty. When they are not on duty, you can still sit, stroll, or jog on beaches. Never swim in closed sections of the beach. Closed sections are marked with signs or red flags. You can learn more about New York City beaches, including locations, rules, seasons, and status.
[Find a beach.](https://www.nycgovparks.org/facilities/beaches)
Beach Status
You can get the status of all public and private beaches in New York City. Status includes information about water quality, beach safety, whether the beach is open or closed, and whether a swimming and wading advisory is in effect. Please note that the “Coney Island Beach Status” applies to both Coney Island Beach and Brighton Beach.
[Get beach status and information about swimming at New York City beaches.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/beach-homepage.page)
Alcoholic Beverages
Alcoholic beverages are not allowed on public beaches.
Barbecuing
Barbecuing on a public beach is never allowed. The following authorized barbecue areas are near or next to beaches. Brooklyn - Manhattan Beach and Coney Island Leon S. Kaiser Playground - at West 33rd Street Manhattan Beach - Oriental Boulevard and Hastings Street Manhattan Beach - Northeast of the promenade, median adjacent to parking lot Queens - Rockaway Beach Michaelis-Bayswater Park - Beach Channel Drive and Beach 32nd Street O'Donohue Park - Boardwalk between Beach 20th and Beach 17th Street Staten Island - Wolfe's Pond and South/Midland Beaches Franklin D. Roosevelt Boardwalk and Beach - Midland and Lincoln Avenues Wolfe's Pond Park - Cornelia and Luten Avenues
Dogs
During beach season, dogs are not allowed on public beaches unless they are identified as a service animal. Dogs are not allowed on the sand at any New York City public beach. Leashed dogs are allowed on the boardwalks or promenades at the following beaches: Orchard Beach Coney Island Brighton Beach Midland Beach South Beach Manhattan Beach From May 1 to October 1, dogs are not allowed to enter any bathing facility, including New York City beaches.
Service Animals
A service animal is partnered with a person who has a disability and has been trained, or is being trained, by a qualified person to aid or guide a person with a disability. A person with a disability can be asked to remove their service animal from the premises if: The Service Animal is out of control and the handler does not take effective action to control it. The Service Animal is not housebroken.
Canoe and Kayak Launch Permits for Orchard Beach Lagoon
A permit is required to operate a canoe or kayak at Orchard Beach Lagoon. To get permit information for the Orchard Beach Lagoon canoe and kayak launch, contact the Department of Parks. Online [Download a Kayak and Canoe Permit Application.](https://www.nycgovparks.org/parks/pelham-bay-park/facilities/kayak) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Surfing at Rockaway Beach
Rockaway Beach between 87th and 91st Streets is New York City's first-ever surfing-only beach. It is open year-round and does not have a lifeguard on duty.
State and Federal Beaches
You can get information about beaches within New York City and the greater Long Island area that are run by New York State and federal governments. You can contact these beaches about maintenance problems and other issues. Popular beaches in parklands operated by the State include: Jones Beach Robert Moses Beach Popular beaches in parklands operated by the Federal Government include: Jacob Riis Fort Tilden Gateway National Recreation Area [Learn more about State parks and beaches in the New York City area.](https://parks.ny.gov/regions/new-york-city/default.aspx) [Learn more about Federal parks and beaches in the New York City area.](https://www.nps.gov/state/ny/index.htm)

title: Benchmarking and Energy Grading Requirements
body:
NYC Benchmarking Law The NYC Benchmarking Law, [Local Law 84 of 2009 as amended](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/local_laws/ll84of2009.pdf), requires certain buildings to annually assess the efficiency of their building's energy and water consumption. The NYC Benchmarking Law standardizes the benchmarking process by requiring building owners to submit their annual energy use in the United States Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA) online benchmarking tool, Energy Star Portfolio Manager (ESPM), by May 1 of every year. Covered Buildings Covered buildings are those that appear in the records of the Department of Finance (DOF) as: 1.    A building that exceeds 25,000 gross square feet (2323 m²)  2.    Two or more buildings on the same tax lot that together exceed 100,000 gross square feet (9290 m²)  3.    Two or more buildings held in the condominium form of ownership that are governed by the same board of managers and that together exceed 100,000 gross square feet (9290 m²), or  4.    A City building. NYC Energy Grading Law The NYC Energy Grading Law, Local Law 33 of 2018 as amended requires certain buildings to post energy efficiency scores and grades. These energy efficiency scores and grades are assigned and disclosed annually in accordance with [§28-309.12 of the NYC Administrative Code](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/apps/pdf_viewer/viewer.html?file=2022GAP_Chapter3_MaintenanceWBwm.pdf§ion=conscode_2022#page=19&zoom=auto,0,494), based on benchmarking reporting consistent with Federal energy efficiency standards. A – score is equal to or greater than 85;  B – score is equal to or greater than 70 but less than 85;  C – score is equal to or greater than 55 but less than 70;  D – score is less than 55;  F – for buildings that didn’t submit required benchmarking information;  N – for buildings exempted from benchmarking or not covered by the Energy Star program. Learn more about benchmarking and energy grading online on the Department of Buildings (DOB) website, email the DOB, or call the Sustainability Help Center, for more information. Online [Learn more about benchmarking.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/codes/ll84-benchmarking-law.page) [Learn more about energy grading.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/codes/ll33-energy-grading.page) Email Send an email to [sustainability@buildings.nyc.gov](mailto:sustainability@buildings.nyc.gov). By Phone
Agency: Department of Buildings
Division: The Sustainability Help Center (CUNY Building Performance Laboratory)
Phone Number: (212) 566-5584
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Energy Efficiency Rating Not Posted To report a building not posting its energy efficiency rating, send an email to: [sustainability@buildings.nyc.gov](mailto:sustainability@buildings.nyc.gov).

title: Bike Rules and Safety
body:
Need something else? [Biking, Rollerblading, or Skating Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02232) to report a problem caused by people biking, riding motorized scooters, rollerblading, or skating [Commercial Bicycling Laws](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02651) to learn the rules for businesses that employ delivery workers who use bikes, e-bikes, or cargo bikes  [Dirt Bikes and All-Terrain Vehicle (ATV) Storage Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03638) You can get information about bike safety, rules, and regulations. You can also request the "Bike Smart - The Official Guide to Cycling in NYC" brochure. You can learn about biking in New York City, including resources for bicyclists. [Get information about biking in NYC.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/bicyclists/bicyclists.shtml)
Bicycle Rules and Regulations
You can get information about New York City's bicycle rules and regulations and New York State's bicycle, vehicle, and traffic laws.  Online [Download a summary of bicycle rules and regulations.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/downloads/pdf/bicyclerules-english.pdf) By Mail
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to request a copy.
General Bicycle Rules and Regulations You can get a partial list of rules. More detailed information is available on the Department of Transportation's website. [Learn more about bike safety and regulations.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/bicyclists/biketips.shtml) Use of Electric Scooters and Electric Bicycles The speed limit for e-bikes, e-scooters, and pedal-assist bicycles is 15 miles per hour. [Learn more about electric scooters and electric bikes.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/bicyclists/ebikes.shtml) Bicycle Helmet Requirements Recreational Cyclists : All children up to age 14 are required by New York State law to wear bike helmets certified by the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). All bicycle riders up to age 14 must wear approved helmets. Delivery Cyclists : New York City law requires all delivery workers who use bikes, e-bikes, or cargo bikes to wear securely fastened, properly fitted helmets that are in good condition. Employers are required to ensure that their delivery cyclists wear helmets. Bicycle Rule Enforcement NYPD enforces traffic rules on City streets and in Central Park. Any cyclist not obeying all traffic rules may be issued a Traffic Violation by a police officer. Riding a Bicycle on the Sidewalk Children aged 12 or younger may ride their bicycles on the sidewalk. All other cyclists may receive a summons for riding on a City sidewalk. Safety Requirements for Delivery by Bike or E-Bike Businesses must equip their delivery bicycles with these safety devices: Bell or other audible device Reflectors Retro-reflective vests Working bicycle lights Working brakes They also must ensure delivery cyclists have access to helmets that meet City safety standards. Delivery cyclists must wear the helmets and fasten them securely. [Learn more about commercial bicycling rules and requirements.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/about/deliverybybike.shtml) Pedal-Assist Bicycles Certain pedal-assist bicycles may be legally operated on New York City streets.   Pedal-assist bicycles are defined as bicycles that have fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts (1 horsepower). The electric motor can only engage when the operator is pedaling and going less than 20 miles per hour. It stops functioning when the operator brakes, stops pedaling, or when the bicycle reaches its maximum speed. Pedal-assist bicycles cannot be equipped with any throttle capacity or have additional motorized equipment attached. The pedal-assist bicycle must have an original label, provided by the bicycle or electric motor manufacturer, stating the maximum motor-assisted speed and motor wattage of the bicycle. Pedal-assist bicycles that have been modified are not considered to be pedal-assist bicycles and may not be operated on NYC streets.
Bike Smart Brochure
You can get the "Bike Smart: The Official Guide to Cycling in New York City" brochure.  The brochure provides tips for a safe ride on: City streets Greenways Bridges Parks  Bike Smart is available in seven different languages:  English Spanish Haitian Creole Italian Korean Mandarin Russian Online [Download a copy of the Bike Smart brochure.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/bicyclists/biketips.shtml#bike-smart) By Mail
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to request a copy.
