title: NYC Biotechnology Tax Credit
body:
The NYC Biotechnology Credit is a tax credit for eligible companies in New York City. The tax credit is applied against the General Corporation Tax and Unincorporated Business Tax. The maximum credit allowed per year is $250,000. It cannot reduce the annual tax below the minimum tax required by law. If your application is approved, the Department of Finance will issue a certificate of eligibility. The tax credit is available for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2023, to December 31, 2025. It can be claimed for a maximum of three consecutive years. [Learn more about the NYC Biotechnology Tax Credit.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/benefits/biotechnology-credit.page)
Eligibility
To be eligible, a company must have qualified expenses (to calculate the credit) and meet the following requirements: Engage in biotechnology Meet one or both of the following requirements: The company must have a ratio of research and development funds to net sales that is equal to or exceeds the average ratio of all companies surveyed by the National Science Foundation The primary products or services of such company must be classified as emerging technologies Employ 100 or fewer full-time employees, with at least 75% based in New York City Have a research and development to net sales ratio of at least 6% Have annual product sales not exceeding $10 million Have gross revenues of no more than $20 million in the preceding year (this includes the gross revenues of affiliates and related members)
Deadline
You must apply no later than January 15 following the calendar year of the credit. If the due date falls on a weekend or a national holiday, the deadline will be the next business day. The deadline for 2025 was January 15, 2026.
Apply
Before you can file an application online, you must register a business tax return using e-Services. [Register or log into an e-Services account.](https://a836-btseservices.nyc.gov/production/eservices/_/) Once you have registered, you will be able to log in. From your account panel: Click "More Requests" Then select "Biotechnology Credit Application" within the Business Credit Applications section.
Get Help
By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: Vital Record Verification
body:
The NYC Office of Vital Records database isn’t accessible to other government agencies.  You can request birth or death verifications if you are from: New York City government agencies State or U.S. territory agencies Federal agencies
New York City and New York State Agencies
New York City and New York State government agencies can request certificates or verifications by mail. You must: Complete a [Premium Birth Certificate Application](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/services/birth-death-records-ordering.page#cert) or [Get the Death Certificate Application.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/services/birth-death-records-ordering.page#cert) Include a letter on official letterhead saying why you need the information Office of the Public Administrator The New York City Office of the Public Administrator can request death records to resolve estate cases. Requests for unverified death certificate will be sent to the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner (OCME) by NYC Health Department (DOHMH). Applicants will then be contacted by OCME for verification. For more information, contact the Office of Vital Records at [nycdohvr@health.nyc.gov](mailto:nycdohvr@health.nyc.gov)
Other States and Federal Agencies
Federal and State agencies can request certificates or verifications by mail. The request must include: A letter on official letterhead saying why you need the information $15 check or money order The Social Security Administration must also pay $15 for a certified copy of the record.

title: Become a Crossing Guard
body:
School crossing guards safeguard school children walking across busy intersections on their way to school. They oversee and control traffic flow around schools in the morning, at lunch time, and at the end of the school day. You can learn how to become a part-time crossing guard. You must meet certain physical and medical requirements, and complete six days of training at the NYC Police Academy once appointed. More information about the position, including how to apply, is available online. [Learn more about becoming a crossing guard.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/careers/civilians/school-crossing-guard.page) You can also contact a Traffic Safety Officer at your local police precinct for more information.

title: Bike Helmet
body:
The City provides free bicycle helmets and fittings to New York City residents at special events during spring, summer, and fall. You must be present at the event to get a helmet. All participants who receive a helmet fitting must sign a waiver.  For children under age 18, a parent or legal guardian must be present to sign the waiver. [Find a bike helmet fitting and giveaway event near you.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/bicyclists/bike-events.shtml) [Learn about how to properly fit a bike helmet.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/bicyclists/biketips.shtml#helmets)
Bike Helmet Requirements
Recreational Cyclists: All children up to age 14 are required by New York State law to wear bike helmets certified by the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). All bicycle riders up to age 14 must wear approved helmets.  Commercial Cyclists: New York City law requires all commercial cyclists to wear securely fastened, properly fitted helmets that are in good condition. Employers are required to ensure that their commercial cyclists wear helmets.
Bike Safety Rules for Children
Children 13 and under are required by New York State law to wear bike helmets certified by the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Children 12 and under may ride their bicycles on the sidewalk. All other cyclists may receive a summons for riding on a City sidewalk. Children under 1 cannot be carried on a bicycle. Children must be carried in a properly affixed child carrier. [Learn more about bike safety and regulations.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/bicyclists/bicyclists.shtml)

title: Boat Pump Out
body:

Resources for Older Adults
The Department for the Aging (NYC Aging) provides referrals to older adults 60 and older who have vision problems.   There are organizations that can help you make the best use of your remaining vision, and learn new ways to do routine daily tasks.  They will help you to be as independent as possible and continue to live safely in your own home and community. These vision rehabilitation agencies provide daily skills training and instructions on how to use a white cane to travel safely.  They can assess your needs in getting around your home, managing in the kitchen safely, reading, using large print and talking devices, and other daily tasks. The following organizations provide assistance to older adults in all boroughs, at no cost: Visions Services for the Blind and Visually Impaired Call (212) 625-1616 or toll free at (888) 245-8333 Lighthouse International Call (212) 821-9200  Helen Keller Services for the Blind Call (718) 522-2122  The Jewish Guild for the Blind ​Call (212) 769-7800  Catholic Guild for the Blind ​Call (212) 371-1000 or (212) 371-2017
NYS Commission for the Blind

title: Boiler Inspection Violation
body:
Need something else? [No Penalty Boiler Inspection](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03581) to learn about DOB's free No Penalty Safety Inspection Program for boilers You will receive a violation notice if your boiler is not inspected and an inspection report is not filed with the Department of Buildings (DOB) during the annual inspection cycle period. The inspection cycle is from January 1 to December 31 of the year. You can learn more online or by phone. Online [Get information about boiler inspections.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/safety/boiler.page) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Clear a Violation
If an inspection was not performed during the inspection cycle period, you must pay a civil penalty of $1,000. Payment must be made by certified check or money order, in US dollars, payable to NYC Department of Buildings.  By Mail or In Person Payment may be made by mail or in person to: NYC Department of Buildings - Boiler Division 280 Broadway, 1st Floor New York, NY 10007
Violation Issued in Error
If an inspection was performed during the inspection cycle period and filed with DOB, you must provide a copy of the inspection report and cashed check as proof that this violation was issued in error. Owners may need to contact their licensed professional to get a copy of the inspection report and the cashed check. Provide a copy of the inspection report and cashed check as proof that this violation was issued in error: By Email Email a scanned copy of the inspection report and cashed check (front and back) to [BoilersInfo@buildings.nyc.gov](mailto:BoilersInfo@buildings.nyc.gov). In Person Bring a copy of the inspection report and cashed check (front and back) to:  NYC Department of Buildings Customer Service Center 280 Broadway, 1st Floor (between Chambers and Reade Streets) New York, NY 10007 Certify Removal of Existing Boiler If a violation is issued for a boiler that no longer exists on the property, the owner must contact a licensed professional (master plumber or oil burner installer) to confirm the boiler does not exist by completing Form OP49 (Self-Certification for Removal of Existing Boiler). The licensed professional must state on the form how the property is being heated. [Download Form OP49 for Self Certification for Removal of Existing Boiler.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/op49.pdf) [Get instructions for filing Form OP49.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/op49_instr.pdf)

title: Boiler Operator Engineer License
body:
If you want to work as a stationary or portable high-pressure boiler engineer in New York City, the Department of Buildings (DOB) requires you to have a High Pressure Boiler Operating Engineer License. To get the license, you must pass the Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) written and practical engineer exam and have at least 5 years of experience working directly under a licensed high pressure boiler engineer, or 3 years of experience if you have a Bachelor of Science degree in mechanical engineering. Boiler operator engineers (sometimes called stationary engineers) control high pressure boilers for buildings or for industrial purposes. They are responsible for the safe operation and maintenance of boilers. The license must be renewed every 3 years.  Online [Get information about how to become a licensed high-pressure boiler engineer.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/industry/obtain-a-high-pressure-boiler-operating-engineer-license.page) [Learn more about renewing a high-pressure boiler engineer license.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/industry/high-pressure-boiler-operating-engineer-license-renewal.page) In Person You must make an appointment for in person assistance at the Department of Buildings' Licensing office: 280 Broadway 1st Floor New York, NY 10007 Monday - Friday, from 9 AM to 12 PM By Phone You can get further assistance or make an appointment.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: Breastfeeding
body:
The NYC Health Department encourages mothers to breastfeed babies. Breast milk is filled with vitamins and nutrients that babies need. It also saves time and money.  You can order free information on breastfeeding, including: NYC Mother's Guide to Breastfeeding You Have the Right to Breastfeed palm card Maternal Coaching card You've Decided to Breastfeed - Stick with It magnet Online [Learn more about breastfeeding.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/breastfeeding.page) [Download the “NYC Mother’s Guide to Breast Feeding” brochure.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/doh/downloads/pdf/csi/csi-breast-feed-mother-guide.pdf) [Download the "You Have the Right to Breastfeed" palm card.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/doh/downloads/pdf/csi/csi-breast-feed-palm-card.pdf) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Women's Healthline
Requests for the Women's Healthline are referred to the National Breastfeeding Helpline. Online [Visit the U.S. Office of Women's Health website.](https://www.womenshealth.gov/) By Phone
Agency: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
Division: National Women's Health Information Center
Phone Number: (800) 994-9662
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 6 PM
Breastfeeding Assistance
Mobile Milk Mobile Milk is a text messaging campaign to encourage and support breastfeeding. To sign up, text "MILK" to 55676. There are two types of messages that you can receive: prenatal and postpartum. Prenatal messages will end after you give birth. Postpartum messages will start after you give birth and ends when your baby is 4 months old.  Virtual Baby Cafés Baby Cafes offer free resources and support for pregnant and breastfeeding parents.  Brownsville Baby Café Thursday: 5:30 PM - 7:30 PM (646) 682-3416 [Pdejesus@health.nyc.gov](mailto:Pdejesus@health.nyc.gov)   Morrisania Baby Café English - Thursday: 11 AM Spanish - Thursday 1 PM [Register for a virtual session at the Morrisania Baby Café.](https://hhc.webex.com/mw3300/mywebex/cmr/cmr.do?siteurl=hhc&AT=join&username=lewiskd) NYC Breastfeeding Warmline The NYC Breastfeeding Warmline provides free virtual breastfeeding support and answers to questions about feeding your baby.  You can schedule a video or phone meeting with a Certified Lactation Counselor.   All calls are confidential and one-on-one. Meetings are held using Zoom, a safe and secure platform that is compliant with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).  Breastfeeding support is available in:  English  Spanish  Haitian Creole Other languages, using interpretation services
Agency: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
Division: NYC Breastfeeding Warmline
Phone Number: (646) 965-7212
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
After hours or if you get the voicemail system, leave a message with your name, phone number, and ZIP code, and briefly describe your experience feeding your baby.

title: Building Facade Inspection
body:

Notification of an Unsafe Condition
The following must report hazardous defects on a building's exterior walls: Licensed architects Engineers These must be reported right away. They can do so by submitting a Notification of UNSAFE Facade, FISP-3, in DOB NOW: Safety. The building owner should begin to repair or stabilize the exterior walls right away. The notice is not a violation or a ticket. An inspector will: Verify the hazardous conditions Determine if enough safeguards have been provided Determine if repairs are in progress If no safeguards are in place, the inspector can issue a DOB violation.

title: Business Courses
body:
NYC Department of Small Business Services (SBS) has resources for Business owners and people interested in starting a business. These include:   Seminars    Workshops   Courses    The courses are free, but class size is limited. Advanced registration is required.   You can find these events throughout the City. They provide people with information that will help them start, grow, and operate a business.   [Find a business course.](https://www.nyc.gov/nycbusiness/article/business-courses)
Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprise (M/WBE) Certification
You can get certified as a Minority and Women-Owner Business Enterprise (M/WBE). There is a virtual webinar every Wednesday.    The webinar covers:    The benefits of getting certified    An overview of the process    Application questions    A document checklist   [View a list of upcoming webinars.](https://www.eventbrite.com/o/nyc-department-of-small-business-services-5423713077)
Government Contracts
Businesses interested in getting government contracts can get one-on-one help and training. This includes local, state, and federal government contracts. Resources are available in Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Staten Island. [Learn more about government contracts.](https://www.nyc.gov/nycbusiness/article/procurement-technical-assistance)
Locally Based Enterprise (LBE) Certification
You can get certified as a Locally Based Enterprise (LBE). This is for construction businesses. You must attend a virtual webinar to certify. They are available every quarter. The webinar covers: An overview of the process Application questions A document checklist [View a list of upcoming webinars.](https://www.eventbrite.com/o/nyc-department-of-small-business-services-5423713077)
Getting Bonded
The Bond Readiness Program helps businesses:    Obtain surety bonds    Increase surety bond capacity for City construction projects     This is for NYC M/WBE Certified and small construction firms. They can receive:    Education    Training   One-on-one financial management guidance    This program is 12 sessions twice a week. There are two sessions a week. You can take it online. [Learn more about the Bond Readiness Program.](https://www.nyc.gov/nycbusiness/article/bond-readiness-program)
Emerging Business Enterprise (EBE) Certification
Businesses can get certified as an Emerging Business Enterprise (EBE). This to help socially and economically disadvantaged businesses. It is offered as a virtual webinar. The webinar covers: An overview of the process Application questions A document checklist [View a list of upcoming webinars.](https://www.eventbrite.com/o/nyc-department-of-small-business-services-5423713077)
Selling to Government
Selling to Government 101 provides vendor training for: Using the City Record Online   Using NYC Agency Procurement Plans   Vendors should bring laptops or tablets to access NYC websites during the training.  [Learn about Selling to Government 101.](https://www.nyc.gov/nycbusiness/topicpage/support-for-businesses#topic10)

title: Breastfeeding Welcome Sign and Toolkit
body:
The NYC Health Department encourages mothers to breastfeed babies. Breast milk is filled with vitamins and nutrients that babies need. It also saves time and money. Employers and small business owners can request a "Breastfeeding Welcome Here" sign and toolkit for businesses, which help support a family friendly environment for employees and customers. [Learn more about breastfeeding in the workplace.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/employee-lactation-program.page)
Breastfeeding Is Welcome Here Sign
Employers and small business owners are encouraged to designate a room for breastfeeding. You can order a "Breastfeeding Is Welcome Here" sign to help identify a space and inform employees. Bilingual signs are available in: English with Spanish English with Haitian Creole  English with Arabic Online Download the sign in: [English and Spanish](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/doh/downloads/pdf/ms/breastfeeding-welcomehere-sp.pdf) [English and Haitian Creole](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/doh/downloads/pdf/ms/breastfeeding-welcomehere-cr.pdf) [English and Arabic](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/doh/downloads/pdf/ms/breastfeeding-welcomehere-ar.pdf) By Mail
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to request a copy.
Breastfeeding Welcome Here Toolkit for Businesses
The "Breastfeeding Is Welcome Here" Toolkit for Businesses equips small businesses with tools to develop a Family Friendly environment for pregnant and parenting employees and customers. The toolkit includes: Information on the economic benefits of adopting a Breastfeeding Friendly worksite The breastfeeding Friendly pledge A sample worksite accommodation policy A poster that can be placed in a visible location for your employees to read A “Breastfeeding Welcome Here” decal
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: Business Financial Assistance
body:
Small business owners and entrepreneurs can learn about available financing products and get help applying for a financing award.
Financing Assistance
Businesses can access free assistance from NYC Small Business Services (SBS) to apply to available loan and grant resources, including federal, state, local, and private funds. SBS helps businesses: Understand which financial product is best suited for their needs Review and put together documents Calculate loan repayment terms Connect with multiple lenders, including banks, credit unions, non-profit lenders and the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) Understand loan payment deferment options [Request financing assistance.](https://sbsconnect.nyc.gov/SignIn?ReturnUrl=%2Fservices%2Ffinancing%2Finquirytype%2F%3Faction%3Dbcl) You must create an account and complete preliminary information before the session. Once you create an account, select “Financing Assistance” to continue. To apply for funding on your own, visit the City's online marketplace, [NYC Funds Finder](https://nycfundsfinder.nextstreet.com/). You can also get more information by phone.
Agency: Small Business Services
Division: NYC Small Business Services Hotline
Phone Number: (888) SBS-4NYC (888-727-4692)
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Please call (212) 618-8810 after hours.
Contract Financing
If your business is working on, or hoping to work on, a project with a City agency or City-funded entity as a prime or subcontractor, you may be eligible for a Contract Financing Loan up to $1,000,000 at an interest rate of 3 percent APR. [Get more information and apply online for contract financing.](https://www.nyc.gov/nycbusiness/article/contract-financing-loan-fund)
Financial Counseling
NYC Financial Empowerment Centers provide free one-on-one professional financial counseling in person and over the phone. Counselors can help you separate personal and business finances and more. Centers do not provide grants. Learn more on the [Financial Counseling](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02001) page.

title: Business Incentives
body:
If you run a small business, incentives can help you develop it and save money. There are different types of incentives: City State Federal Incentives can help with: Facility investment Business retention Business expansion The Department of Small Business Services (SBS) can help you access incentives. They provide: Information Guidance Technical assistance Online [Learn more about small business incentives.](https://www.nyc.gov/nycbusiness/topicpage/support-for-businesses#topic5) [Find a Business Solutions Center.](https://maps.nyc.gov/sbs/) By Phone
Agency: Small Business Services
Division: NYC Small Business Services Hotline
Phone Number: (888) SBS-4NYC (888-727-4692)
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Please call (212) 618-8810 after hours.
Energy Cost Savings Program (ECSP)
The Energy Cost Savings Program (ECSP) helps businesses save money on electricity and gas. The program offers rebates of up to: 45 percent on regulated electric costs 35 percent on regulated natural gas costs To be eligible, your business must be: A non-retail commercial or industrial business In or moving to the five boroughs, but not Manhattan South of 96th Street In a newly constructed or renovated building Strict filing deadlines apply. These businesses are not eligible: Hotels Hospitals Retail businesses Personnel services firms Public benefit corporations [Learn more about the Energy Cost Savings Program (ECSP).](https://nyc-business.nyc.gov/nycbusiness/description/energy-cost-savings-program)
Industrial Business Zone Relocation Tax Credit
The Industrial Business Zone Relocation Tax Credit helps businesses move to certain parts of New York City. To be eligible, your business must be: A manufacturing firm Moving to an Industrial Business Zone in New York City The credit: Is available one-time only Covers eligible moving costs Is up to $1,000 per full-time employee or $100,000, whichever is lower [Learn more about Industrial Business Zone Relocation Tax Credit.](https://nyc-business.nyc.gov/nycbusiness/description/industrial-business-zone-relocation-credit)

title: Business Name or Address Change
body:
You can update your business information online with the Department of Finance (DOF). New York State registration requirements include: Partnerships must register with the County Clerk's Office where the business is located. A sole proprietorship (under a name other than your own, such as a trade name or an assumed name or "doing business as") must register with the County Clerk's Office where the business is located. Corporations must register with the Secretary of State, Department of State, in Albany. Federal Employer ID Number (EIN)   By federal law, corporations, partnerships, and certain sole proprietorships must have an Employer Identification Number (EIN) to use as a taxpayer identification number. No additional identifying number is required to do business in New York City; the EIN assigned by the IRS is accepted. To apply for an EIN, use Federal Form SS-4, which is available online. title: Carbon Monoxide
body:
Call 911 Call 911  to report carbon monoxide emissions or poisoning.
Carbon Monoxide is a colorless and odorless gas that can be produced from improperly vented furnaces, plugged or cracked chimneys, water heaters, fireplaces, stoves and tail pipes. One of the most dangerous sources of carbon monoxide is car exhaust. Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Symptoms People with carbon monoxide poisoning often report feeling sick and having feelings of malaise which continues to worsen. The most common symptom of carbon monoxide is headache. Other symptoms may also include dizziness, chest pain, nausea, and vomiting.
Carbon Monoxide Detector Requirements
Building owners are required to install carbon monoxide detectors (alarms) in: All new and existing one- and two-family homes Apartment buildings Hotels, motels, and lodging or rooming houses  Apartment hotels, school dormitories, single room occupancy hotels, and welfare houses Hospitals, clinics, nursing homes, old age homes, and nurseries Schools, academies, libraries, and colleges For multiple dwellings and one- and two-family homes, you must install detectors within 15 feet of the primary entrance to each sleeping room. To report a broken or missing carbon monoxide detector in a rental unit, use the [Apartment Maintenance Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01074) page. You may not be able to get a Temporary Certificate of Occupancy or a final Certificate of Occupancy until detectors are properly in place. Carbon monoxide detectors are required to be replaced as their useful life expires, according to the manufacturer's instructions and based on the original date of installation. The replacement device must be a model that has an end-of-life alarm.   While owners are required to install and replace carbon monoxide detectors, tenants are responsible for maintaining them and changing the batteries. Tenants must pay the owner $25 when the owner installs a new carbon monoxide detector, replaces a carbon monoxide detector that has reached the end of its useful life, or replaces one that the tenant lost or damaged. Tenants have up to 1 year to make the payment. Co-ops and Condos For owner-occupied co-ops and condos, the board and the shareholders must decide who is responsible for installing carbon monoxide detectors. Deaf and Hard of Hearing Tenants Tell your landlord if you are a deaf or hard of hearing tenant who cannot hear sounds from a standard carbon monoxide or smoke detector. The landlord is required to install a detector that fits your needs. Usually, these detectors have a strobe light and must be hardwired into the building's electrical system. Exempt Buildings If your building has no fossil fuel burning furnaces or boilers, some units may be exempt from carbon monoxide rules. Additional information is available on the Department of Buildings website. [Visit the DOB website.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/index.page) Installation by Tenant Owners are required to provide and install at least one carbon monoxide detector in each apartment. Tenants can install a carbon monoxide detector, but they need to have an agreement with the owner to do it. This agreement should provide the owner access to the apartment to confirm the device is approved, installed properly, and working. If the tenant and landlord have such an agreement, the tenant does not have to pay the $25. Non-Residential and Commercial Buildings There is no requirement to install carbon monoxide detectors in commercial buildings, unless they are mixed with residential units. If there are residential units, these units need to have detectors. [Learn more about carbon monoxide detectors and regulations.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/smoke-carbon-monoxide-detectors.page)
Types of Detectors
Most hardware and drugstores sell carbon monoxide detectors marked "UL." For existing buildings, carbon monoxide detectors can be battery-operated or can plug into an electrical outlet. Detectors that plug into an outlet must have a battery backup in case the power goes out. New buildings or substantially improved buildings must have detectors that are hard-wired to the building's electrical systems. You may install a combination smoke alarm and carbon monoxide detector. Deaf and Hard of Hearing Tenants Tell your landlord if you are a deaf or hard of hearing tenant who cannot hear sounds from a standard carbon monoxide or smoke detector. The landlord is required to install a detector that fits your needs. Usually, these detectors have a strobe light and must be hardwired into the building's electrical system.
Certificate of Installation
When an owner installs a carbon monoxide detector, the owner must file a certificate of installation within 10 days of installing a carbon monoxide detector. You may file the certification electronically. Copies of the Certificate are also available at any of the Department of Housing Preservation and Development's  (HPD) Code Enforcement borough offices. Owners are also required to install signage and provide tenants with notice about the Carbon Monoxide detector legal requirements and manufacturer’s recommendations, as well as to keep records regarding carbon monoxide detector installation. [Learn more about HPD's carbon monoxide requirements.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/detectors.page) For more information about HPD Code Enforcement borough offices use the, [HPD Code Enforcement Borough Service Centers](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01073) page.

If you need general information about filing, paying, and requesting refunds, visit the page for the specific business tax type: [911 Surcharge](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02536) [Banking Corporation Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02565) [Cigarette Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02628) [Commercial Motor Vehicle Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02652) [Commercial Rent Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02653) [Fire Premiums Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02729) [General Corporation Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02504) [Horse Race Admissions Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02792) [Hotel Room Occupancy Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02794) [Liquor License Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02557) [Real Property Transfer Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02950) [Unincorporated Business Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03067) [Utility Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03071)
Failure to File
A Delinquency Notice is sent when a taxpayer: Didn’t file a tax return or an extension but had filed the previous year Didn’t file a final return indicating the business is no longer doing business in the City Didn’t file a tax return after filing an extension or a Declaration of Estimated Tax If you’ve already filed a return and made a payment for the period in the notice, you don’t have to file again. However, if you receive any additional notices about filing that return, you must respond to them. To respond to a Delinquency Notice, you must either file the delinquent return along with payment or submit a response to the notice online using Business Tax E-Services. [Access Business Tax e-Services.](https://a836-btseservices.nyc.gov/production/eservices/_/) If you’ve already submitted a response to the notice online and need to submit additional information, or if you want to submit a response that is not listed as an option on the delinquency response form, you can mail a letter along with your Delinquency Notice to: NYC Department of Finance Quality Analysis Group 375 Pearl Street, 29th Floor New York, NY 10038
Unpaid Taxes
Businesses with unpaid taxes may receive multiple notices from the Department of Finance (DOF). A Notice of Tax Due is sent when you file your business taxes, but there is an outstanding balance that remains unpaid. After an audit, you will receive a Notice of Determination if additional taxes are owed. You can dispute a Notice of Determination by filing an appeal. If you don’t respond to a Notice of Determination or a Notice of Tax Due , you will be mailed the Notice and Demand for Payment Due . If you do not pay, your case will be referred to collections, and collections may docket a warrant. If these notices go unanswered, the case is referred to DOF's Collections Division, and may be referred to an outside collection agency. DOF can impose fines (levy) or take legal action against you to collect the business tax debt, including entering a tax warrant in the court record as an enforceable judgment against you. If that happens, you’ll get a Tax Warrant Notice . That judgment is a public record and can affect your credit rating. A tax warrant may result in: Direct charges to your bank accounts Seizing assets, which may involve sending Sheriff's officers to a business or padlocking a business and auctioning off its assets Referring the judgment debt to an outside collection agency You will receive a Notice of Disallowance after a refund request has been examined, and the refund is denied.   If you receive a denial of a refund claim for General Corporation, Business Corporation, Banking Corporation and or Unincorporated tax(es), you have two years from the date stated on the Notice of Disallowance to  file a Request for Conciliation Conference or a Petition for Hearing with the Tax Appeals Tribunal. If you receive a denial of a refund claim for any other tax, you have 90 days from the date stated on the Notice of Disallowance to file a Request for Conciliation Conference or file a Petition for Hearing with the Tax Appeals Tribunal. The disallowance becomes final if you do not appeal by the deadline. If you receive a notice from a collection agency you must contact the number on the notice in order to discuss the debt. Responding to Notices If you receive a notice from DOF, you can pay your balance through Business Tax e-Services. Enter the notice number that appears on the lower left-hand side of the notice. [Access Business Tax e-Services.](https://a836-btseservices.nyc.gov/production/eservices/_/) You can also email your response to a notice. [Contact DOF about notice of taxes due and demand for payment.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-by-email/contact-notices-of-taxes-due-and-demands-for-payments.page) If you’ve received a Tax Warrant Notice you can call DOF for information.
Agency: Department of Finance
Division: Department of Finance Collections
Phone Number: (212) 440-5300
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8:30 AM - 4:30 PM
Interest and Penalties
If you don't file your return or pay the tax by the deadline, you will be charged interest. For some tax types, you can also be charged interest for underpaying. If payments are mailed, the Department of Finance (DOF) uses the postmark date as the official receipt date. If the minimum amount is not paid on time, a penalty may be imposed. To avoid being charged an underpayment penalty for underpayments of estimated tax, you should file form NYC-222, NYC-22B, or NYC-221. These forms will help you determine the correct amount of estimated tax and the proper due date. [Learn more about late filing and payment penalties.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/business/business-filing-information.page)
Interest Rates from April 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026 Tax Interest Rate 911 Surcharge 10% for underpayments Banking Corporation Tax 5% for overpayments 10% for underpayments Cigarette Tax 10% for underpayments Commercial Motor Vehicle Tax 10% for underpayments Commercial Rent Tax 10% for underpayments Fire Premiums Tax 5% for overpayments 10% for underpayments General Corporation Tax 5% for overpayments 10% for underpayments Horse Race Admissions Tax 10% for underpayments Hotel Room Occupancy Tax 10% for underpayments Liquor License Tax 10% for underpayments Real Property Transfer Tax 10% for underpayments Unincorporated Business Tax 5% for overpayments 10% for underpayments Utility Tax 10% for underpayments
Penalty or Interest Dispute To dispute a penalty or interest charge, you must write the Department of Finance a letter giving specific reasons why it should be removed. You must also include your Employer Identification Number (EIN) or Social Security Number. Requests are normally processed within 15 days. Online Log in to your [e-Services](https://a836-btseservices.nyc.gov/production/eservices/_/) account. By Mail
Mail to: NYC Department of Finance Adjustments and Discrepancy Unit PO Box 5563 Binghamton, NY 13902-5563
Disputes and Audit Appeals
If you disagree with a notice, you can send a letter or call the number on the front of the notice to discuss why you don't agree or to schedule an Exit Conference with a tax auditor. If you’ve received a formal Notice of Determination or Notice of Disallowance , you generally have a limited time to appeal. You have 90 days to appeal a Notice of Determination  (or 150 days if the Notice is addressed outside the US). You may pay the tax shown; File a Request For a Conciliation Conference; or Petition for a Tax Appeals Tribunal Hearing. [Learn more about audit appeals.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/business/business-audit-appeals-process.page) If the taxes remain unpaid, DOF may take legal action against you to collect the business tax debt, including entering a tax warrant in the Court record as an enforceable judgment against you.
Reduced Refunds Reasons a refund may be reduced include: Discrepancy in pre-payments Math error Penalty for late filing or late payment Underpayment of estimated taxes You can get more information and dispute reduced refunds by phone or email. By Email [Contact the Department of Finance.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-us.page) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Penalty or Interest Dispute To dispute a penalty or interest charge, you must write the Department of Finance a letter giving specific reasons why it should be removed. You must also include your Employer Identification Number (EIN) or Social Security Number. Requests are normally processed within 15 days. Online Log in to your [e-Services](https://a836-btseservices.nyc.gov/production/eservices/_/) account. By Mail
Mail to: NYC Department of Finance Adjustments and Discrepancy Unit PO Box 5563 Binghamton, NY 13902-5563
Payment Problems
Mailing Error If you mailed your payment to New York State by mistake, you can contact the State through their website.  [Visit the Department of Taxation and Finance website.](https://www.tax.ny.gov/) e-Services New Bank Account Email Notification The Department of Finance (DOF) will send an email anytime a new bank account or routing number is used to make a payment in your e-Services account to pay business or excise taxes. DOF needs to verify the new account information as required by federal law. This can cause a delay of up to three days for your payment to be withdrawn from your bank and posted to your e-Services account. Once the account information is verified, the payment will be withdrawn from the new bank account. Subsequent payments made from this account will not be subject to delay. The payment will be credited to the date the payment was submitted in e-Services. Bounced Payments When the Department of Finance (DOF) receives your payment, they will present it to your bank. If the funds are not available, DOF will automatically attempt to collect the funds again. If the funds cannot be collected, DOF will add a $20 penalty to the amount of tax you owe. If your payment is late, penalties and interest may also be charged. You can dispute the charges by requesting a penalty or interest adjustment. You should contact your bank with questions about its policy on bounced payments. If you need more help with a bounced payment, you can contact DOF by phone.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Missing or Misapplied Payments You can get help with questions about missing or misapplied payments. Be sure to include your: Full Name Current address Employee Identification Number (EIN) and Social Security Number Copies of your proof of payment, such as: A copy of the front and back of a canceled check A copy of a cashed money order A copy of a credit card statement The confirmation number for an online payment Online [Contact the Department of Finance.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-us.page) By Mail
Mail to: NYC Department of Finance Adjustments and Discrepancy Unit PO Box 5563 Binghamton, NY 13902-5563
Refunds
You may request a refund because of an overpayment. Overpayments may result from an amended return, an audit, or paying more money than was owed. Each type of business tax has its own refund request forms and procedures. You can learn how to request a refund by visiting the page for a specific tax type: [911 Surcharge](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02536) [Banking Corporation Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02565) [Cigarette Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02628) [Commercial Motor Vehicle Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02652) [Commercial Rent Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02653) [Fire Premiums Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02729) [General Corporation Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02504) [Horse Race Admissions Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02792) [Hotel Room Occupancy Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02794) [Real Property Transfer Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02950) [Unincorporated Business Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03067) [Utility Tax](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03071)
Refund Information and Assistance You can get information about business tax refunds, request forms, and help with refund problems. Online [Learn more and get forms for business tax overpayment refunds.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/business/business-refunds.page) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Reduced Refunds Reasons a refund may be reduced include: Discrepancy in pre-payments Math error Penalty for late filing or late payment Underpayment of estimated taxes You can get more information and dispute reduced refunds by phone or email. By Email [Contact the Department of Finance.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-us.page) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Stop Payments and Uncashed Refund Checks You may not be able to cash a refund check if an overpayment bounced after Department of Finance (DOF) already sent out a refund check for the overpayment. If that happens, DOF will put a stop payment on the refund check if you haven’t cashed it yet. DOF also puts stop payments on uncashed refund checks that are older than 6 months. If your refund check can’t be cashed but you think the money is owed to you, mail DOF a letter that includes your: Name Address (especially if you have moved) Employer Identification Number (EIN) or Social Security Number An explanation of why you think the check should be replaced Requests are normally processed within 15 days.
Mail to: NYC Department of Finance Refunds Unit 59 Maiden Lane, 20th Floor New York, NY 10038-4648
Extension Request
You can request an extension of filing time, but not an extension of time to pay. Extensions can be filed online through e-Services or by mail. Online [Access Business Tax e-Services.](https://a836-btseservices.nyc.gov/production/eservices/_/) Mail To request a filing extension by mail, you must complete the extension request form. [Download the extension request form.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/finance/downloads/pdf/25pdf/business_tax_forms/nyc-ext_2025.pdf) Mailed extension requests should be sent to the address on the form.
Debt Relief and Payment Plans
Military Service Member Debt Relief If you are an active member of the military (or a representative of one), you can request relief from business and excise tax warrants. To request debt relief, you must complete the Military Personnel Application and submit it and any required documents to the Department of Finance. To learn more, visit the [Debt Relief for Military Service Members](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02519) page. Payment Plans You can set up a payment plan to pay your outstanding balance if you are current in filing all required tax returns. Payment plans are available for UBT-I taxpayers but not for non-resident employees who file Form NYC 1127. Online [Access Business Tax e-Services.](https://a836-btseservices.nyc.gov/production/eservices/_/) By Phone
Agency: Department of Finance
Division: Department of Finance Collections
Phone Number: (212) 440-5300
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8:30 AM - 4:30 PM
Voluntary Disclosure and Compliance If you owe the City taxes, you may be eligible to join the Voluntary Disclosure and Compliance Program (VDCP). If you are accepted into VDCP, penalties will be waived and you may not be required to file past due tax returns or make tax payments for some period.  You aren’t eligible for the program if you are currently under audit by the Department of Finance or have been contacted by them for taxes due. If you are discovered before coming forward, you may face penalties, interest, and possible criminal prosecution, in addition to owing the tax amount due. To learn more, go to the [Voluntary Disclosure of Taxes Owed and Compliance (VDCP)](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03085) page.
Dissolved or Inactive Businesses
A business that’s no longer operating in New York City is still responsible for paying all the unpaid taxes that were due while it was operating. This includes penalties and interest if those taxes weren’t paid by the due date. Corporations must file annual Activity Reports for each inactive tax year. Corporations that did business in the City and paid taxes must also fill out a Request for Dissolution form and mail it to DOF. For more information, go to the [Corporation Dissolution](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01166) page.
Copies of Tax Returns
The Department of Finance (DOF) has a strong policy of tax secrecy. Only the taxpayer or the taxpayer's authorized representative may request a copy of a filed tax return. The information will only be mailed to the business address on file with DOF. There is a fee of $1 per page. Your request should include the following information: Name of business Tax identification number (EIN or SSN) Tax type Tax year or period Name and contact phone number If you’re an authorized representative, you must submit a signed [Power of Attorney](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03146) from the taxpayer with their request. Mail to: NYC Department of Finance Entity Processing Unit 59 Maiden Lane, 19th Floor New York, NY 10038 You can get help with questions about business tax return copies.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Get Help
Policy and Procedures You can get information on business tax policy and procedures and help resolving issues, including: Specific filing requirements Department of Finance (DOF) memoranda Updates on audit issues Statements of Audit Procedure (SAPs) Redacted Letter Rulings Rule-Making Actions Online [Learn about business tax support and guidance.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/business/business-tax-help.page) [Contact the Department of Finance.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-us.page) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Payments and Billing You can get business tax information and assistance with: Bills Estimated taxes Deadlines Tax rates Credits Refund denials or reductions Outstanding balances Assessments Minimum tax payment amounts Online [Learn more about business tax filing and paying.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/taxes/business.page) [Contact the Department of Finance.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-us.page) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Need more help? If you have already contacted the Department of Finance about an issue and were unable to resolve it, visit the [Taxpayer Advocate](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01663) page to learn how to get help.

title: Horse Drawn Carriage Handling Course
body:
The City provides a horse-drawn carriage driver's course. If you are planning to get a license to operate a commercial horse-driven carriage, you must first take this course and pass a final exam. The course is provided by the NYC Health Academy. It is 12 hours long and is conducted over 2 days. The cost is $25. The course is offered four times a year: January April July October You must have a valid motor vehicle driver's license issued in the United States to take this course. You will be asked to provide that license on the first day of class. Classes are held at the Health Academy, located at: The Riverside Health Center, 2nd floor 160 West 100th Street (near Columbus Avenue)
Registration and Payment
Online If you register online, you must pay with: American Express Discover Visa (debit and credit) MasterCard (debit and credit) Electronic check (you must provide your account number and bank routing number) A 2% convenience fee will be added to all credit and debit card payments. [Learn more about the Carriage Horse Driver’s Course.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/business/health-academy/carriage-horse-drivers-course.page) [Register and pay for the class.](https://a816-healthpsi.nyc.gov/OnlineRegistration/dohmh/DOHMHService) In Person If you register in person, you can pay by: Certified Check Money Order American Express Discover Visa MasterCard To register in person, visit: The Citywide Licensing Center 42 Broadway Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM Wednesday: 8:30 AM - 5:00 PM By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Get Help
You can get help by phone if you have questions about: Payments Refunds Rescheduling a class Status of temporary certificate and license surrendering Using the online registration system
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: Carshare
body:
Need something else? [Towed Vehicle](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02055) for missing personal vehicles that were parked in a carshare parking space [Illegal Parking](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01986) to report illegally parked vehicles blocking a carshare parking space [Street Sign Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01063) to report a problem with a street sign The Department of Transportation’s (DOT) Carshare program provides dedicated parking spaces for the use of eligible carshare organizations. These parking spaces are located at curbside locations and in municipal parking facilities citywide. Carshare members may reserve a vehicle, walk up to the car at their reservation time, and drive away, returning later to the same reserved spot. The following companies are participating in DOT’s Carshare program: Getaround Truqit Zipcar You must apply directly to a company for a Carshare membership. [Learn more about DOT's Carshare Program.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/motorist/carshare.shtml)
Carsharing
Carshare is a service that gives its members short-term use of a car, usually by the minute or hour. Carshare companies typically provide round-trip service, where members borrow and return cars at the same location.  Carshare benefits the environment and residents by:  Improving local air quality  Reducing congestion  Lowering household transportation costs  Improving mobility options for New Yorkers
Parking Locations
On-street and off-street carshare parking space are available citywide. You can get a list of locations online. [Find a Carshare parking location.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/motorist/carshare.shtml#locations)
Parking and Driving Rules
Carshare members are responsible for paying for all tolls, traffic or parking tickets while using a carshare vehicle. Members must also pick up and drop off vehicles to the same location.
Parking Space Rules Enforcement
Only Carshare vehicles may park in Carshare parking spaces. If you parked your own car in a carshare parking space, it is considered an illegally parked vehicle. The NYPD is authorized to ticket and tow illegally parked vehicles. The carshare company operating the service at that location can relocate a parked vehicle from its carshare parking space to the nearest available lawful on-street parking space at no charge to the carshare member or car owner. The location of towed or relocated vehicles will be shared with the nearest NYPD precinct to that carshare parking space.
Accessibility
Carshare companies participating in the program provide mobility options for customers with disabilities. The companies must provide a vehicle with professionally installed hand controls to any carshare member within 48 hours of the request.
Carshare Operations Assistance
The company whose logo is on the carshare parking space curb regulation sign is responsible for carshare operations at its parking spaces.  You should contact the carshare company directly if you have questions or problems with: Finding the car Unlocking the car Starting a trip Operating the car Ending a trip if a carshare parking space is blocked by an illegally parked vehicle
Parking Space Maintenance
The company whose logo is on the carshare parking space curb regulation sign is responsible for maintaining the space. The company must clean the curb within the carshare parking spaces and 15 feet on either side of the site to the same quality and frequency as adjacent alternate side parking regulations. Carshare companies are also responsible for removing ice or snow within 24 hours after an ice or snow event.  DOT is responsible for cleaning, repairing, or replacing damaged signs. You can report maintenance issues with signs and spaces to DOT. [Contact the Department of Transportation.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/contact/contact-form.shtml)
Carshare Program Complaint or Comment
You can make a complaint or provide feedback to DOT about the Carshare Program, including: General complaints or comments about the program Complaints or comments about specific carshare parking locations Suggestions for locations of future carshare parking spaces Maintenance issues at carshare parking locations, such as graffiti, trash, and ice or snow removal Online [Contact the Department of Transportation.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/contact/contact-form.shtml) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: Catch Basin Installation
body:
Need something else? [Catch Basin Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01084) to report a problem with an existing catch basin [Catch Basin or Sewer Odor](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02315) to report a bad smell coming from a catch basin or sewer [Highway Flooding](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02200) to report flooding on a highway [Street Flooding](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02198) to report flooding or ponding on a street The City no longer accepts requests for catch basin installations. A catch basin is a part of a storm drain or sewer system which is designed to trap debris so that it cannot enter the drainage pipes. When the City inspects a street flooding or ponding situation, it will evaluate the need for a catch basin and arrange installation if necessary.
Parts of the New York City Sewer System
Catch Basin A catch basin is a part of a storm drain or sewer system which is designed to trap debris so that it cannot enter the drainage pipes. Culvert A culvert is a drain or pipe that allows water to flow under a road, railroad, trail, or similar obstruction. Manhole A manhole is the top opening to an underground utility vault used to house an access point for making connections or performing maintenance on underground and buried public utility and other services including sewers, telephone, electricity, storm drains and gas. Manhole Cover A manhole cover is a removable plate forming the lid over the opening of a manhole, to prevent anyone or anything from falling in, and to keep out unauthorized persons and material. Sewer A sewer is a pipe under the ground for carrying away water and waste.

title: Central Park
body:
Need something else? [Events](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01892) for information about Central Park activities [Park Maintenance Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01060) Central Park is Manhattan's largest park. It extends from 59th Street, north to 110th Street and from Fifth Avenue, west to Central Park West. It is open from 6 AM to 1 AM. Central Park is operated by the Central Park Conservancy. [Learn more about Central Park.](http://www.centralparknyc.org/)
Barbecuing
Central Park only allows barbecuing on three days during the year: Memorial Day Labor Day  The 4th of July You cannot barbecue in the following areas of Central Park:  Athletic fields Closed landscapes Playgrounds Woodlands (North Woods, Ramble) Conservatory Garden (105th St and Fifth Avenue) Any other non-prohibited location in the park can be used to barbecue. Propane tanks are not allowed.
Cars in Central Park
As of June 27, 2018, Central Park is permanently closed to cars.  The four Central Park transverse roads at 97th, 86th, 79th, and 65th Streets remain open to motor vehicles.

title: Certificate of Conduct
body:
Need something else? [Certificate of Disposition](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02613) You can request a Certificate of Conduct to show whether or not you have a criminal history in New York City.  The request process depends on if you are a: NYC resident, or Former incarcerated person  [Learn more about applying for a Certificate of Conduct.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/services/law-enforcement/record-requests.page)
New York City Resident
To apply for a certificate, you must first schedule an appointment. Walk-ins are not  accepted. Only individuals with appointments may visit the office. Appointments can be scheduled online. [Schedule an appointment.](https://appointments.nypdonline.org/) Once you have an appointment, visit the Certificate of Conduct and Non-Criminal Fingerprint section (Room 152-A) at One Police Plaza in lower Manhattan. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 4 PM. Processing hours are 8 AM to 3 PM.  You must submit a $50 money order or certified check with your application. The money order or check must be made payable to New York City Police Department. Credit and debit cards are also accepted but debit cards must have a Visa or Master Card logo. You must also provide valid identification. Processing normally takes approximately 10 working days. Required Documentation Accepted types of documentation and identification required for obtaining a Certificate of Conduct are listed below. Documents must be original. No document photocopies, pictures of documents or laminated documents will be accepted. All documents must be intact.   U.S. Citizen U.S. Citizens are required to submit the following documents when applying for a Certificate of Conduct. No document photocopies will be accepted. Valid US Passport, or Original U.S. birth certificate and a valid U.S. driver's license or DMV identification card, or IDNYC (New York City identification card), or Voter's registration card and a valid driver’s license or DMV identification card, or IDNYC (New York City identification card), or Certificate of Naturalization Non-U.S. Citizen Non-U.S. Citizens are required to submit the following documents when applying for a Certificate of Conduct:  Valid passport or Alien Registration Card or Employment Authorization Card, or Current letter from the Department of Homeland Security (United States Citizenship and Immigration Services) which requests a Certificate of Conduct, local background check or non-criminal fingerprints. The letter should indicate the applicant's name, address, alien registration number and current status in this country and a valid U.S. driver's license with photo or Department Motor Vehicle photo identification card (issued in USA), or IDNYC (New York City identification card), or Current letter on letterhead from the applicant's consulate or an attorney that contains the applicant's full physical description (height, weight, hair color, eye color, etc.) and date of birth and  a valid U.S. driver’s license with photo or Department Motor Vehicle photo identification card (issued in USA) or IDNYC (New York City identification card).
Former Incarcerated Person
Former incarcerated people can request a Certificate of Relief or a Certificate of Conduct after a criminal conviction.  Both certificates can help reduce the legal barriers to employment, voting, and housing if you have a criminal record. Whether a Certificate of Relief or a Certificate of Conduct is appropriate for you depends on your criminal record. title: Certification of No Harassment
body:
Under local law, if a residential building owner wants to: Change the use or occupancy of a building or Demolish it or any of its parts They must apply for and receive a Certification of No Harassment (CONH) from the Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD). An owner must have a CONH before applying to the Department of Buildings (DOB) for a permit for any residential building that is: A single room occupancy multiple dwelling (SRO) A multiple dwelling or interim multiple dwelling located in one of the following areas: The Special Clinton District The Special Hudson Yards District Preservation Area P-2 of the Special Garment Center District The Greenpoint-Williamsburg anti-harassment area The Special West Chelsea District A multiple dwelling on the CONH Pilot Program Building List The CONH process makes sure alteration or demolition projects don't: Harass lawful occupants into leaving or  Deprive lawful occupants of their rights  HPD will investigate if harassment happened during the inquiry period. If HPD finds that harassment occurred, they begin a case at the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings(OATH).  Based on the OATH case, HPD will then decide whether to issue the CONH. Under the law, a denial of the CONH prevents an owner from getting any alteration or demolition permits for the building for a period of years. Applications may be submitted to HPD online or with a paper application. [Learn more about Certification of No Harassment or Exemption and their applications.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/certification-of-no-harassment-conh.page) Get Help Email For questions related to the CONH program, applications for SROs, Special Districts, and the pilot program, send an email to [conhinfo@hpd.nyc.gov](mailto:conhinfo@hpd.nyc.gov). By Phone
Agency: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
Division: Certificate of No Harassment
Phone Number: (212) 863-8266
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 4 PM
How to Apply
To apply for a Certification of No Harassment (CONH), a property owner must complete the application and pay the required fee as noted on the application. Applications may be submitted to HPD online or by submitting a paper application. Online You may submit a CONH Application or CONH Exemption Application for SROs, Special Zoning Districts or for the Pilot Program via the HPD Enforcement Desk.  You must establish a new user account for this application (you cannot use your existing PROS or eCertification accounts). You must confirm your user account registration by responding to the HPD Enforcement Desk confirmation email. Note: If you are using Google Chrome and the application does not open, please try a different browser. Paper Application Process You may submit a paper application as well by downloading the appropriate form below: [CONH Application](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/services/conh-application.pdf) [CONH Exemption Application](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/services/conh-application-exemption.pdf) [CONH Pilot Program Application](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/services/conh-pilot-program-application.pdf) [CONH Pilot Program Exemption Application](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/services/conh-pilot-program-application-exemption.pdf) Please read the complete instructions about how to apply and information regarding the submission of additional documents for each application.

title: Charter Schools
body:
You can get information and make complaints about charter schools and their staff. Complaints about crossing guards and school safety staff are handled by the New York Police Department (NYPD). Charter schools are public schools that are managed by a not-for-profit board of trustees.  These may include: Educators Community members Leaders from the private sector They operate with freedom from many regulations that apply to traditional public schools. Charter schools do not have to follow the public school calendar or DOE's school closure policy for severe weather or emergencies. You should contact your child's school directly for that information. [Learn more about charter schools.](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/enrollment/enroll-in-charter-schools/learn-about-charter-schools)
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Charter School Admission Policies
Admission is open to all New York City students by application and lottery, with priority given to children who live in the Community School District where the school is located and to siblings of students currently attending the school. Under the law, charter schools must have a fair and open admissions process. They must do outreach and recruitment in all parts of the community they serve. If there are more applicants than available seats, many charters use a lottery to randomly pick which students to accept. Many charter schools also have waiting lists.
Transportation for Charter School Students
For school transportation, charter schools are considered non-public schools. Students can take school buses if they live outside the district but in the same borough as the school. All other terms and conditions for pupil transportation apply.

title: Child Safety
body:
Call 911 Call 911 if a child is in immediate physical danger.
You can learn about child safety. You can also learn how to choose an appropriate child caregiver or babysitter to care for your child.
Leaving a Child Alone or with a Babysitter/Caregiver
According to the law, there is no set age at which a child can be left alone. The parent is responsible for deciding whether or not the child is mature and responsible enough take care of herself or himself. While the law does not specify age, very young children cannot take care of themselves and should not be left alone. There is no law about the minimum age that a person must be to babysit children. Parents are responsible for deciding whether or not the babysitter or caregiver is mature and responsible enough to take care of their child. Babysitter or Child Caregiver Safety Parents should be cautious when leaving children with caregivers or babysitters. You should be sure that the person you choose has the patience and experience to deal with a crying baby. You can find a licensed [Child Care](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02516) Center or get [Child Care Financial Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03118) from a center or network associated with the Administration for Children's Services (ACS). You can also report [Child Abuse](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01221) if you think that your baby's caregiver or babysitter may be abusing or neglecting your child. [Download the Child Safety brochure for tips about keeping children safe.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/acs/child-welfare/take-good-care.page) Picking a Safe Caregiver or Babysitter When choosing a caregiver or babysitter, you should select someone who: Has experience caring for babies and young children Is patient and mature enough to care for a fussy, overexcited, or crying baby Understands that young children must always be watched Will never shake, hit, yell at, make fun of, or keep food from a child as punishment Does not abuse alcohol or drugs, or carry a weapon, and will not surround a child with others who may be drinking, using or selling drugs, or carrying weapons Avoiding a Dangerous Caregiver or Babysitter There are warning signs of a potentially dangerous caregiver or babysitter. They include someone who is: Angry or very impatient when children have tantrums, cry, or misbehave Violent or controlling with their partners Physically or verbally abusive with children An abuser of alcohol and drugs, including marijuana Using prescription medications that have bad side effects or make them drowsy Not trust-worthy for any reason
When Your Baby Keeps Crying
No matter how angry or frustrated you feel when your baby or toddler cries, and no matter how much he or she cries, never shake your baby or toddler. Shaking can cause bleeding in the brain that can injure or even kill a child. It takes only a few seconds of shaking to seriously hurt a baby’s developing brain. When your baby keeps crying: Never shake your baby. Make sure he or she isn’t hungry, wet, cold or hot. Give him or her a pacifier. Walk around holding your baby close to you, in your arms or in a carrier. Talk or sing to him or her. Call a trusted friend, relative, or neighbor to talk to, or ask someone to come over and keep you company. If your baby keeps crying, put him or her in the crib. Make sure the baby is safe. Check in every five minutes or so. It is much better to let the baby cry than to do something to stop the crying that may be harmful.
Children’s Services Community Outreach for Child Safety
The Office of Community Partnerships (OCP) helps community-based organizations learn about child safety and preventing child abuse and neglect. OCP partners with the following communities to improve child safety, support families, and recruit foster homes: Bedford-Stuyvesant, Bushwick, and East New York in Brooklyn Highbridge, Mott Haven, and Soundview in the Bronx East Harlem and the Lower East Side in Manhattan Elmhurst and Jamaica in Queens Stapleton on Staten Island You can get information about joining the Community Partnership Program if you are a community-based organization, faith-based institution, or a resident in one of these areas.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Child Safety Video or DVD
The Administration for Children's Services’ (ACS) short film "A Life to Love: Preventing Accidental Injury" offers tips on keeping children safe in a variety of everyday situations. The film is 14 minutes long. It offers information about preventing tragedies such as Shaken Baby Syndrome and Sudden Infant Death Syndrome. [Watch "A Life to Love."](https://www.nyc.gov/site/acs/child-welfare/child-safety-video.page)

title: City Agency Language Access Feedback
body:
All New York City agencies, offices, and customer service centers should be able to provide free interpretation to assist customers who do not speak English or who are more comfortable communicating in another language. All agencies must also translate their most commonly distributed materials into 10 designated citywide languages. You can make a complaint about the lack of interpretation or translation at a City agency or about the quality of language access. You can also request that a City agency or office provide additional language access services to the public. Your case will not be hurt if you make a complaint or request. You can make a complaint or request no matter what your immigration status is. You are not required to leave your name, if you want to be anonymous. If you do leave your name and address, the agency will send you a letter explaining what they have done to respond to your complaint or request.
Complaints
You can make a complaint if: A City employee knew you do not speak English but did not ask if you would like an interpreter. A City employee was not able to provide an interpreter either in person or on the phone to help you understand or apply for a City service or benefit. You waited too long to receive interpretation services. The quality of interpretation or translation was poor. It helps if you can provide this information when 311 takes your complaint: A description of the problem When the problem happened The agency you spoke to The names of the employees you spoke to The Office address you went to or the phone number you called The language you speak You cannot make a complaint about private businesses or stores that did not help you in your language.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Requests
You can make a request that a City agency or office provide additional language access services to the public, including translations of agency materials. It helps if you can provide this information when 311 takes your request: The name of the agency you are making the request to The language you speak
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
New York City Public Schools Access Request
New York City Public Schools (NYCPS) schools and offices can assist customers who do not speak English or who are more comfortable speaking another language. You can make a complaint about school staff that was not able to provide an interpreter, either in person or on the phone, or translated documents. You can also make a request for additional language services. You can make a complaint no matter what your immigration status is. Your child’s status at the school will not be affected. Use the [School Document Translation](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02973) page to request to translate NYCPS documents.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Local Law 30
Local Law 30 went into effect in July 2017. It requires City agencies that provide direct services to the public to translate their most commonly distributed documents into ten designated citywide languages. Those languages are: Arabic Bengali Chinese French Haitian Creole Korean Polish Russian Spanish Urdu It also requires that City agencies with direct public services provide over-the-phone interpretation in at least 100 languages.

title: Cigarette Tax
body:
Need something else? [Business Tax Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02602) for help with payment issues, copies of filed returns, audits, and notices of unpaid taxes. The Cigarette Tax must be paid on all smoking products, whether bought for resale or the consumer. The tax is paid by a stamping agent and passed along to consumers in the cost of each pack of cigarettes. The customer pays the cigarette tax as part of the purchase price. [Learn about the Cigarette Tax.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/business/business-cigarette-tax.page)
Filing and Paying
You can get Cigarette Tax forms online. [Get Cigarette Tax forms.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/business/business-cigarette-tax.page) Online You can file and pay the tax through Business Tax e-Services after you are registered with NYC Department of Finance, Sheriff's Office, Tobacco Tax Unit. You can pay by: Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) withdrawn directly from your bank E-check Credit card (American Express, Master Card, VISA, and Discover) Debit card (VISA and Master Card debit cards that don’t require the entry of a PIN number to complete a transaction) There is a 2% convenience fee for paying by credit or debit card. There is no convenience fee for paying by EFT or e-check. To pay online, you will need the notice number from your bill (first 13 digits) plus the billing zip code. If there is a debit block on the bank account and you wish to pay online or by using software, the number needed to release the block is 6136400434. [Access Business Tax e-Services.](http://nyc.gov/eservices)
By Mail Forms and payment should be sent to the address on the form. If you use a private delivery service such as UPS or FedEx, send payments and forms to:  NYC Department of Finance Sheriff's Office Tobacco Tax Unit 30-10 Starr Avenue, 2nd Floor Long Island City, NY 11101
Interest Rate
If you don't file your return or pay the tax by the deadline, you will be charged interest. From April 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026, the interest rate is 10%.
Refunds
You can request a refund for overpayment of the Cigarette Tax. The Department of Finance doesn't pay interest on refunds for this tax. [Get Cigarette Tax forms.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/business/business-cigarette-tax.page)
Cigarette Purchase over the Internet
It is illegal to purchase untaxed cigarettes in NYC. You cannot purchase untaxed cigarettes over the internet to be shipped to any address within NYC. If you purchase cigarettes that do not have the legal tax stamp you are required to pay the NYC cigarette excise tax which is $1.50 per pack of 20 cigarettes, or $15 per carton. You must file a NYC Cigarette Tax Payment Form immediately upon receipt of the untaxed cigarettes. Additionally you must also pay the New York State cigarette and tobacco products tax which is $4.35 per pack of 20 cigarettes. You should file NYS form CG-15 “Cigarette Use Tax Return” within 24 hours of purchasing the untaxed cigarettes. Failing to pay the tax, and/or purchasing untaxed cigarettes could result in fines or criminal prosecution.
Ways to Get Help
You can get answers to questions about the tax or help with filing and paying. By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
