title: Dumpster Permit
body:
Need something else? [Dumpster Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02139) to report a dumpster that is blocking a sidewalk or street, overflowing, or uncovered The Department of Transportation (DOT) requires a Construction Debris or Commercial Refuse Container permit to place a dumpster or debris container on a City street or sidewalk. The debris or refuse container must be of commercial grade. It must also have a DOT permit before it is placed on the City street or sidewalk. Permits must be obtained by a carting company or general contractor, not by the property or business owner.  Each permit allows the placement of one refuse container. [Learn more about the commercial refuse container permit.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/infrastructure/container-permits.shtml) [Apply for a commercial refuse container permit.](https://nycstreets.net/Public/SignIn/Index)
Construction Debris Container
Worksites such as a major street or building renovation that require a Department of Buildings permit are eligible for a Construction Debris Container Permit. These dumpsters are typically 20 or 40 yard containers or numerous mini containers that are stored on the street for up to 90 days. Construction Debris Container Permits are available to carting companies registered with DOT or registered general contractors. Permits must be posted at the worksite for the duration of the construction project. [Learn about DOT construction permits.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/infrastructure/permits.shtml)
Bulk Item Refuse Container
Homeowners or commercial entities may place a refuse container on a City street or sidewalk to clean out bulk items only from their home or business. These containers may not be used for perishable waste or construction material from a worksite requiring a Department of Buildings (DOB) or DOT Construction permit.    The refuse container must be of commercial grade and placed on the City street or sidewalk by a carting company registered with DOT.  Permits must be obtained by the carting company, not by the property or business owner. Each permit allows placement of one refuse container for up to 5 consecutive days.
Refuse Container Enclosure
Property owners or tenants who want to build a structure on the sidewalk adjacent to their building to enclose a small dumpster or trash containers are required to obtain a Revocable Consent. Revocable Consents are granted by DOT's Office of Franchises, Concessions and Consents after extensive review by: City agencies Elected officials The local Community Board The City’s Public Design Commission The revocable consent agreement requires the grantee to insure the structure and pay an annual fee. [Learn about revocable consents.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/infrastructure/revconif.shtml)
Storage Container or Pod
Storage containers (sometimes referred to as "pods") used for non-construction activity, such as temporary storage or shipping of personal goods or furniture, are not permitted for storage on City streets.

title: Education Councils
body:
Community and Citywide Education Councils (CCEC) work with the Chancellor and district superintendents to review educational programs in each school district.  There are 32 Community Education Councils in New York City. Each community school district that includes public Kindergarten through 8th grade must have a Community Education Council. There are also four Citywide Education Councils that advocate for students in special populations, including: High schools English Language Learners District 75 Special Education For parents or guardians to run or vote, they must first sign up for a NYC Schools Account by going to schoolsaccount.nyc. [Learn more about education councils.](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/school-life/get-involved/education-councils) [Get information about Education Council elections.](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/get-involved/families/education-councils/currently-available-council-seats)
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Term Duration
All Community and Citywide Education Council members are selected for 2-year terms by the officers of the Parent Associations or Parent Teacher Associations (PA/PTAs) of the schools in their district. The new term will began July 1, 2025 and continues through June 30, 2027.

title: Basement Apartment Conversion Pilot Program (BACPP)
body:
The Basement Apartment Conversion Pilot Program (BACPP) was a program for homeowners in Brooklyn's Community District 5. The program's goal was to create more legal, safe housing. Eligible homeowners could receive loans to convert their basements or cellars into apartments. These units had to be: Safe Legal Available for rent These loans were either low-interest or no-interest. In some instances, they were forgivable. To be eligible, the building had to be: A 1-3 family building Located in Brooklyn's Community District 5, which includes East New York or Cypress Hills neighborhoods Applications are no longer being considered. Information and assistance are available in English and Spanish. [Learn more about the pilot program.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/basement-apartment-conversion-pilot-program.page)

title: Electric Vehicle
body:
Need something else? [Illegal Parking](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01986) to report a vehicle parked at a charging station but not actively charging New York City supports the use of all-electric vehicles (EVs). EVs are a clean alternative to gasoline and diesel-fueled vehicles. EVs: Reduce fuel costs Emit 70% less carbon dioxide emissions Do not pollute from tailpipes EVs reduce pollution and keep New York City streets clean. [Learn more about all-electric vehicles (EVs).](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/motorist/electric-vehicles.shtml#/find/nearest)
Electric Vehicles Incentives
You can get a Federal tax rebate on the purchase of an electric vehicle. The tax rebate is up to $7,500 (based on the battery size). Electric vehicles can use carpool lanes on the Long Island Expressway. The number of passengers does not matter. [Learn about electric vehicle Federal tax incentives.](https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/taxcenter.shtml) [Learn about the New York State Clean Pass Vehicle program.](https://www.dot.ny.gov/programs/clean-pass)
DOT Electric Vehicle Charging Program
Curbside Charging Program Department of Transportation (DOT) has installed 100 public curbside EV chargers across all 5 boroughs. This is in partnership with Con Edison and charging provider FLO. EV owners pay for curbside charging on a per hour basis using FLO's mobile app or a Radio-Frequency Identification (RFID) card. These parking spaces are reserved for actively charging EVs only. Vehicles parked in these spaces but not actively charging may be ticketed by the NYPD. In addition to the “EV Charging Only” regulations at curbside charges, users are still responsible for complying with existing on-street parking regulations, including metered parking regulations.  [Find curbside charging locations.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/motorist/electric-vehicles.shtml#/curbside) Contact FLO for issues with curbside FLO EV chargers: Online: [FLO.com/new-york-city](https://www.flo.com/new-york-city/) Phone: (855) 543-8356 Municipal Lots and Garages Charging Program DOT is building a network of EV Charging Station Hubs offering Level 2 and DC Fast Charging options (up to 150kw) at DOT-owned public parking facilities across the City. This is in partnership with New York Power Authority (NYPA) and EV Connect. Drivers must pay for parking at the municipal lots and follow the posted parking regulation signs. The city currently operates three DC fast charging hubs at the following city-owned public parking facilities:  Court Square Municipal Parking Garage in Queens  Queens Borough Hall Municipal Parking Garage in Queens  Delancey/Essex Municipal Parking Garage in Manhattan White Plains Road Municipal Parking Field in the Bronx Bensonhurst #1 Municipal Parking Field in Brooklyn Contact EV Connect for issues with EV Connect Garage & Lot Chargers: By Email: [driver_support@evconnect.com](mailto:driver_support@evconnect.com) Phone: (866) 816-7584 To report an EV Charger issue in a Municipal Garage or Lot, visit the [Public Garages and Parking Lots](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02380) page. Learn More You can learn more about the curbside charging program, DOT's EV charging programs, and charger locations online. [Learn more about curbside EV charging.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/motorist/electric-vehicles.shtml#/curbside) [Find locations of public electric vehicle chargers nationwide.](https://afdc.energy.gov/stations#/find/nearest) [Submit feedback about the Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Station Program.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/contact/contact-form.shtml?routing=ev)
DCAS Electric Vehicle Charging Program
The Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) offers general public access to fleet chargers located in publicly accessible locations for a fee. Participants must have a ChargePoint card. [Learn more about DCAS public charging ports.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dcas/downloads/pdf/fleet/electric-vehicle-public-charging-rules.pdf) The public chargers are located in: Bronx Van Cortlandt Park Golf Course 189 Van Cortlandt Ave W Bronx, NY 10471 Van Cortlandt Park Shandler Rec Area Ballfield Lot Bronx, NY 10467 Manhattan  Icahn Stadium 10 Central Road New York, NY 10035 Queens Central Storehouse 66-26 Metropolitan Avenue Queens, NY 11379 World’s Fair Marina 109-5 Marina Road Corona, NY 11368  Rockaway Beach 102 32 Street Queens, NY 11691  Staten Island Midland Beach, Lot 8 920 Father Capodanno Blvd, Midland Beach, NY 10305 Ocean Breeze Athletic Complex 625 Father Capodanno Blvd Staten Island, NY 10305 Report a Problem To report a problem with DCAS public charging ports, send an email to [NYCFleet@dcas.nyc.gov.](mailto:NYCFleet@dcas.nyc.gov)
Home Charger Installation and Reducing Costs
Electric Vehicle Charger Home Installation EV chargers require a direct connection to an electrical panel in a home. A licensed electrician must complete the installation. They can handle the permit requirements for the installation. Reducing Electricity Costs for Vehicle Charging Most customers pay for electricity based on a flat rate. This means that the cost of electric is the same no matter what time you use it. You can use "late night electricity" to save money. This means electricity used during overnight is cheaper. Electricity used during the day is more expensive. Homeowners can take advantage of late-night electricity billing by either: Adding a second electric meter Choosing to pay for electricity based on "time of use"

[Kindergarten Enrollment](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02834) [School Transfer](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02989) [Charter Schools](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02617) Students who are new to the public school or have moved to a new neighborhood can register at their zoned school once the school year begins. Both the student and a parent or guardian must be present at the time of registration with all the required documentation. To find a zoned school, go to the [School Zones](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02991) page. Online [Get enrollment information for kindergarten and elementary school.](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/enrollment/enroll-grade-by-grade/kindergarten) You can also email questions to [ESEnrollment@schools.nyc.gov](mailto:ESEnrollment@schools.nyc.gov). By Phone
Agency: Department of Education
Division: Office of Student Enrollment
Phone Number: (718) 935-2009
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 6 PM
Agents are available during business hours, except on public school holidays.
No Zoned School
Students who are new to the New York City public school system or have moved to a new neighborhood and don't have a zoned school can enroll at a [Family Welcome Center](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03128). Online [Family Welcome Centers](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03128) are providing assistance online. By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Registration Requirements
What to Bring to Register To register your child for school, you must bring: Two proofs of address Proof of the child's age, such as a birth certificate, passport, or record of baptism Your child's immunization records Latest report card/transcript (if available) Individualized Education Program (IEP) and/or 504 Accommodation Plan (if applicable and available) All children under the age of 5 years (6-59 months) are required to receive the flu shot if they attend a New York City regulated preschool or child care center. Visit the [Flu Shot and Prevention](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02735) page to learn more. Proof of Address Bring two of the following to prove your address: Income tax form for the last calendar year State, City, or other government-issued identification (including an IDNYC card) which isn't expired, and includes the address of residence Official NYS Driver License, Non-Driver ID card, or learner permit which isn't expired, and includes the address of residence A rent receipt, which includes the address of residence, dated within the past 60 days A residential utility bill (gas or electric) issued by National Grid, Con Edison, or the Long Island Power Authority dated within the past 60 days Water bill for the residence dated within the past 90 days A cable bill for the residence, which includes the name of the parent and the address of residence, dated within the past 60 days Documentation or a letter on letterhead from a federal, state, or local government agency dated within the past 60 days that includes the resident's name and address. Examples of agencies include: Internal Revenue Service (IRS) New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) The federal Office of Refugee Resettlement Human Resources Administration (HRA) Administration for Children's Services (ACS) or an ACS subcontractor A lease agreement, deed, or mortgage statement for the residence A current property tax bill for the residence Official payroll documentation from an employer issued within the past 60 days that includes the home address, A letter on the employer's letterhead isn't adequate. Examples include: Paystub with home address Form submitted for tax withholding purposes Payroll receipt Voter registration documents that include the name of the parent and the address of residence Unexpired membership document based upon residency, such as neighborhood residents' association, which includes the name of the parent and the address of residence Evidence of custody of the child, including judicial custody orders or guardianship papers issued within the past 60 days that includes the name of the student and the home address

title: Emergency Preparedness
body:
Need something else? [Hurricane Preparedness](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02810) to learn about hurricane preparation, including evacuation zones and centers [Notify NYC](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01082) to learn about the public messaging system which informs the public of emergency activity in New York City [Prescription Preparedness](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01605) to learn how to prepare for emergencies if you take prescription medication NYC Emergency Management (NYCEM) created the Ready New York campaign in 2003 to educate New Yorkers about the hazards they may face. The campaign also encourages residents to prepare for all types of emergencies in New York City. You can get Ready New York guides that cover a variety of topics. You can also learn about other Ready New York resources and events.
Request a Ready New York Guide
You can get Ready New York guides that outline the very basic steps New Yorkers should take to prepare for emergencies. The guides also contain information about how to put together a Go Bag and an emergency supply kit. Although the City does not provide Go Bags, Ready New York explains how to assemble one. In addition to the general Ready New York guides, there are specialized guides for: Elementary and middle school students Seniors People with disabilities Businesses Pets You can also get: A pocket-sized Ready New York guide A quick reference card to record your disaster plan details and contact information for all household members Audio versions of Ready New York guides for the hard of hearing Select guides are available in English, Spanish, Arabic, Bengali, Chinese, French, Haitian Creole, Italian, Korean, Polish, Russian, Urdu, and Yiddish, as well as others. You also can download the Ready NYC mobile application for your Apple or Android device. Online [Get Ready New York Guides and Resources.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/ready/guides-resources.page) [Download a Ready New York pocket guide.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/ready/guides-resources.page#pocket_guide) [Download the Ready New York Reference Card.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/em/downloads/pdf/emergency_reference_card.pdf) [Download the Ready NYC app.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/ready/guides-resources.page#rny_app) [Email the Ready New York program.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/ready/ready-new-york-inquiries.page) By Mail
Ready New York Program New York City Emergency Management 165 Cadman Plaza East Brooklyn, NY 11201
Ready New York: My Emergency Plan
The Ready New York: My Emergency Plan + Hurricanes and New York City is an interactive workbook designed to help New Yorkers, especially those with disabilities and access and functional needs, create an emergency plan.  My Emergency Plan walks users through: Establishing a support network Capturing important health information  Evacuation planning Gathering emergency supplies How to prepare for a hurricane, including a map detailing hurricane evacuation zones and routes in New York City The Ready New York: Hurricanes and New York City guide is now included in the My Emergency Plan workbook. The workbook is available in the following languages: English Spanish Chinese Russian Arabic Bengali French Haitian Creole Italian Korean Polish Urdu Yiddish Online [Download Ready New York: My Emergency Plan.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/ready/guides-resources.page#my_emergency_plan) By Mail
Ready New York Program New York City Emergency Management 165 Cadman Plaza East Brooklyn, NY 11201
Ready New York Videos
NYC Emergency Management has produced videos that focus on emergency preparedness.  These videos are available online. [Watch Ready New York Videos.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/ready/videos-more.page) [Request copies of Ready New York materials.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/ready/ready-new-york-inquiries.page)
Ready New York Events
NYC Emergency Management hosts presentations and fairs designed to educate New Yorkers about how to prepare for all types of emergencies.  You can search for a Ready New York Event on the Citywide Events Calendar, or visit the Ready New York program online. [Find an event on the Citywide Events Calendar.](https://www.nyc.gov/main/events/) [Learn more about Ready New York.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/ready/ready-new-york.page)
Request a Ready New York Speaker
Ready New York speakers teach emergency preparedness to community groups, businesses, schools, and other groups. Trained speakers from NYC Emergency Management provide a detailed presentation on the most common hazards New Yorkers may face and how to prepare for them.  [Learn how to request a Ready New York speaker.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/ready/request-event.page)
Community Preparedness
NYC Emergency Management helps local organizations build capacity within their community to prepare for, respond to, and recover from an emergency through its Community Preparedness program. Online [Learn about community preparedness.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/ready/community-preparedness.page) [Contact the Community Preparedness Team.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/ready/community-preparedness-inquiries.page) By Mail Community Preparedness Program New York City Emergency Management 165 Cadman Plaza East Brooklyn, NY 11201
PlanNowNYC
You can get information about how to stay safe during a terrorist attack or other emergency situation. PlanNowNYC provides tips to help you stay informed about possible emergencies and make a plan. [Learn about staying safe during an emergency.](https://plannownyc.cityofnewyork.us/)
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: Emergency Action Plan (EAP) Director On-Site Test
body:
A candidate's supervisor can get information about scheduling an on-site Emergency Action Plan (EAP) Director test. Candidates cannot schedule their own tests. The supervisor can request an exam by email. Please note “FSD On-Site request/Candidate’s last name, first name/Premises address” in the subject line. The email should include: Premises information, such as the type (ie, hotel, office), the address (including borough and ZIP), Building ID Number, and any Also Known As addresses. Candidate's Information, including social security number and Certificate of Fitness number for the premises. Additional requirements, including if the exam must take place outside of the regular start time, Monday - Thursday, from 10 AM to noon. Supervisor's name, title, business address, contact phone number, and email address. To request an exam, send an email to [High-Rise@fdny.nyc.gov](mailto:High-Rise@fdny.nyc.gov).
Supervisor Requirements
Before requesting an on-site exam, the supervisor must: Ensure the candidate is qualified by the Certification Unit Ensure the building has an accepted EAP on file with FDNY
Candidate Requirements
To qualify for the EAP Director on-site test, the candidate must: Hold an F-58, F-25, or F-85 Certificate of Fitness as a Fire Safety Director for the building in question Pass a 7-hour approved EAP Director course Pass the EAP Director computer exam Once all information has been verified by the Certificate of Fitness Unit, the candidate will have 1 year to take the on-site exam.
Emergency Overtime Test
In the case of hardship, you can schedule an emergency overtime test Monday to Friday after 4 PM. The licensed master fire suppression contractor must make this request in writing. The City will bill the contractor for the additional overtime expense.
Cancel an EAP Director On-Site Test
All requests for cancellations must be submitted via email at least 72 hours before the scheduled exam time. Please note "Request for On-Site Exam Cancellation" in the subject of the email. The email should also include the candidate's name, social security number, exam date, and premises address. This information will help expedite the cancellation. To request a cancellation, send an email to [High-Rise@fdny.nyc.gov](mailto:High-Rise@fdny.nyc.gov).

title: DOB Proof of Compliance for OATH Violation
body:
If you receive an Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH) violation, formerly known as Environmental Control Board (ECB) from the Department of Buildings (DOB), you must correct the violating condition in a timely manner and submit the following documents for proof of compliance: An original Certificate of Correction affidavit ([AEU2 Form](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/aeu2.pdf) or [AEU3321 Form](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/aeu3321.pdf)) Proof of correction such as  permits, photographs, receipts, inspection results, etc. and A notarized statement ([AEU20 Form](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/aeu20.pdf)) attesting to how the violation was corrected, if submitting an AEU2 form Proof of payment of any applicable DOB civil penalties [Learn more about correcting DOB OATH violations.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/safety/oath-summonses.page) Submitting Documents The paper Certificate of Correction affidavit and statement forms can no longer be sent or delivered in-person. To certify correction, submit the required documents to DOB's Administrative Enforcement Unit (AEU) in DOB NOW, use an eFiling account to login to DOB NOW and select the BIS Options portal. [Download the Certificate of Correction Request User Guide for step-by-step instructions.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/cofc_user_guide.pdf) If you already have a DOB eFiling account, you can log into DOB NOW and select the BIS Options portal. [Log into DOB NOW.](https://nyc.gov/dobnow) If you don't have an account, you can create a new eFiling account.  [Register with eFiling.](https://a810-efiling.nyc.gov/eRenewal/loginER.jsp) DOB will assist you with submitting a Certificate of Correction.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
How to Pay a Penalty You can pay a penalty using CityPay. [Use CityPay to pay an OATH violation.](https://a836-citypay.nyc.gov/citypay/ecb)
Immediately Hazardous (Class 1) Summonses
You must correct Class 1 (immediately hazardous) violations immediately. If the immediately hazardous condition is not corrected in a timely manner, you may be issued a DOB Violation with a $1500 civil penalty. The $1500 civil penalty is in addition to penalties assessed by OATH. [Learn more about correcting DOB OATH violations.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/safety/oath-summonses.page)
NYC.ID Account
Starting on June 3, 2024, all existing and new DOB NOW users are required to have an NYC.ID account. Users will complete a one-time process of creating an NYC.ID account An NYC.ID account is required to access DOB NOW: Build Safety BIS Options Licensing DOB NOW: Inspections and eFiling account registration is not changing and will not require an NYC.ID account [See NYC.ID announcement.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dobnow_login_sn.pdf)

title: Hurricane Evacuation
body:
Call 911 Call 911  if someone is in immediate danger.
During a hurricane or coastal storm, the Mayor may issue an evacuation order for those living in hurricane evacuation zones. Specific instructions about which areas of the City should be evacuated will be communicated through various channels, including: Local media [Notify NYC](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01082) [NYC.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/) [NYC.gov/emergencymanagement](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/index.page) [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/NYCGov) [X (formerly known as Twitter)](https://x.com/nycgov) If you are in an evacuation zone and your zone is ordered to evacuate: Leave as soon as you can.  Consider going to a hotel, a friend or relative’s home, or an evacuation shelter.  Bring a Go Bag with important documents and items along with you. Evacuate early if you rely on elevators to get out of your building. Elevators may be out of service and may not be always available. Use public transportation to evacuate, if possible. Be aware that public transportation, including MTA's Access-A-Ride, may shut down hours before the storm arrives. Allow additional travel time and consider your needs. [Learn more about hurricane evacuation.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/ready/coastal-storms-hurricanes.page)
Evacuation Zones and Centers
Hurricane evacuation zones are areas that may be affected by storm surge flooding. The City uses data from the National Weather Service, topographic maps, and actual events to define areas that are most at risk. During coastal storms, evacuation areas are identified by the assigned zone. When a coastal storm is approaching, the City may order the evacuation of neighborhoods in danger of flooding from storm surge, starting with whatever Zone the storm reaches first and adding more Zones as needed.  You can find out: If you live in a hurricane evacuation zone The hazards you may face from a hurricane How to prepare for a hurricane Locations of hurricane evacuation centers Make sure to include the borough and zip code when looking up an address. The evacuation centers are listed in order of proximity to your address. [Look up your hurricane evacuation zone and find evacuation centers near you.](https://finder.nyc.gov/hurricane)
If you need to evacuate and can’t stay at a hotel or with family or friends, you can stay at an emergency evacuation center. Evacuation centers will be set up in schools, City buildings, and places of worship. Family members or members of your emergency support network can come with you. Many evacuation centers are wheelchair accessible. Evacuation centers provide basic food, water, and supplies but you should be prepared to bring a Go Bag with special medical equipment and items that you may need. Locations are subject to change depending on the emergency.  Medical Conditions and Equipment at Centers Evacuation centers have a limited ability to provide medical services. If you are sick or have a serious medical condition, go to a hospital instead of a center. If you need mobility aids, oxygen tanks, or other medical equipment, bring it with you to the evacuation center. You will probably be taken to a Special Medical Needs Evacuation Center. Refrigeration for medication will only be provided at accessible evacuation centers. If possible, bring a small cooler or ice pack so that you can keep your medicine cold. Personal Electronic Use at Centers Evacuation centers will provide access to charging stations for electronic devices. You will be given priority if you need to charge medical or other equipment. The City is not responsible for items or devices that are left unattended. Evacuation Guidance for People with Disabilities If possible, make arrangements with friends, family, or neighbors before weather conditions become severe.  If an evacuation order is in effect for your area, stay with family or friends if possible and use shelters as a last resort. Check and see if they have symptoms of COVID-19 or have people in their home at higher risk for serious illness. If they have symptoms or people at higher risk in their home, make other arrangements. Most evacuation centers do not have special equipment, such as oxygen and mobility aids. Some of them will be able to address special needs but have a limited ability to provide medical services. If you are sick or have a serious medical condition, go to a hospital instead of a center. Evacuation centers will take pets and service animals, but you must bring supplies and food for them. Carriers are strongly recommended to contain pets in a crowded environment.  [Get more information about emergency preparedness.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/mopd/resources/emergency-preparedness.page)
Go Bag
Everyone in your household should have a Go Bag; a collection of things you would want if you have to leave in a hurry. Your Go Bag should be sturdy and easy to carry, like a backpack or a small suitcase on wheels. You'll need to customize your Go Bag for your personal needs. Pack your Go Bag with the following items: Bottled water and nonperishable food, such as granola bars Copies of your important documents in a waterproof container (e.g., insurance cards, Medicare/Medicaid cards, photo IDs, proof of address, marriage and birth certificates, copies of credit and ATM cards) Flashlight, hand-crank or battery-operated AM/FM radio, and extra batteries List of the medications you take, why you take them, and their dosages Contact information for your household and members of your support network Cash, in small bills Notepad and pen Back-up medical equipment (e.g., glasses, batteries) and chargers Aerosol tire repair kits and/or tire inflator to repair flat wheelchair or scooter tires Supplies for your service animal or pet (e.g., food, extra water, bowl, leash, cleaning items, vaccination records, and medications) Portable cell phone chargers Other personal items Include items that can help protect you and others from COVID-19, including hand sanitizer, and face coverings for each person.
Transportation Assistance
When the Mayor issues an evacuation order during a hurricane or coastal storm, you can request transportation assistance through 311 if you: Are a person with a disability or other access or functional needs, and Have no other options to evacuate safely. Depending on your need, you will either be taken to:  An accessible evacuation center in an accessible vehicle, or   A hospital outside of the evacuation zone via ambulance You may not be able to request transportation to a specific address.
Pet Evacuation
If you are a pet owner, make every effort to shelter your pet at a kennel or with friends or relatives outside the evacuation area. At all times, you are allowed to bring a pet in a carrier on MTA subways, buses, and trains. You must have the pet muzzled and controlled on a sturdy leash. When an evacuation order is declared, you can bring a legal pet too large for a carrier. Pets at Evacuation Centers Only legal pets are allowed in evacuation centers. Service animals are always allowed. If you bring your pet to an evacuation center, please bring supplies to care for your pet, including: A secure cage or carrier Proof of required shots Food and water Medication A leash A muzzle You are responsible for the feeding, clean up, and care of your pet at the center. You do not need a cage or carrier for a service animal that helps people with disabilities. For more information on pet emergency planning, visit the [Emergency Preparedness](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02713) page to review the Ready New York: My Pet’s Emergency Plan.
Coastal Evacuation Route Signs
The City has installed Coastal Evacuation Route signs in parts of the Bronx, Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island. These signs help direct residents who will be driving personal vehicles to evacuation centers in the event of a coastal storm evacuation. You can get maps detailing potential hurricane evacuation zones and routes in New York City. [Get hurricane preparation resources, including maps and guides.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/em/ready/guides-resources.page#hurricane_guide)

title: Fair Workweek Law
body:
Under the Fair Workweek Law, fast food, retail, and utility safety employers in New York City must give workers predictable work schedules.  Also, fast food employers:  Must give existing workers the chance to work more hours before hiring new workers  Cannot fire or lay off workers or reduce their hours by more than 15% without just cause or a legitimate economic reason Fast food, retail, and utility safety workers and employers in New York City can get more information and assistance from the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) about: Legal rights for fast food, retail, and utility safety workers Legal responsibilities for fast food, retail, and utility safety employers Complaints about employers Online [Get more information about the Fair Workweek Law](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/workers/workersrights/fastfood-retail-workers.page). Submit questions by email to [OLPS@dca.nyc.gov](mailto:OLPS@dca.nyc.gov). By Phone A DCWP representative can answer questions during regular business hours.
Agency: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
Division: Office of Labor Policy and Standards
Phone Number: (212) 436-0380
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Phone assistance is available, but some calls may go straight to voice mail. Please leave a detailed message and a representative will contact you. As an alternative, visit nyc.gov/workers.
Worker Rights Under the Law
Retail and utility safety worker rights under the Fair Workweek Law include: 72 hours’ advance notice of work schedule No on-call shifts No call-in shifts within 72 hours of the start of the shift No shift cancellations with less than 72 hours’ notice No shift additions with less than 72 hours’ notice unless worker consents in writing Updated written schedule from employers if changes are made with less than 72 hours’ notice Fast food worker rights include: No firing or reduction of hours without just cause No layoffs except for economic reasons Written explanation for firing, reduction of hours, or layoff  Regular schedule and first work schedule in writing on or before first day of work 14 days’ advance notice of work schedule Premium pay for schedule changes by employer less than 14 days before the first shift on the work schedule and the right to say no to additional hours $100 premium to work “clopening” shifts and the right to say no Priority to laid-off or current workers to work newly available shifts before employer hires new employees
Starbucks Settlement
In December 2025, DCWP announced a settlement with Starbucks that requires Starbucks to pay more than $35.5 million in restitution to over 15,000 workers harmed by its unlawful practices, as well as any additional workers who come forward. In addition, DCWP is monitoring Starbucks' compliance with reinstating any workers who were laid off following recent closures of New York City stores. Eligibility You may be eligible for restitution if you worked for Starbucks in an hourly position between July 4, 2021 and July 7, 2024. You will receive a check in the mail this winter. If you are an employee who experienced a violation after July 7, 2024, you may still be eligible for compensation by filing a complaint with DCWP. If you are a laid off Starbucks employee who was denied the right to reinstatement at another Starbucks location, file a complaint with DCWP. [File a complaint.](https://a866-dcwpbp.nyc.gov/worker-complaint/file-complaint?topic=fair-workweek-fast-food) If you have any questions regarding this settlement, contact the DCWP Office of Labor and Policy Standards (OLPS) at [OLPS@dcwp.nyc.gov](mailto:OLPS@dcwp.nyc.gov).
Dunkin', Taco Bell, and Theory Settlements
The Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) announced settlements with Dunkin' and Taco Bell franchisee Salz Management LLC and fashion retailer Theory over violations of the City's Fair Workweek Law. Under the settlement, Salz Management and Theory must pay restitution to 830 workers named in the settlement. If you are named in the settlement, DCWP will contact you on how to get payment. Theory workers from the two store locations involved in the settlement will receive a check via mail or direct deposit beginning April 2026. Salz Management workers will receive two checks via mail or direct deposit around August 2026 and January 2027. If you have any questions regarding your payment or need to change an address, reach out to DCWP by emailing [dcwp@noticeadministrator.com](mailto:dcwp@noticeadministrator.com).

title: Family Homelessness and Eviction Prevention Supplement (FHEPS)
body:
The Family Homelessness and Eviction Prevention Supplement (FHEPS) program provides rental assistance for permanent housing for families with children that receive Cash Assistance AND: live in shelters  are being evicted OR have been evicted   FHEPS was formerly known as FEPS, or the Family Eviction Prevention Supplement. If you live in a shelter, you can get help applying for FHEPS from your case manager or housing specialist. If you live in the community, you can find out if you are eligible by visiting a Human Resources Administration (HRA) Benefits Access Center (formerly known as Job Center). [Learn more about the FHEPS program.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/fheps.page)
You can get the locations, hours and phone numbers of Benefits Access Centers in your area. All Centers are accessible for people who use wheelchairs. [Find a Benefits Access Center.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/locations/job-locations-and-service-centers.page)
FHEPS Eligibility
FHEPS eligibility for families includes these requirements, among others. Families that qualify for FHEPS must include: A child under 18 years of age, A child 18 years of age who is enrolled full time in high school, or a vocational or technical training program, OR A pregnant woman Families qualifying for FHEPS must also: Live in or be eligible to live in an HRA shelter Live in a DHS shelter after being evicted from their home sometime in the year before they entered shelter Have lost their housing because of a domestic violence situation Have lost their housing because of health or safety issues, OR Be facing eviction or have been evicted in NYC within the past 12 months. Families must have an active Cash Assistance case or qualify for Cash Assistance once they leave a homeless shelter.
Apply
If you live in a shelter, you can get help applying for FHEPS from your case manager or housing specialist. If you want to stay in your current residence, the HRA Homelessness Diversion Unit (HDU) at your Benefits Access Center (formerly known as Job Center) will initiate your FHEPS application and refer it for a final FHEPS eligibility determination.
You can get the locations, hours and phone numbers of Benefits Access Centers in your area. All Centers are accessible for people who use wheelchairs. [Find a Benefits Access Center.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/locations/job-locations-and-service-centers.page)
Modify or Restore a FHEPS Grant
The HRA Homelessness Diversion Unit (HDU) at your Benefits Access Center (formerly known as Job Center) can submit requests to modify an existing FHEPS grant or restore a closed FHEPS grant.  You can request a modification to your FHEPS grant if your income, rent expense, or household composition changes. You can request a restoration of your FHEPS grant if it ended within the last 12 months and your family is still eligible for FHEPS.
You can get the locations, hours and phone numbers of Benefits Access Centers in your area. All Centers are accessible for people who use wheelchairs. [Find a Benefits Access Center.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/locations/job-locations-and-service-centers.page)

title: Flood Insurance and Flood Risk Assessment
body:
Need something else? [Hurricane Preparedness](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02810) to find the Hurricane Evacuation Zone of a particular address Flood insurance is required if you live in the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) defined floodplain and have a federally-backed mortgage. Flood insurance is not included in regular homeowners insurance, but anyone can purchase flood insurance, whether or not their homes were affected by Hurricane Sandy or are in the FEMA 100-year floodplain. [Learn more about flood insurance.](https://www.floodsmart.gov)
Agency: Federal Emergency Management Agency
Division: National Flood Insurance Program
Phone Number: (800) 427-4661
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Maps
FEMA's Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs) identify areas that are at risk of flooding. These maps are tied to the City's Building Code, which establishes safe construction standards for building in the floodplain. Property owners can use these maps to determine their flood insurance requirements.   You can determine if your structure is in the floodplain. You can also look up your specific preliminary Base Flood Elevation (BFE) and flood zone by address. [Learn about Flood Insurance Rate Maps and find out if you are located in the floodplain.](http://www.region2coastal.com/) NYC Property Owner Notification Letters FEMA sent letters to New York City residents living in or near the FEMA Preliminary Flood Insurance Rate Map flood zones. The letter advises residents to understand the flood risk and to purchase flood insurance if necessary. If you have received a letter, you should first check whether or not you are in a flood zone.  If you have a mortgage and are not in a high-risk flood zone, you are not required to buy flood insurance. You can still purchase flood insurance if you prefer. If you are in a flood zone, you can get more information on flood insurance requirements from FEMA. [Get information on flood insurance and your flood risk.](https://www.floodhelpny.org/) Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) Update FEMA has updated their Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs) to identify areas that are at risk of flooding. Flood risk is assessed in 3 ways:   Floodplain:  A 100-year floodplain is the area that has a 1% chance of coastal flooding each year. A 500-year floodplain is the area that has a 0.2% chance of coastal flooding each year.  A Riverine is the area near a stream or river that is at risk of flooding.   Flood Zones:  For New York City, there are five zones. You can find detailed information on the different zones on the FEMA website. Base Flood Elevation (BFE): A BFE is the elevation to which the 100-year flood event is expected to rise.  [Visit FEMA's Flood Map Service Center website.](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home) FEMA FIRMs Technical Appeal The Comments and Appeals Period for the City ended on June 28, 2015. The City has filed a technical appeal of the Preliminary FIRMs. [Learn more about the FIRM appeals.](http://www.region2coastal.com/appeal/) [Visit the NYC Flood Maps website.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/floodmaps/index.page) Department of Buildings (DOB) Offices to Review FIRMs FIRMs can be viewed in person at the DOB office in your borough:
Walk-in hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 12 PM. DOB Bronx Borough Office 1775 Grand Concourse, 5th Floor (between East 175 Street and Walton Avenue) Bronx, NY 10453 DOB Brooklyn Borough Office 345 Adams Street, 3rd Floor (between Willoughby and Johnson Streets) Brooklyn, NY 11201 DOB Manhattan Borough Office 280 Broadway, 3rd Floor (between Chambers and Reade Streets) New York, NY 10007 DOB Queens Borough Office 120-55 Queens Boulevard (between 80th Road and 82nd Avenue) Kew Gardens, NY 11424 DOB Staten Island Borough Office 10 Richmond Terrace, Borough Hall, 2nd Floor (between Staten Island Ferry Terminal and Nick LaPorte Place) Staten Island, NY 10301
Further Assistance You can contact a Map Expert for more information and assistance.
Agency: Federal Emergency Management Agency
Division: Map Service Center
Phone Number: (877) 336-2627
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available through the automated phone system during business hours.
FloodHelpNY Flood Risk Assessment and Insurance Assistance
Homeowners throughout New York City’s flood-prone neighborhoods may be impacted by rising sea levels and flood insurance rates. The Center for NYC Neighborhoods (CNYCN) can help homeowners: Understand your flood risk through the free web platform FloodHelpNY.org  Understand potential solutions to reduce or mitigate your flood risk — examples include elevating your home, elevating your mechanicals, installing flood vents, and basement infill. Understand your flood insurance rates and potential changes to your policy in the future. Learn about an “elevation certificate,” a key document that can help you lower your insurance rate. Provide you with a referral to free housing and legal counseling for help with other homeownership questions.  Determine if you are eligible for the Backwater Valve Installation program, available for qualifying neighborhoods to help prevent storm-related sewer backup. Online [Learn more about FloodHelpNY.](https://www.floodhelpny.org/) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: Fingerprinting
body:
If you need fingerprinting for a specific application or situation, you can get fingerprinted by the New York Police Department, for a fee. First, make sure you understand the requirements you must meet. Then, you must schedule an appointment. Walk-ins are not  accepted. Only individuals with appointments may visit One Police Plaza. Appointments can be scheduled online. [Schedule an appointment.](https://appointments.nypdonline.org/) Make sure to bring required documentation and payment to your appointment. [Learn about getting non-criminal fingerprinting.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/services/law-enforcement/record-requests.page) Required Documentation Documents must be original. No document photocopies, pictures of documents or laminated documents will be accepted. All documents must be intact.  Bring one of the following: Valid driver's license with photo; DMV photo identification card (issued in the US); IDNYC (New York City identification card); Valid Passport; Alien Registration Card; Employment Authorization card; or Certificate of Naturalization. Fee The first fingerprint card costs $25, and each additional card costs $1. You can pay by check or money order made out to the New York Police Department. Major credit cards are also accepted at One Police Plaza.
Center-Based Day Cares and Pre-Schools
If you want to work at child care, home care, or family care facilities, including those entities that are under contract with the City of New York, you must first be fingerprinted. You must be screened for criminal convictions and/or pending criminal actions. All prospective hires must have their fingerprints checked against New York State and Federal criminal records databases. Notifications of arrests in New York State are provided on an ongoing basis for all active employees. Appointments Fingerprinting for child care staff is conducted on behalf of DOI and NYC Health Department at IdentoGO centers (operated by IDEMIA). IdentoGO centers are located throughout the five boroughs as well as outside New York City.  Applicants must schedule an appointment to be fingerprinted at IdentoGO. Walk-in service is not available.  Specific location information and service hours are available online.  [Visit the IdentoGO website.](https://uenroll.identogo.com/) Required Documents You must bring: Fully completed application, which must be obtained from your employer or program. The application must have your original signature along with the Permit number of the organization for which you will be working. Photo identification from the following list: Driver's license or non-driver ID Student ID Naturalization or Green Card U.S. Passport Cash Assistance card Other Government-issued ID Processing fee Processing Fee The processing fee is $101.75.  The fee can be paid for by: Credit card (MasterCard, American Express, VISA or Discover). If you choose to pay with a credit or debit card, you will be charged a fee of 2% of the payment. Postal Money Order from the U.S. Post Office, made payable to IdentoGo. Other types of money orders will not be accepted. Results Fingerprint results will not be sent to the child care program. You and your employer will receive a letter notifying you if you can work once your fingerprint and all other Comprehensive Background Check requirements are met. If you need more assistance, send an email to [childcareinfo@health.nyc.gov](mailto:childcareinfo@health.nyc.gov).
Home-Based or After-School Child Care Sites
New York State law requires fingerprinting of all providers, assistants, and household members over the age of 18 in home-based day care and all staff and volunteers in after-school child care as part of the license application process. Fingerprinting is provided by appointment. You can find instructions for making an appointment in the "Request for NYS Fingerprinting Services Info Form" (Form OCFS-4930) in the New York State Day Care License Application booklet. [Download the OCFS-4390 form.](https://ocfs.ny.gov/main/childcare/live_scan.asp)

title: Fire or Ambulance Report
body:
The Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) provides the public with access to certain agency records in compliance with City, State, and Federal laws. You can request a: Fire Incident Report that shows the details of a response to a fire or other emergency incident at a particular location. Pre-Hospital Care Report that shows the details of a patient’s treatment and/or emergency transportation.
Fire Incident Reports
The FDNY creates reports on its response to fire and other emergency incidents (including non-fire emergencies) occurring within the five boroughs of New York City. The FDNY does not maintain records for incidents occurring outside of NYC. You can obtain a copy of a Fire Incident Report online. [Request a Fire Incident Report through NYC OpenRecords.](https://a860-openrecords.nyc.gov/)
Pre-Hospital Care Reports
Patients who were treated or transported by the FDNY Bureau of Emergency Medical Services (FDNY EMS) may request a copy of their Pre-Hospital Care Report (PCR). These records were previously known as the Ambulance Call Report (ACR). The FDNY only maintains Pre-Hospital Care Reports for patients treated or transported by FDNY EMS. For all other patient records, contact the responding ambulance provider or receiving hospital. If an invoice was issued for emergency transportation, it will list the name of the ambulance provider. If the provider was not the FDNY, you will need to contact the listed provider. [Learn how to request a copy of your Pre-Hospital Care Report.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fdny/about/resources/record-requests/records-request.page) [Learn how to request a copy of your FDNY EMS bill.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/fdny/downloads/pdf/about/ambulance-billing-notice.pdf)

title: Fire Premiums Tax
body:
Need something else? [Business Tax Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02602) for help with payment issues, copies of filed returns, audits, and notices of unpaid taxes. Any insurance company incorporated under laws of any jurisdiction other than New York State has to pay tax on fire insurance they write for New York City property. This tax is also known as the Foreign or Alien Insurers Tax or the Foreign Fire Tax.
Filing and Paying
You must use the NYC-FP form (Annual Report of Fire Premiums Tax Upon Foreign and Alien Insurers) to file this tax. [Get the NYC-FP form.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/finance/downloads/pdf/25pdf/business_tax_forms/nyc-fp_2025.pdf) No Payment Required If no payment is required and you are only submitting a return, mail NYC-FP form to: NYC Department of Finance P.O. Box 5564 Binghamton, NY 13902-5564 Payment Required If you are required to submit payment, you can submit payment online or by mail: Online [Access Business Tax e-Services.](http://nyc.gov/eservices) By Mail [Get the NYC-200V form.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/finance/downloads/pdf/17pdf/business_tax_forms/nyc-200v_2017.pdf) Mail Payment and Form NYC-200V ONLY to: NYC Department of Finance P.O. Box 3933 New York, NY 10008-3933
Deadline
The tax is due by March 1st for the recently completed year.
Interest Rates
If you don't file your return or pay the tax by the deadline, or if you overpay, you will be charged interest. From April 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026, the current interest rates are: 10% for underpayments 5% for taxes that remain or become overpaid
Refunds
You can request a refund for overpayment of the Fire Premium Tax. You must use the NYC-FP form to file an amended return. The Department of Finance has 90 days from the due date, extended due date, or filing date (whichever is later) to issue a refund without interest. [Get the NYC-FP form.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/taxes/business-forms/business-forms-additional.page)
Ways to Get Help
You can get answers to questions about the tax or help with filing and paying. By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: Fire Safety Director On-Site Test
body:
A candidate's supervisor must make the request to schedule an on-site Fire Safety Director test. Candidates cannot schedule their own test. The supervisor can make the request online. All requests for Fire Life Safety Director (FLSD) Onsite Exams must be submitted on the [FDNY Business](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fdny/business/support/fdny-business.page) website. [Learn more about Fire Life Safety Director (FLSD) Onsite Exams.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/fdny/downloads/pdf/business/flsd-user-guide.pdf) Supervisor Requirements Before requesting an on-site exam, the supervisor must: Ensure the candidate is qualified by the Certification Unit Ensure the building has a Fire Safety and Evacuation Plan on file with FDNY Candidate Requirements To qualify for the Fire Safety Director on-site test, the candidate must: Pass the Fire Safety Director computer exam Pass a 20-hour certified Fire Safety Director course Receive a Certificate of Completion Once all information is verified and qualified by the Certificate of Fitness Unit, the candidate has 1 year to take the on-site exam.
Emergency Overtime Test
In the case of hardship, you can schedule an emergency overtime test Monday to Friday after 4 PM. The licensed master fire suppression contractor must make this request in writing. The City will bill the contractor for the additional overtime expense.
Cancel a Test
All requests for cancellations must be submitted via email at least 72 hours before the scheduled exam time. Please note "Request for On-Site Exam Cancellation" in the subject of the email. The email should also include the candidate's name, social security number, exam date, and premises address. This information will help expedite the cancellation. To request a cancellation, send an email to [High-Rise@fdny.nyc.gov](mailto:High-Rise@fdny.nyc.gov).

title: Flu Shot and Prevention
body:
Need something else? [School Immunization Requirements](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02979) for requirements for children 5 and older [Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03608) The NYC Health Department recommends that everyone 6 months and older get a flu shot as soon as possible. This is especially important for people considered at high risk for flu complications. People at high risk for flu include: Children between 6 months and 5 years old People 50 years and older Pregnant people (any trimester) People with ongoing medical conditions, such as asthma, diabetes, or heart disease To avoid getting or spreading flu, also known as influenza, you should also: Cover your coughs or sneezes using your sleeve or a tissue (not your bare hand). Wash your hands often with soap and water, especially after coughing or sneezing. Alcohol-based hand cleaners are also effective.  Try to avoid close contact with sick people.  Limit your contact with other people if you are running a fever with a cough or sore throat, and stay home from school or work for 24 hours after your fever is gone. [Get more information and resources about flu prevention.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/flu-seasonal.page)
Flu Shot Locations
Flu (influenza) is a seasonal upper airway and lung infection that causes fever and a cough or sore throat. It is most common during the fall and winter months between September through May. The flu vaccine is widely available throughout the City during flu season. You can find vaccine sites online, by text, or by phone. You can also: Visit your health care provider or an NYC Health + Hospitals clinic. Check nearby locations, such as pharmacies. Pharmacies may vaccinate adults and children as young as 2 years of age. Most health insurance plans cover flu vaccination without a copay. If you don't have insurance, you may be able to get the vaccine for free or low-cost, including at NYC H+H sites. Before you go, contact individual sites for more information about accepted insurance plans and payment options. Online [Find flu vaccine locations.](https://vaccinefinder.nyc.gov/)
By Text Text 55676 and type "flu" for English or "gripe" for Spanish to find a place to get a flu shot. By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Flu Shot Requirement for Preschools and Child Care Centers
As of December 31, 2014, all children under the age of 5 years (6-59 months) are required to receive the flu shot if they attend a New York City regulated preschool or child care center. The NYC Health Department is mandating the flu shot to address the high number of deaths in young children due to complications from the flu. Your child may not be allowed to attend school either in person or remotely if they have not received the flu vaccine.  You may be able to get a medical exemption if your child has a health condition where the vaccine may be harmful. Contact your child’s school or program to find out what is needed for this exemption. At this time, religious exemptions are not permitted for mandated vaccines.

title: Food Allergy Poster
body:
Food establishments must display the Food Allergy Poster if it has seating for customers. The poster tells employees how to protect customers from food allergies. Symptoms of an Allergic Reaction
The symptoms of an allergic response to a food allergen may include the following:  Hives Itching Swelling of the eyelids, face, lips, and tongue Runny nose Abdominal cramps Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea Hoarse voice Difficulty breathing Anaphylaxis Death If you are experiencing these symptoms, you should contact your doctor.

Need something else? [Become a Food Provider](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01133) You can get free food from a food pantry or soup kitchen. Food pantries give you groceries to use at home. Packages include canned goods and other non-perishable food items. You would be given enough food to make more than one meal per person. Soup kitchens serve meals at community centers. Mobile soup kitchens serve meals from vans. Each person gets one meal.
[Find a food provider.](https://finder.nyc.gov/foodhelp/) Call the food pantry or soup kitchen first to confirm their hours before visiting.
More Resources Visit the [Food Resources](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03304) page to learn about other emergency food options.
Complaints
You can report a problem with a food pantry.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: Food Protection Course
body:
You need a food protection certificate to manage a food service business or non-retail food processing business. To get the certificate, you must take the Food Protection Course and pass an exam. [Learn about the Food Protection Course.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/business/food-operators/training.page)
Mobile Vendor Course
You must take the Food Protection Course for Mobile Vendors to apply for a Mobile Food Vendor License. The course takes eight hours to complete and is given over two days. Each session is four hours long. The course is offered in English and Bangla. After you complete the course and pass the final exam, you will get a certificate to show that you have met the Health Code requirement. You will also be issued your Mobile Food Vendor license. Class Location Health Academy The Riverside Health Center, 3rd floor 160 West 100th Street (near Columbus Avenue) Cost The course, including final exam, costs $53. Anyone registering for this course must also apply for and pay separately for a Mobile Food Vendor License at the same time. The cost of the license is $50. Schedule This is an eight-hour class, held over two days. Class meets for four hours each day. Most weeks, there are two classes conducted in English. One on Tuesdays and Wednesdays and another on Thursdays and Fridays. The schedule for the Bangla class varies. How to Register You can register and pay in person at the Citywide Licensing Center. Citywide Licensing Center 42 Broadway New York, NY 10004 Appointments are required. Email [LicensingAppointments@dcwp.nyc.gov](mailto:LicensingAppointments@dcwp.nyc.gov) Call (212) 436-0441 (Monday - Friday, 8 AM - 4 PM) You can pay with: Master Card (debit and credit) Visa (debit and credit) American Express Discover Card Certified check Money order
Mobile Food Vending Renewal Course
Licensed mobile food vendors must take an online refresher course in food protection and safe operating practices and pass a final exam every four years to maintain their license.  The course takes approximately 15 minutes to complete and is free. Registration is required.  [Take the Mobile Food Vending Refresher Course.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/business/health-academy/food-protection-for-mobile-vendors-renewal.page)
Food Establishment Online Course
You can take the Food Protection Course for food establishments online. The online course satisfies the same requirements as the classroom course. The course has 15 lessons. Each lesson takes about one hour to complete. You can take the course in English, Spanish, and Chinese. A study guide is available in 36 languages. The online course is free, but there is a fee for the final exam. [Learn more and take the course.](https://a816-healthpsi.nyc.gov/prjFPC/F2300_Default.aspx) Final Exam To get a food protection certificate, you must pass the final exam. After you complete the online course, you will be told how to schedule and pay for the exam. The cost is $24.60. The exam is offered in 36 languages. You must take the final exam in person at: NYC Health Academy Riverside Health Center 160 West 100th Street, 3rd Floor, Manhattan If you pass, you will get a temporary certificate which shows that you have met the Health Code requirement. The certificate does not expire.
Food Establishment Classroom Course
You can take the Food Protection Course in a classroom setting. The entire course takes 15 hours to complete and is given over five days. Each session is three hours long. The course is offered in English, Spanish, and Bengali. Final exams are given on the last day of the class. If you pass the exam, you will get your food protection certificate that day. Class Location Health Academy The Riverside Health Center, 3rd floor 160 West 100th Street (near Columbus Avenue) Cost The course costs $114.00. Schedule This is a 15-hour course held over five days. Classes usually start on a Monday and end on a Friday. Each session is three hours long. If Monday is a City holiday, classes begin that Tuesday and end on Friday. Each session is three hours and 45 minutes long. How to Register Online You can register and pay for the course online with: Master Card (debit and credit) Visa (debit and credit) American Express Discover Card Electronic check (you must provide your bank routing number and account number) A 2.49% convenience fee will be added to all credit and debit card payments. [Register and pay for the course.](https://a816-healthpsi.nyc.gov/OnlineRegistration/dohmh/DOHMHService) In Person You can register and pay in person at the Citywide Licensing Center. Citywide Licensing Center 42 Broadway New York, NY 10004 Appointments are required. Email [LicensingAppointments@dcwp.nyc.gov](mailto:LicensingAppointments@dcwp.nyc.gov) Call (212) 436-0441 (Monday - Friday, 8 AM - 4 PM) You can pay with: Master Card (debit and credit) Visa (debit and credit) American Express Discover Card Certified check Money order CUNY Schools Offering Course Some CUNY schools also offer the Food Protection Course. These classes satisfy the NYC Health Department requirement for certification in food protection. College of Staten Island Kingsborough Community College Hostos Community College LaGuardia Community College New York City Technical College Queens College York College Contact each school directly for schedule and registration information.
Soup Kitchen and Summer Camp Worker Course
You can get a certificate in food protection to work at or volunteer in a soup kitchen or to serve food at a summer or day camp. The Food Protection Course for soup kitchen and camp workers takes four hours to complete. After completing the course, you will get a card to show that you have met the Health Code requirement. The certificate does not expire. Class Location Health Academy The Riverside Health Center, 3rd floor 160 West 100th Street (near Columbus Avenue) Schedule The course is usually held once a month. More classes are added in the spring and summer. How to Register Online [Register for the course.](https://a816-healthpsi.nyc.gov/OnlineRegistration/dohmh/DOHMHService) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Course Certificate Substitution
If you already have a certificate in food protection for restaurants, you may use that certificate to satisfy the mobile food vending license requirement for a certificate in food protection. You must present that certificate at the time you apply for a Mobile Food Vendor License.
Get Help
You can get help by phone if you have questions about: Payments Refunds Rescheduling a class Status of temporary certificate and license surrendering Using the online registration system
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Login or Password Forgotten If you've forgotten your login or password, click on the "Forgot My Password" link on the Food Protection Course Welcome page. Your user ID and password will be sent to your email address.

title: Food Protection Certificate Replacement
body:
If you have lost or damaged your Food Protection Certificate, you may get a replacement if you have taken the Food Protection Course and passed the final exam within the last 10 years. If you took the class more than 10 years ago you must retake the course and pass the final exam. All replacements are obtained in person at the Health Academy. Appointments and payment online are required. Appointments are available Wednesday and Thursday between 10 AM and 4 PM. You can pay online with the following: Master Card (debit and credit) Visa (debit and credit) American Express Discover Card Electronic check (you must provide your bank routing number and account number) The cost is $16. The Health Academy is located at: The Riverside Health Center 160 West 100 Street, Room 203 New York, NY 10025 Online [Pay and schedule an appointment to replace your food protection certificate.](https://a816-healthpsi.nyc.gov/OnlineRegistration/dohmh/DOHMHService.action) By Phone

title: Freelance Worker and Hiring Party Assistance
body:
Freelance workers and hiring parties in New York City can contact the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) about: Legal rights for freelance workers Legal responsibilities for employers and hiring parties Complaint about a hiring party, including no written contract, nonpayment or late payment, and retaliation Court Navigation Program, including resources for freelance workers You can get more information and assistance from DCWP. Online [Ask a question about the Freelance Isn't Free Act.](https://a866-dcwpbp.nyc.gov/worker-complaint/ask-question?topic=freelancer) By Phone A DCWP representative can answer questions during regular business hours.
Agency: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
Division: Office of Labor Policy and Standards
Phone Number: (212) 436-0380
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Phone assistance is available, but some calls may go straight to voice mail. Please leave a detailed message and a representative will contact you. As an alternative, visit nyc.gov/workers.
Freelance Isn't Free Act
The City’s Freelance Isn’t Free Act, which became law on May 15, 2017, creates new rights, remedies, and resources for freelance workers in New York City to help ensure they are paid on time and in full. The Freelance Isn’t Free Act: Requires contracts between freelance workers and hiring parties that are worth $800 or more to be in writing. Prohibits hiring parties from paying workers late or underpaying workers. Protects freelance workers against retaliation for asserting their rights under the Law. [Get more information about the Freelance Isn’t Free Act.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/about/freelance-isnt-free-act.page)
Office of Labor Policy and Standards
DCWP’s Office of Labor Policy and Standards (OLPS) assists with issues that impact immigrants, people of color, and women in the workplace. In addition, OLPS: Enforces key municipal workplace laws Conducts original research, outreach, and education Develops policies that are responsive to New York City’s evolving economy and workforce [Learn more about the Office of Labor Policy and Standards.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/about/office-of-labor-policy-standards.page)
Splashlight Settlement
The Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) reached a settlement with Splashlight, a creative production company, over violations of NYC's Freelance Isn't Free Act. Under the settlement, Splashlight must pay restitution to 350 freelancers named in the settlement. If you are named in the settlement, DCWP will contact you on how to get payment. If you have any questions regarding your payment or need to change an address, reach out to DCWP by emailing [dcwp@noticeadministrator.com](mailto:dcwp@noticeadministrator.com).

title: Friendly Visiting Program for Older Adults
body:
The Department for the Aging, in partnership with Citymeals on Wheels, offers a Friendly Visiting Program specifically for older adults age 60 and older who have difficulty leaving their homes. The program matches older adults with a volunteer who will visit them at home on a regular basis. This gives both participants a chance to share: Interests Ideas Opinions Experiences You can contact a Case Management agency to sign up.

title: Fuel Truck Inspection
body:
The Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) inspects home heating oil delivery trucks to confirm the accuracy of the truck’s meters and air eliminator devices to ensure that consumers are not charged for oil they did not receive. After an inspection, DCWP places an official seal on the meter and a sticker on the back of the truck to indicate it passed inspection. Businesses can schedule a fuel truck inspection. Online [Request a fuel truck inspection.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/businesses/licenses.page) By Fax (646) 500-5918 By Mail DCWP Bureau of Weights and Measures Testing Station  245 Meserole Avenue  Brooklyn, NY 11222

title: Historic Birth, Death, or Marriage Record
body:
Need something else? [Birth Certificate Order](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01012) from 1910 to the present [Death Certificate Order](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01028) from 1951 to the present [Marriage Record](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01030) from 1950 to the present Historical Vital Records of NYC, as part of the Municipal Archives, provides access to millions of digitized birth, death and marriage records dating from 1855 to 1950 within the five boroughs of New York City. You can search, browse, download or order certified copies from the Municipal Archives’ vital records collection, including: Birth certificates (before 1910) Death certificates (before 1951) Marriage records (before 1950) Online [Search Historical Vital Records of NYC.](https://a860-historicalvitalrecords.nyc.gov/) In Person Appointments are strongly encouraged. [Learn more about scheduling an appointment with the Municipal Archives.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/records/about/frequently-asked-questions-new.page) By Email [familyhistory@records.nyc.gov](mailto:familyhistory@records.nyc.gov) for family history research
Order a Certificate
You can order vital records, letters of exemplification, and No Amendment/Correction letters online or by mail. The cost of each certified copy of a vital record is $18. Letters of exemplification and No Amendment/Correction letters are $12 per copy. If you require a certified copy of a historic vital record, please submit an order and choose mail delivery.   Online You can place an order and make a payment with your credit or debit card, or by e-check. There is a nonrefundable service fee of $3.50 when using a credit or debit card. [Order a copy of a historical vital record.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/records/historical-records/order.page) By Mail You can submit an application by mail. You can pay by check or money order made payable to NYC Department of Records and Information Services. Mail your application and payment to: 31 Chambers Street, Room 103  New York, NY 10007 The application form is available online. [Download the application for a certified copy of a Vital Record.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/records/pdf/New-mail-order-form-2022.pdf) You can also request an application be mailed to you.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to request a copy.
Processing Times
The current processing time is: 1-2 weeks for non-certified PDF copies 8-10 weeks for certified copies If you ordered multiple certificates, they may have different processing times and may be mailed separately.
Vital Record Not Found
You will receive a "Not Found" letter if the Municipal Archives was unable to find the record you requested. Please note that the fee paid is for the search and issuance of search results and will not be refunded even if the search result is “Not Found”. Birth Certificate Not Found Approximately 25 percent of all births prior to 1910 were not reported to New York City.  Church records or the federal and state censuses are alternative resources. The federal census is available from the National Archives. [Find Federal Census data on the National Archives' website.](https://www.archives.gov/research/census)
Further Assistance
You can get answers to frequently asked questions online. You can also send an email to the Department of Records and Information Services if you have questions about refunds or credit card processing errors. [View answers to frequently asked questions.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/records/about/frequently-asked-questions-new.page)

title: GED and Literacy
body:

[CUNY Prep](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02110) for GED Services for children under the age of 18 Effective January 2022, New York State selected the General Educational Development (GED) Test to replace the Test Assessing Secondary Completion (TASC) Test as the primary pathway to a High School Equivalency (HSE) Diploma for students who left high school without graduating.  You can get information about: Applications Test results Eligibility requirements Disability options Diploma verification Duplicate diplomas Testing schedules Status of mailed documents Online [Get information about the GED.](https://www.acces.nysed.gov/hse/ready-set-test-new-high-school-equivalency-exam-here) By Phone
Agency: New York State Education Department

Non-English Speaker Literacy
Training programs for adults and out-of-school youth are offered by community-based organizations throughout the City. Instruction is provided to adults and to out-of-school youth who have limited reading, writing, mathematics, or English skills. Programs include basic education, preparation for GED, and English for speakers of other languages.
