title: Child Proof Stove Knob Covers Complaint
body:
Need something else? [Apartment Maintenance Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01074) to report a broken or missing stove control knob Per Local Law 117 of 2018 and Local Law 44 of 2022, property owners of rental apartments with gas powered stoves are required to: Notify tenants about the availability of stove knob safety devices and Provide stove knob safety devices for apartments where a child under 6 years of age lives at the request of the tenant. Types of safety devices include: Removable stove knob covers (which go over the existing stove knob) Permanent stove safety knobs with integrated locking mechanisms Tenants in apartments without a child under 6 living there may also request covers.   If you want child proof stove knob covers, you should respond to the owner's notification or write to the owner at any time to request them, and the landlord or super must provide them. You do not have to give a reason for your request. You or someone on your behalf can make a complaint that your landlord or building manager refused to provide child proof stove knob covers. You must provide your contact information.
Report that child proof stove knob covers have not been provided.
Tenant Request
Owners must provide child proof stove knob safety devices (either temporary or permanent as requested by the tenant) when a tenant requests them, regardless of whether a child under 6 years of age lives in the apartment.

title: Legal Assistance and Inquiries for Older Adults
body:
Need something else? title: CityFHEPS Rental Assistance
body:
Need something else? [HRA Rental Assistance Programs for Landlords](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01578) to get assistance with CityFHEPS if you are a landlord [Discrimination](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01783) to report housing discrimination CityFHEPS is a program that can help you find and pay for permanent housing if you are eligible. Eligible candidates include: Low-income families who live in shelters Individual adults who live in shelters   Low-income families and adults who are at risk of becoming homeless If you live in a shelter, you can get help finding out if you are eligible for a CityFHEPS subsidy from your case manager or housing specialist.  If you live in the community, you can go to a Homebase location to be screened for CityFHEPS subsidy eligibility. [Learn more about CityFHEPS.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/cityfheps.page)
Eligibility
Eligibility for a CityFHEPS subsidy includes a range of requirements. [Get answers to frequently asked questions about CityFHEPS.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/cityfheps.page) Currently in a Shelter If you live in a shelter, the details will be discussed when you meet with your case manager or housing specialist.  At Risk of Becoming Homeless If you are at risk of becoming homeless, a Homebase counselor will review the eligibility details with you. Most offices are open Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM. Please contact the specific site before your visit to confirm their office hours. Offices will work to accommodate schedule needs, when possible.
[Find a Homebase location.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/homebase-locations.page)
Request a Modification
If your income has changed or your CityFHEPS rent has increased, you can apply for a modification to your CityFHEPS subsidy.   A fillable version of the CityFHEPS Modification Request form is available online.  You will be asked to submit supporting documents with your form.  If you need help completing the form, please contact your local Homebase office.  [Get the online form, which is found in the Additional Documents for Tenants section.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/cityfheps-documents.page) Online Use the [ACCESS HRA Mobile App](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page) from anywhere and at any time to submit images of your completed modification request form. By Email Send your form and supporting documents to [CityFHEPSRenewals@hra.nyc.gov](mailto:CityFHEPSRenewals@hra.nyc.gov). By Mail Mail your form and copies of your supporting documents to: Rental Assistance Program Unit 109 East 16th Street, 1st Floor, Room 102 New York, NY 10003 Further Assistance If you need help completing the form, contact your local Homebase office.
[Find a Homebase location.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/homebase-locations.page)
You can also get more information by phone.
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.
Renewal Process
Your CityFHEPS subsidy must be renewed annually.  The renewal application is mailed to you five months before the end of your CityFHEPS subsidy year.   You can submit your completed and signed renewal application by email or postal mail.  Please be sure to submit supporting documents with your renewal application. [Get the online form and view frequently asked questions in the Additional Documents for Tenants section.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/cityfheps-documents.page) Online Use the [ACCESS HRA website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/) from anywhere and at any time to renew your CityFHEPS. You can submit your renewal when the "Renew" button is shown. You can submit any documents using the document upload feature on the [ACCESS HRA Mobile App](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page). By Email Send your renewal application and supporting documents to [CityFHEPSRenewals@hra.nyc.gov](mailto:CityFHEPSRenewals@hra.nyc.gov). By Mail Mail your renewal application and copies of your supporting documents to: CityFHEPS NYC Human Resources Administration 109 East 16th Street, 10th Floor New York, NY 10003 In Person You can drop off your CityFHEPS renewal application Monday through Friday from 8:30 AM to 5 PM, except on City holidays. title: Paternity Test
body:
The Human Resources Administration offers [low-cost DNA testing](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hra/downloads/pdf/services/child_support/dna_testing.pdf) for parents seeking to determine the correct parenthood of their child. The cost is $45 per person.  You will be referred to a state-certified laboratory. A swab is used to take DNA samples from inside the cheeks of the baby and both parents; the test is quick and painless. You do not have to go to the lab the same day as the other parent. If you are under age 18, the laboratory may require you to have one of your parents accompany you. Results will be sent to you by mail about 2 weeks after the lab receives all 3 samples. Testing is only for biological parents and their minor(s). Testing is not intended for adults seeking to determine their paternity for living/deceased parent(s) or sibling(s). You can schedule an appointment or get more information by email or phone. By Email [dcse.cseweb@dfa.state.ny.us](mailto:dcse.cseweb@dfa.state.ny.us) Please put "DNA Test" in the subject line of your email. Include your full name, child support case ID (if you have one), and date of birth in the body of the email. By Phone
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Division: Paternity Services
Phone Number: (929) 221-5008
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM

title: Off-Hour Delivery Program
body:
Need something else? [Noise from Vehicle](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01102) to report a vehicle making noise that is not a part of the Off-Hour Delivery program. The Department of Transportation (DOT) expanded the Off-Hour Deliveries program, which encourages businesses in congested areas of the city to accept deliveries between 7 PM and 6 AM.  The areas currently participating in the program are: Downtown Brooklyn Lower Manhattan Midtown Manhattan Jamaica, Queens The program aims to reduce traffic congestion in areas with high pedestrian volumes and limited curb space. Carriers and receivers also benefit from: Reduced transit time Reduced fuel and delivery costs Less difficulty with parking More predictable delivery windows [Learn more about the Off-Hour Deliveries program.](https://ohdnyc.com/)
Noise Complaints
You can report delivery trucks and vans in the Off-Hour Deliveries (OHD) program that are making noise between 7 PM and 6 AM. You must make your report by phone. What You Can Report You can report noise from: Trucks idling Refrigeration truck units Loud back up alarms Truck gates slamming Forklifts Drivers talking or playing loud music The trucks or vans must participate in Off-Hour Deliveries and be making noise in an OHD program area. What You Need You must provide: The delivery company's name or a description of a logo or other identifying marks on the truck A description of the truck's location (for example, in a loading dock or double parked on street) Name or address of the business receiving the delivery
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to report the problem.

title: Fair Fares NYC
body:
Need something else? [Manage Your Fair Fares NYC Discount](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03183) [Fair Fares NYC Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03182) [Buses and Subways](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01014) to replace a Reduced-Fare card Fair Fares NYC helps eligible New Yorkers with low incomes manage their transportation costs by providing them with either a 50% discount on approved NYC transit systems or a 50% discount on Access-A-Ride paratransit trips. Fair Fares NYC participants are enrolled in the program for one year before a renewal must be submitted. [Get answers to frequently asked questions about Fair Fares NYC.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fairfares/faq/faq.page) Managing Your Fair Fares Discount Visit the [Manage Your Fair Fares NYC Discount](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03183) page to learn about: Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card replacements and balance transfers Changing the payment method for your Fair Fares NYC subway and bus discount Changing to an Access-A-Ride discount  Canceling a Fair Fares NYC discount  Refunds for certain Fair Fares NYC MetroCards Help with expired cards
Eligibility
If you are a New York City resident, you may be eligible for a Fair Fares NYC discount if you: Are between (and including) the ages of 18 and 64, and Are in a household that meets the income guidelines listed below: Persons in Household Maximum Annual Income 1 $23,940 2 $32,460 3 $40,980 4 $49,500 5 $58,020 6 $66,540 7 $75,060 8 $83,580 More than 8 Add $8,520 for each additional person Are not receiving (or are not eligible for) full carfare from the Department of Social Services/Human Resources Administration (DSS/HRA) or any other NYC agency, and If choosing the Fair Fares NYC subway and bus discount, are not currently participating or eligible to participate in any other transportation discount program ** ** If choosing the Fair Fares NYC discount for Access-A-Ride trips, you may still be eligible even if you receive a discount (or free rides) on subways and buses from the MTA. Fair Fares NYC will not ask about immigration status or record any information about immigration status. [Check your eligibility and apply for Fair Fares NYC.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fairfares/index.page)
Subway and Bus Discount
If eligible, you can use a Fair Fares NYC subway and bus discount to pay half the current price for a single fare on approved NYC transit systems and use a free transfer after each single fare payment within the NYCT guidelines. The current discount fare on approved NYC transit systems is $1.50. When you use your Fair Fares NYC discount, the OMNY card reader will know to charge you $1.50. If you take 12 paid rides within a consecutive 7-day period and use the same payment method to pay for each individual ride, all additional rides during that timeframe will automatically be free. This is known as the 7-day fare cap. You can use your Fair Fares NYC subway and bus discount for: New York City subways Eligible New York City buses, including local, limited, and Select Bus Service (SBS) The Staten Island Railway (SIR) Roosevelt Island Tramway Hudson Rail Link The Fair Fares NYC subway and bus discount is not available for: Metropolitan Transit Authority (MTA) Express Buses The Long Island Rail Road (LIRR) Port Authority Trans-Hudson (PATH) AirTrain Metro-North Railroad An OMNY card that was issued by Fair Fares NYC can be used to pay the full fare on MTA Express Buses and AirTrain. Choosing a Payment Method When you submit an application or renewal, you will be asked to choose how you want to pay the discounted fare on approved NYC transit systems. You can pay the fare using one of the following payment methods: A Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card A personal OMNY card Credit card or debit card or mobile device If you want to use a personal OMNY card, credit or debit card, or mobile device, you must have the OMNY transit account number associated with that payment method. The Fair Fares NYC program will need that number to ensure that you are charged the discounted fare and not the full fare. [Create an OMNY account.](https://omny.info/register)
Access-A-Ride Discount
MTA Access-A-Ride customers who meet the eligibility requirements for the Fair Fares NYC program can pay half the current price for a single fare on their Access-A-Ride trips. The current discount fare on an Access-A-Ride trip is $1.50. Access-A-Ride drivers only accept cash payment for Access-A-Ride trips. Access-A-Ride customers who already have a reduced fare card through the MTA are still eligible for a Fair Fares NYC discount if they meet the other eligibility criteria and are applying for a discount on their Access-A-Ride trips. If you are not participating in the Fair Fares NYC program and you are an Access-A-Ride customer, visit the [Fair Fares NYC website](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fairfares/index.page) to check your eligibility and apply.
Apply
You can apply for a Fair Fares NYC discount online or in person. The application process has two steps: 1.    Check your [eligibility](https://www.nyc.gov/office-of-the-mayor/fair-fares-nyc.page)and submit the application. 2.    Submit required documents, if any, within 10 calendar days of submitting your application using the [NYC ACCESS HRA mobile app](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page). Your application is not complete until you submit required documents, if any. The Fair Fares NYC application process does not require an eligibility interview. How to Apply You can apply for a Fair Fares NYC discount online. If needed, you can get help completing an application and submitting required documents at a Fair Fares location. Online Use the [ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/fairfares) or [NYC ACCESS HRA mobile app](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page) from anywhere and at any time to apply for Fair Fares NYC. In Person [Find a Fair Fares NYC location.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fairfares/contact-us/contact-us.page) What Happens Next Applications are sent to the program for review and an eligibility decision when you affirm on ACCESS HRA that you submitted all documents for your application or when the 10 calendar day period to submit documents ends, whichever happens first. The review can take up to 30 days.
Renew
You must submit an annual renewal and be found eligible to continue getting your Fair Faires NYC discount. Your [ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/fairfares)account will display reminder messages and you will be mailed a notice when it's time to renew your enrollment. The notice and reminder messages will include your deadline to submit the renewal. You may also receive notifications by text and email if that information is included in your ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC account. Renewals should be submitted as early as possible. If your renewal is submitted timely and approved, your discount will continue without interruption. If you miss your renewal deadline, you will have to submit a new application. Renewal Process The renewal process has two steps: Submit your renewal. Submit required documents, if any, within 10 calendar days of submitting your renewal using the [NYC ACCESS HRA mobile app](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page). The Fair Fares NYC renewal process does not require an eligibility interview. The quickest way to submit your renewal is online. If needed, you can get help completing your renewal and submitting required documents at any Fair Fares NYC location. Online Use the [ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC website](http://www.nyc.gov/accessfairfares) or [NYC ACCESS HRA mobile app](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page) from anywhere and at any time to submit your renewal for Fair Fares NYC. In Person [Find a Fair Fares NYC location.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fairfares/contact-us/contact-us.page) What Happens Next Renewals are sent to the program for review when you confirm on ACCESS HRA that you submitted all documents for your renewal or when the 10 calendar day period to submit documents ends, whichever happens first. The review can take up to 30 days. If your renewal is approved, your enrollment in Fair Fares NYC program will be extended for one year.
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.
Supporting Documentation
You may be asked to provide supporting documentation to verify your identity, age, residency, and income.   If you are required to submit supporting documentation, you must submit the documents within 10 calendar days from the date you submit your application or renewal. If you do not submit the documents within this timeframe, you will have to submit a new application.  Documents can only be submitted through the NYC ACCESS HRA mobile app. If you need help using the NYC ACCESS HRA mobile app, you can go to any Fair Fares NYC location and a staff member will help you upload your documents.  [Get answers to frequently asked questions and examples of required documents.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fairfares/faq/faq.page) Online Using the [NYC ACCESS HRA mobile app](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page), you can upload images from the gallery of your smartphone or tablet or take pictures of your documents and submit them as part of your application. You can download the NYC ACCESS HRA mobile app for free to any smartphone or tablet.   The status of the uploaded document is updated in real time. If the document upload is successful, your ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC account will display “Documents Received” on the Documents page on the ACCESS NYC website or Required Documents page on the NYC ACCESS HRA mobile app. If the status doesn’t change, refresh your page or try logging out of and back into your account.
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.
In Person [Find a Fair Fares NYC location.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fairfares/contact-us/contact-us.page)
Status and Decision
You can view the status of your application or renewal anytime online by logging into your [ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/login) account.  You will be mailed a notice once a decision is made on your application or renewal. You can also see the decision in your ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC account.  Application Approved  If your application is approved, you will be enrolled in the Fair Fares NYC program for one year.  If you selected the subway and bus discount and asked to:   Get a Fair Fares NYC OMNY card, you will receive your card in the mail 2 to 3 weeks after your application is approved. The card cannot be picked up in person.  Use a personal OMNY card, a credit card or debit card, or mobile device as a payment method, you can start using that payment method immediately after your application is approved.  If you selected the Access-A-Ride discount, you will be able to use the discount on Access-a-Ride trips booked starting 3 calendar days after the MTA verifies that you are an Access-a-Ride customer.  Renewal Approved  If your renewal is approved, your enrollment in the Fair Fares NYC program will be extended for one year.  If you have a Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card, you can use it for several enrollment years if you remain eligible for the program. You will only receive a new card in the mail if:   This is the first time you requested a Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card, or  Your current Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card is going to expire (the new card will arrive before your current card expires)  If you use an OMNY card you already have, a credit card or debit card or mobile device as a payment method, the discount will continue automatically when your renewal is approved.  If your discount is for Access-A-Ride trips, it will continue automatically when your renewal is approved.  Application or Renewal Denied  Your application or renewal may be denied if you do not meet the program eligibility requirements. You can log into your [ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/login) account to view the reason for the denial. Fair Fares NYC will also send you a notice if your application or renewal is denied. The notice will explain why you are not eligible for a Fair Fares NYC discount.  If you think the denial was a mistake, you can make a request to review your application or renewal in person at a Fair Fares NYC location or by phone. You must make this request within 14 calendar days from the date on the notice you received. If it has been more that 14 calendar days, please submit a new application.  By Phone

title: Manage Your Fair Fares NYC Discount
body:
Need something else? [Fair Fares NYC](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03181) to apply for or renew [Fair Fares NYC Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03182) [Buses and Subways](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01014) to replace a Reduced-Fare card If you are a Fair Fares NYC participant, you can use your [ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/login) account to:  Report a problem with a Fair Fares NYC issued One Metro New York (OMNY) card   Change your discount payment method for fares on approved NYC transit systems  Update your contact information   Change from a Subway and Bus discount to an Access-A-Ride discount  Change from an Access-A-Ride discount to a Subway and Bus discount  If you have a Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card and there is a problem with your card, it is very important that you report the problem as soon as you notice the issue.   New York City Transit (NYCT) doesn’t issue refunds for the balance that is on an OMNY card. You can only transfer a balance from one OMNY card to another OMNY card. The best way to protect the balance on your card is to link it to a free and secure OMNY account. [Create an OMNY account.](https://omny.info/register) Fair Fares NYC participants who still have a Fair Fares NYC MetroCard may be able to request a refund review in person or by mail.  Renewing Your Discount If you need to renew your Fair Fares NYC discount, visit the [Fair Fares NYC](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03181) page instead.
Report a Problem with a Fair Fares NYC Issued OMNY Card
If your Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card is lost, stolen, damaged, or never received, you must first report the issue before you can request a replacement card or change the payment method you use to pay the Fair Fares NYC Subway and Bus discount fare.  Report a Lost, Stolen, Damaged, or Never Received Fair Fares Issued OMNY Card  You can report the problem with your Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card online, by phone, or in person. Online  Log in to your [ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/login)account. Select the “Report OMNY Card Lost, Stolen, or Damaged” link in the Quick Links section and follow the instructions on the screen. By Phone
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.
In Person [Find a Fair Fares NYC location.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fairfares/contact-us/contact-us.page) Replacement for a Lost, Stolen, Damaged, or Never Received Fair Fares Issued OMNY Card Fair Fares NYC can replace a:  Lost, stolen, or damaged Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card once per enrollment year Fares NYC issued OMNY card that was lost in the mail Once you report the problem, you may: Change the discount payment method you use to pay the Fair Fares NYC subway and bus fare to a personal OMNY card, credit card, debit card, or mobile wallet. If you choose this option, you will need to provide an OMNY transit account number to submit the request.  Have a replacement Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card, if eligible, sent to you by mail. You will receive the card 2 to 3 weeks after you report the problem. It will not have any money on it.  If you have not received the card in the mail after the 3-week mailing period, you can report the card as lost in the mail again and then choose one of the following:  Change the discount payment method to a personal OMNY card, a debit or credit card, or mobile wallet. Get a replacement Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card in person at any Fair Fares NYC location 5 days after you report the problem. Have a replacement Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card mailed to you. If you choose this option, you cannot pick up a Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card in person. The Fair Fares program is not able to issue a card in person if one has been mailed to you. You can check the status of the replacement card or new payment method you chose online or by phone.  Online Log in to your [ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/login) account. Select the “Report OMNY Card Lost, Stolen, or Damaged” link in the Quick Links section and follow the instructions on the screen. By Phone
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.
Change a Discount Payment Method
You can submit a request to change the payment method you use to pay your Fair Fares NYC subway and bus discount fare during your enrollment year. You can only submit a request to change your payment method once in a 24-hour time period. The new payment method will work 24 to 72 hours after you submit the request. If you change your payment method in the middle of a 7-day fare period, the 7-day fare cap period will restart. Any fares that you paid for using your old payment method won’t count towards the 12 paid rides fare cap. If you want to change your payment method to a personal OMNY card, credit or debit card, or mobile device, you must have an OMNY transit account number for that payment method. The Fair Fares NYC program cannot complete the request without that number.  If you have an unexpired Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card, you will be able to make that your payment method again.  The request can be submitted online, by phone, or in person. Online Log in to your [ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/login) account.  Select the “Change OMNY Discount Payment Method” link in the Quick Links section and follow the instructions on the screen. If you don’t already have an OMNY transit account number, you will be able to create one as part of your request. By Phone Before you call, please make sure that you have an OMNY transit account number for the new payment method. You can get an OMNY transit account number by contacting OMNY Customer Service.
Agency: Metropolitan Transportation Authority
Division: OMNY Customer Service
Phone Number: (877) 789-6669
Business Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week
If you do have your OMNY transit account number, you can contact HRA for assistance with changing your payment method.
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.
In Person [Find a Fair Fares NYC location.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fairfares/contact-us/contact-us.page)
Add Money to a Fair Fares NYC Issued OMNY Card
You can use the following payment methods to add money to your Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card: Cash Credit card Debit card Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) Card You can add money to your card online, by phone, or in person. You can also set up automatic reloads in a registered OMNY account.  Online You can sign up for an OMNY account.  This secure account allows you to: Track your progress toward reaching the 7-day fare cap Reload your OMNY card Manage your payment methods Receive account notifications  Instantly freeze your card if it's lost or stolen To link your Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card to your OMNY account, choose the "Add travel card" option on the Wallet screen. [Create or log into your OMNY account.](https://omny.info/register) By Phone You can call the OMNY Customer Service to load money onto your OMNY card.
Agency: Metropolitan Transportation Authority
Division: OMNY Customer Service
Phone Number: (877) 789-6669
Business Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week
In Person You can add money to your OMNY card: At an MTA OMNY card vending machine At [participating retail stores](https://omny.info/retail-locations) across NYC
Fair Fares NYC Issued OMNY Card Balance Transfer
You can transfer money from a lost, stolen, damaged, expired, or expiring Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card to a new Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card or a personal OMNY card. If you don’t have an OMNY account, keep a record of your 18-digit card number, CVV number and expiration date (on the back of your card). This will allow OMNY Customer Service to assist you when you need to contact them. Refunds are not issued for balances that are on an OMNY card that is lost, stolen, damaged, or expired. You can only move the remaining balance to another OMNY card. Fair Fares OMNY Card If you get a new Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card, the balance from your old Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card will automatically move to your new card. Personal OMNY Card If you are going to use a personal OMNY card, you must call OMNY Customer Service to move the balance from your Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card to your personal OMNY card. When you call, you will be asked to provide information about the lost, stolen, damaged, expired, or expiring Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card such as the: Email address or zip code linked to your OMNY account. [Create or log into your OMNY account.](https://omny.info/register). Serial number or OMNY Transit Account Number for your Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card. You can find the Transit Account Number in your [ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/login) account. By Phone
Agency: Metropolitan Transportation Authority
Division: OMNY Customer Service
Phone Number: (877) 789-6669
Business Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week
Expiring Fair Fares Issued OMNY Cards
An OMNY card is valid for several years. If your Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card is expiring in less than 30 days, the Fair Fares NYC program will automatically mail you a new Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card if you are still enrolled in the program. Your balance will automatically move from your old card to your new Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card.
Change to an Access-A-Ride Discount
Fair Fares NYC participants who are also Access-A-Ride customers can submit a request to change their Subway and Bus discount to an Access-A-Ride discount to get 50% off their Access-A-Ride paratransit trips. You will be asked to provide your Access-A-Ride customer identification number when you submit this request. The request can be submitted online, by phone, or in person. The MTA must verify that you are an Access-A-Ride customer before your discount will be applied. Your Fair Fares NYC ACCESS HRA account will display messages on the status of your request. After the MTA confirms your Access-A-Ride customer status, you will receive a notice and, if the MTA has your email on file, an email letting you know that your request has been approved. If you were previously using the Fair Fares NYC subways and bus discount, the payment method for that discount will be deactivated. Online [Log in to your ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC account](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/login). Select the “Update Access-A-Ride Information” link in the Quick Links section and follow the instructions on the screen. By Phone
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.
In Person [Find a Fair Fares NYC location.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fairfares/contact-us/contact-us.page)
Close Your Fair Fares NYC Discount
You may cancel (opt-out) of your Fair Fares NYC discount at any time. You can request to cancel by phone, in-person, or by mail. You cannot make this request online. If you cancel your Fair Fares NYC discount and you have an unexpired Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card, the card will still work but you will be charged a full fare when you use it. By Phone
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.
In Person [Find a Fair Fares NYC location.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fairfares/contact-us/contact-us.page)
By Mail Fair Fares NYC PO Box 7099 New York, NY 10008-7099 Include the following information in the envelope with your request: Your first and last name Fair Fares NYC Client ID/Access-A-Ride ID Number (found on the home page in your ACCESS HRA Fair Fares account) Your OMNY transit account number, if applicable A note requesting to cancel your discount
Fair Fares NYC MetroCards
In November 2025, a Fair Fares NYC issued OMNY card was mailed to all participants who still had a Fair Fares NYC MetroCard and were still eligible for the Fair Fares NYC program. All Fair Fares NYC MetroCards have been deactivated and cannot be used. You can request a refund review if you have a Fair Fares NYC MetroCard that is damaged, expiring, or expired regardless of the payment method that you used to add money to the card. Return Your Fair Fares NYC MetroCard You must return your Fair Fares NYC MetroCard to the Fair Fares NYC program in person or by mail to request a refund review. You cannot make this request over the phone.  You should only request a refund review if you think there is money left on the card. Your request for a refund review must be received within two years of the card’s expiration date. The refund review request will not be processed until your card is received. The Fair Fares NYC program will contact New York City Transit (NYCT) to start the refund review process. You do not need to contact NYCT.
In Person [Find a Fair Fares NYC location.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/fairfares/contact-us/contact-us.page)
By Mail Include the following information in the envelope with your card:  Your first and last name Fair Fares NYC Client ID number (found on the home page in your [ACCESS HRA Fair Fares NYC](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/login) account or a Fair Fares NYC notice that was sent to you) Whether you think there is money left on the card Send your card and the above information to: Fair Fares NYC PO Box 7099 New York, NY 10008-7099 Approved Refunds for a Fair Fares NYC MetroCard NYCT will conduct a review to determine the refund amount, if any, after the Fair Fares NYC program asks them to start the refund review process. The NYCT refund review process can take 6 to 8 weeks.  For approved refunds, NYCT will issue the payment based on how the purchase was made. Purchases made using a credit or EBT card are issued a credit to that same card Purchases made using cash or a debit card are issued as a check and sent to the mailing address on record with the Fair Fares NYC program If you would like to check on the status of a refund review, please call NYCT Customer Service. If your purchase was made using a credit or EBT card, please check your account before you call 511 to request a status update.

Business Hours: Daily: 6 AM - 10 PM
Staff is available through the automated phone system during business hours. Call volume is often high. If you don't get through, call back later.

Fair Fares NYC Locations are open Monday through Friday from 8:30 AM to 5 PM, except city holidays.

title: New York State DREAM Act
body:
The New York State DREAM act lets undocumented students apply for State financial aid and scholarships for higher education. Under this law: Undocumented students can apply for the Tuition Assistance Program (TAP) Undocumented students can access the 529 College Savings Program Anyone who is eligible for financial assistance through the NYS DREAM Act can get information and help with the application process.  [Learn more about the NYS Dream Act.](https://www.hesc.ny.gov/applying-aid/nys-dream-act/) [Learn more about NYS DREAM Act application assistance.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/immigrants/legal-resources/nys-dream-act-application-assistance.page)
DREAM Act and NYS DREAM Act
The NYS DREAM Act helps undocumented students attend and complete college. This legislation does not grant citizenship. Only the federal government can make laws about immigration status.
Federal Financial Aid Programs
The NYS DREAM Act does not impact federal programs like Pell Grants and FAFSA. Only the federal government can make such changes.

title: Gas Leak Notice
body:
Call 911 Call 911 to report natural gas odors or other potential gas leaks.
Need something else? [Essential Service Interruption Notice Not Posted](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01947) to report a residential building owner for not posting a notice before gas service is disrupted Owners of residential buildings are required to post a Notice of Procedure for Tenants Regarding Suspected Gas Leaks with information to advise tenants of the procedure they should follow then they suspect that a gas leak has occurred. The notice must be: Delivered to each tenant and prospective tenant of such dwelling (all tenant-occupied units, including 1- and 2- family homes) with the lease or lease renewal form for such tenant or prospective tenant AND  Posted and maintained in a common area of the building  Failure to post and to provide the appropriate notice can result in a violation being issued. The notice advises tenants that when they suspect that a gas leak has occurred, they should take the following actions:  Quickly open nearby doors and windows and then leave the building immediately; do not attempt to locate the leak. Do not turn on or off any electrical appliances, do not smoke or light matches or lighters, and do not use a house-phone or cell-phone within the building;  After leaving the building, from a safe distance away from the building, call 911 immediately to report the suspected gas leak;  After calling 911, call the gas service provider for this building. Online [Download a sample gas leak notice for suspected gas leaks only.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/services/sample-signage-suspected-gas-leaks.pdf) [Download a sample combined notice for smoke and carbon monoxide detectors and gas leak notice.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/services/sample-notice-combined-suspected-gas-leak-smoke-carbon-monoxide.pdf)

title: Community Cleanup Tool Loan Program
body:
If you're interested in creating a volunteer clean-up project in your neighborhood, you can borrow cleaning supplies and tools from the Department of Sanitation (DSNY). DSNY lends brooms, shovels, and rakes to community groups and block associations for community clean-up projects. You must return the equipment when you are done using it. DSNY also provides volunteers with bags and gloves. After the cleanup, DSNY will collect the bagged debris. If you would like to organize a clean-up event, you must first submit a project plan to DSNY three weeks in advance. The project plan must include: Event location Event date and rain date Number of volunteers Tools needed Once your plan is complete, contact DSNY by email or by phone for further assistance. If you're interested in volunteering for a community clean-up project, you can check [DSNY Events Calendar](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/events/index.page) for upcoming events. By Email [customerservice@dsny.nyc.gov](mailto:customerservice@dsny.nyc.gov). By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: Property Tax Payment Deferral
body:
The Property Tax and Interest Deferral (PT AID) program helps homeowners who are experiencing hardship defer payments for past and future property taxes and avoid the tax lien sale. You may be eligible for a PT AID payment plan if: You own a 1-, 2-, or 3-family home or a condominium unit The property has been your primary residence for one year or more The total income for all owners is $107,300 or less (federal adjusted gross income) DOF offers four different PT AID programs for those who qualify. Each plan offers different payment options, terms, and requirements.
Low-Income Senior Plan (LIS)
Homeowners 65 and older who are experiencing hardship may be eligible for the Low-Income Senior (LIS) plan. Under the plan, you may be able to defer a portion of or all of your property tax payments. Eligibility You're eligible for the plan if: You are 65 or older You have owned a 1-, 2-, or 3-family home or a condominium unit for at least one year You have lived on the property for at least one year The combined income of all owners is $107,300 or less (federal adjusted gross income) Plan Duration You can choose a plan with a fixed period of time or without a fixed period of time. Fixed period of time agreement will end after a certain number of years A plan without a fixed period of time will end when you opt out or no longer qualify If you no longer quality, your unpaid taxes will be due in full. Amount of Deferred Payments If you qualify, your payments for delinquent and future property taxes will be limited to 0% (full deferral), 25%, 50%, or 75% for a fixed period or long-term. You should choose a payment percentage that best fits your budget. The more that tax payments are deferred, the higher the amount you will eventually have to repay. To estimate the amount of each installment payment on the plan, use the [LIS Plan Calculator](https://a836-rpie.nyc.gov/ecicalculator/LowIncomeSenior.cfm).  After you finish calculating the payments, submit and print the payment plan calculator form to use in your application.
You can’t defer payment of: More than 25% of your equity in a tax class 1 (one-, two-, or three-unit residential) property or 50% of equity for condominiums Payments that are required because of any lien sold prior to making your application Water or sewer bills The total amount of deferred tax payments is capped when it equals or exceeds 25% of your equity in a tax class 1 (one-, two-, or three-unit residential) property or 50% of equity for condominiums. A property's equity is the market value of the home minus any mortgages, liens, and other liabilities. The payment of additional taxes and charges can't be deferred if the cap is reached. You may request adjustment of the deferral cap based on increase in market property value.
Fixed-Term Income-Based Plan (FTI)
Low-income homeowners experiencing hardship may be eligible for the Fixed-Term, Income-Based (FTI) plan. Eligibility You're eligible for the plan if: You have owned a 1-, 2-, or 3-family home or a condominium unit for at least one year You have lived on the property for at least one year The combined income of all owners is $107,300 or less (federal adjusted gross income) Plan Duration The term of the plan is calculated by dividing the total amount of income (2%, 4%, 6%, or 8% of AGI) by the monthly or quarterly payment amount. After your plan expires, you must: Pay current charges in full, and Pay delinquent taxes in full or enter into a standard DOF payment agreement within six months Amount of Deferred Payments While you are on the plan, your monthly or quarterly payments for delinquent and projected taxes and charges due will be limited to 2%, 4%, 6%, or 8% of your adjusted gross income (AGI). You should choose a payment percentage that best fits your budget. The more tax payments that are deferred, the higher the amount you will eventually have to repay. To estimate the amount of each installment payment on the plan, use the [FTI Plan Calculator](https://a836-rpie.nyc.gov/ecicalculator/FixTermPlan.cfm). After you finish calculating the payments, submit and print the payment plan calculator form to use in your application.
You can’t defer payment of: More than 25% of your equity in a tax class 1 (one-, two-, or three-unit residential) property or 50% of equity for condominiums Payments that are required because of any lien sold prior to making your application Water or sewer bills The total amount of deferred tax payments is capped when it equals or exceeds 25% of your equity in a tax class 1 (one-, two-, or three-unit residential) property or 50% of equity for condominiums. A property's equity is the market value of the home minus any mortgages, liens, and other liabilities. The payment of additional taxes and charges can't be deferred if the cap is reached. You may request adjustment of the deferral cap based on increase in market property value.
Extenuating Circumstances Plan (ECI)
Homeowners experiencing extenuating circumstances may be eligible the Extenuating Circumstances Income-Based (ECI) plan. Eligibility You're eligible for the plan if: You have owned a 1-, 2-, or 3-family home or a condominium unit for at least one year You have lived on the property for at least one year The combined income of all owners is $107,300 or less (federal adjusted gross income) You meet the definition of having extenuating circumstances Extenuating circumstances involves the loss of income due to death, serious illness, or unemployment of owner or immediate family member, or enrollment in DEP’s Water Debt Assistance Program. You must submit documentation to prove your extenuating circumstance, such as a death certificate, income tax return, or medical document. Plan Duration The term of the plan is for a minimum of one year, but it may be extended if situation persists. After your plan expires, you must: Pay current charges in full and Pay delinquent taxes in full or enter into a standard DOF payment agreement within six months Amount of Deferred Payments While you are on the plan, your monthly or quarterly payments for delinquent and projected taxes and charges due will be limited to 2%, 4%, 6%, or 8% of your adjusted gross income (AGI). You should choose a payment percentage that best fits your budget. The more tax payments that are deferred, the higher the amount you will eventually have to repay. To estimate the amount of each installment payment on the plan, use the [ECI Plan Calculator](https://a836-rpie.nyc.gov/ecicalculator/extenuatingCircumstance.cfm). After you finish calculating the payments, submit and print the payment plan calculator form to use in your application.
You can’t defer payment of: More than 25% of your equity in a tax class 1 (one-, two-, or three-unit residential) property or 50% of equity for condominiums Payments that are required because of any lien sold prior to making your application Water or sewer bills The total amount of deferred tax payments is capped when it equals or exceeds 25% of your equity in a tax class 1 (one-, two-, or three-unit residential) property or 50% of equity for condominiums. A property's equity is the market value of the home minus any mortgages, liens, and other liabilities. The payment of additional taxes and charges can't be deferred if the cap is reached. You may request adjustment of the deferral cap based on increase in market property value.
Circuit Breaker Plan
You may be eligible for a payment plan which limits your annual payment to 10% of your adjusted gross income, or $1,500, whichever is greater. The plan includes property tax charges projected over the full tax year plus any delinquent charges you might owe. Eligibility Your property must be a tax class 1 residential property, or a condominium The property’s assessed value must be $250,000 or less The property must have been your primary residence for at least one year You must have a federal adjusted gross income of $107,300 or less Your most recent quarterly property tax charges must exceed 10% of your quarterly income Visit the [PT AID Payment Terms Estimate](https://a836-rpie.nyc.gov/ecicalculator/CircuitBreakerPlan.cfm) to get an estimate of your payment. [Download the PT AID brochure.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/finance/downloads/pdf/translations/ptaid/ptaid-brochure.pdf) [Learn more about the Property Tax Interest Deferral (PT AID) Program.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/property/pt-aid.page)
PT AID Payment Plan vs. Standard Payment Plan
Like the PT AID payment plans, a standard payment plan allows you to pay overdue property taxes in multiple installments, but because it doesn't take into account your income or ability to pay, your scheduled payments are likely to be higher. Standard plans also don't allow you to defer payments for future property tax bills; you must continue to make payments on your property taxes as they become due. If you currently have a standard payment plan, you may switch to a PT AID plan if you are in good standing and meet the eligibility requirements of the program. To learn more about standard payment plans, visit the [Property Tax Payment Plan](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01248) page.
Apply
To apply, you must choose which plan you want to apply for and submit a completed PT AID application and the required documents online, in person, or by mail. Online [Apply for the PT AID program.](https://a836-pts-efile.nyc.gov/SmartFile/Filing/FilingType/Info/NYC_PTAID_INIT) Documents may be sent as photos or scanned. In Person Bring your completed application and the required documents to a [DOF Business Center](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01015). Paper applications are available at all DOF Business Centers. No appointment is necessary, however you can schedule an appointment to ensure social distancing at the centers. By Mail
Mail to: NYC Department of Finance PT AID Unit 59 Maiden Lane, 19th Floor New York, NY 10038
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Forms
Initial Application You can get a paper application by mail or in person. By Mail
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to request a copy.
In Person
Bronx DOF Business Center 3030 Third Avenue, 2nd Floor (between East 155 and East 156 Streets) Bronx, NY 10455 Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM [Learn more about the Bronx Business Center.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-us-visit-bronx.page)
Brooklyn DOF Business Center 210 Joralemon Street (between Court and Adams Streets) Brooklyn, NY 11201 Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM [Learn more about the Brooklyn Business Center.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-us-visit-brooklyn.page)
Manhattan DOF Business Center 66 John Street (between Dutch and William Streets) New York, NY 10038 Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM [Learn more about the Manhattan Business Center.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-us-visit-manhattan.page)
Queens DOF Business Center 144-06 94th Avenue (between Liverpool Street and Sutphin Boulevard) Jamaica, NY 11435 Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM [Learn more about the Queens Business Center.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-us-visit-queens.page)
Staten Island DOF Business Center 350 St. Marks Place, 1st Floor (between Hyatt Street and Victory Boulevard) Staten Island, NY 10301 Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM [Learn more about the Staten Island Business Center.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-us-visit-statenisland.page)
PT AID Calculator Form You must submit a payment terms calculator form with your application to confirm you know: How the payment plan affects your budget The amount of your installment payment The length of your payment plan To get the form, you must use a PT AID Calculator to answer questions about your property, how much you owe, and how often you want to pay. Use the: [ECI Plan Calculator](https://a836-rpie.nyc.gov/ecicalculator/extenuatingCircumstance.cfm) [FTI Plan Calculator](https://a836-rpie.nyc.gov/ecicalculator/FixTermPlan.cfm) [LIS Plan Calculator](https://a836-rpie.nyc.gov/ecicalculator/LowIncomeSenior.cfm) Income Worksheet You must submit an income worksheet with your application if you did not file a federal or NY State tax return last year. [Download the Income Worksheet](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/finance/downloads/pdf/ptaid/ptaid-worksheet.pdf).
Required Documents
To apply for PT AID, you must provide: A completed and signed application A government-issued ID, such as a valid driver's license, non-driver ID, IDNYC Card, U.S. Passport, or Military ID Your most recent federal or NY State tax return or the Income Worksheet Your property's deed or title A bank mortgage or insurance policy statement or a utility or credit card bill that's at least one year old A completed and signed payment plan calculator form If enrolled in the Department of Environmental Protection's Water Debt Assistance Program, include a document or statement from the program For the ECI plan, you must include documentation of your extenuating circumstances, such as: Death certificate Income tax return for the past year Unemployment compensation documents Hospital documents Military documents Court documents If DOF determines that you are eligible, you will be asked to pay for a title search report to identify mortgages and liens that affect your property's value.
Next Steps After Applying
If the Department of Finance confirms your eligibility, a title search report will be required of your property. DOF will notify you by mail within 15 days whether your application has been approved or disapproved, or if more information is needed to be able to process your application. Properties with incomplete applications will be placed in the next tax lien sale cycle if the application is not completed within 45 days or if DOF rejects the application.
Renew or Change
Homeowners enrolled in any PT AID plan must renew annually. DOF will mail a PT AID Renewal Change Form two months prior to the expiration date of the plan you are enrolled in. You must complete the form and mail back to DOF. You can also request to change the PT AID plan that you are enrolled in or the terms of the plan. You can make only one change to the terms of the agreement every 6 months. If the ownership of the property has changed you will need to submit documentation (if someone was added to or removed from the deed, or one spouse passed away).
Leaving the Program
Low-Income Seniors (LIS) Plan You will leave the program if: The fixed term expires You don’t recertify or file a renewal application You don’t address a missed payment within six months You pass away You move (unless you are hospitalized or relocate temporarily to a nursing home for three years or less) When you leave the program, you or your beneficiary will have nine months to arrange for payment of deferred amounts. Failure to do so may cause the City to sell the tax lien. If the owner is deceased, the surviving spouse will have 18 months to arrange for payment of deferred amounts. They may apply for deferral separately. Fixed-Term, Income-Based (FTI) or Extenuating Circumstances (ECI) Plan You will leave the program if: The fixed term expires You decide to finish your agreement before the term ends You don’t recertify or file a renewal application You don’t address a missed payment within six months You move (unless you are hospitalized or relocate temporarily to a nursing home for three years or less) When you leave the program, you will have nine months to arrange for payment of deferred amounts. Failure to do so may cause the City to sell the tax lien.

Professional misconduct includes the following but is not limited to: Permitting or aiding an unlicensed person to perform activities requiring a license Practicing beyond the scope of the profession Releasing confidential information without authorization Failing to return or provide copies of records on request Abandoning or neglecting a patient in need of immediate care Performing unnecessary work or unauthorized services Practicing under the influence of alcohol or other drugs Complaints must be submitted in writing to the New York State Office of Professional Discipline (OPD). title: No Penalty Private Elevator Safety Inspection
body:
The New York City Department of Buildings (DOB) offers a No-Penalty Safety Inspection Program for Private Elevators and other private elevator devices, including dumbwaiters, platform lifts, and stairway chair lifts. The program for this year has ended.
Property owners are legally required to register these devices and have a certificate of compliance from the Department of Buildings to ensure they can be operated safely. Unregistered elevators, and ones that aren’t properly maintained, may pose a serious safety risk to passengers. Property owners with private elevator devices in their buildings are encouraged to take advantage of this opportunity, not only for their own safety, but also for the safety of their friends and families. This safety inspection does not exempt jurisdictional elevators from code-required category 1 and category 5 cycle inspections.

title: Taxi and For-Hire Vehicle Congestion Surcharge
body:
Need something else? [Congestion Pricing Program](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03612) [Governor](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01187) for comments or complaints about the surcharge [Taxi Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01241) for complaints about an incorrect fare being charged New York State imposes a congestion surcharge for some taxis and for-hire vehicles for trips that: Both begin and end in NY State, and Begin in, end in, or pass through Manhattan south of, but not including, 96th Street (the congestion zone) This surcharge is separate from the [Congestion Pricing](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03612) toll charged for entering the Congestion Relief Zone in Manhattan. The surcharge applies to: Taxis Green cabs Limousines Black cars Livery vehicles (also known as community cars) Rideshare or transportation network company vehicles Pool vehicles The surcharge does not apply to: Transportation in connection with funerals Buses Ambulances and ambulettes MTA transportation In general, the surcharge is: $2.50 per trip in a medallion taxicab vehicle $2.75 per trip in a for-hire vehicle that is not a medallion taxicab or a pool vehicle 75 cents per pool trip This amount must be passed through to passengers and reported separately on any receipt given to the passenger.    Liability for the surcharge (responsibility for collecting, paying, and filing returns with the State) depends on the type of vehicle. [Learn more about the congestion surcharge and liability.](https://www.tax.ny.gov/bus/cs/csidx.htm)

title: Animal Abuse Registry
body:
Need something else? [Animal Abuse](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02224) to report a neglected or abused animal New York City residents convicted of an animal abuse crime must register with the NYC Animal Abuse Registry. You can: Learn about the registration process Report someone who failed to register Subscribe to the Registry if you own an animal-related business or organization [Learn more about the Animal Abuse Registry.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/animal-abuse-registry.page) Animal Abuse Registration Act The 2014 Animal Abuse Registration Act requires anyone living in New York City who is convicted of an animal abuse crime after October 2, 2014, and who is at least 18 years old at the time of conviction, to contact the NYC Health Department to be added to the NYC Animal Abuse Registry.
How to Register
If you are required to register for the Animal Abuse Registry, you must contact the NYC Health Department within 5 days of being released from incarceration, or within five days of sentencing if you were not incarcerated. The registration period lasts for 5 years after sentencing or, if incarcerated, for five years after your release from incarceration.  Failure to register as required may be punishable by up to a year in jail, a fine of up to $1,000, or both. You can register by email or by phone. By Email [animalabuseregistry@health.nyc.gov](mailto:animalabuseregistry@health.nyc.gov). By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Required Updates to Registry If you are on the Registry, you must contact the NYC Health Department to update your registration: Each year within 20 days of your first registration date Within 5 days of any change in original registration information
Report Someone Who Fails to Register
You can report someone you believe should be listed on the Animal Abuse Registry. By Email [animalabuseregistry@health.nyc.gov](mailto:animalabuseregistry@health.nyc.gov). By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Businesses and Organizations
The 2014 Animal Abuse Registration Act requires certain animal-related businesses and organizations to check the NYC Animal Abuse Registry and refuse to sell or transfer ownership of an animal to anyone listed in the Registry. Before a business or organization requests a subscription to the registry, they must be approved by the NYC Department of Health.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: NYC311 Accounts
body:
Need something else? [Service Request Status](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01066) With an NYC311 Online Account, you can: Track your service requests in one convenient location  Submit service requests faster by prefilling your contact information  Set preferences for how you receive request status updates   You aren’t required to have an online account to use our website or file service requests; it just makes things a bit easier. We are changing the way you log in to your 311 Account. We’re now using NYC.ID, the single sign-in for many City websites. This change makes your account safer and easier to use with other City government websites.
Link Your 311 Account to NYC.ID
If you use the same email address for both your 311 Account and your NYC.ID, just log in with your NYC.ID password and username.  If you do not use the same email address for both your 311 Account and your NYC.ID, you’ll need to create a new NYC.ID to keep your past 311 service request history. Here is what you need to do:  Go to the NYC.ID [Create Account](https://www1.nyc.gov/account/register.htm?target=aHR0cHM6Ly9wb3J0YWwuMzExLm55Yy5nb3YvcHJvZmlsZQ&fromKiosk=false&client_id=piQBWIKc2ZJpuup6mVjJbNSU) page.  Complete the form. Make sure to enter the email address you’ve used for your 311 Account. Please note: If you don’t do this now, you’ll lose your service request history.  Submit the form.  Confirm your email address.
Create an NYC.ID
Signing up is easy. To create an NYC.ID: Click “Sign Up” on the right side of the NYC311 homepage or [click here](https://www1.nyc.gov/account/user/profile.htm?target=aHR0cHM6Ly9wb3J0YWwuMzExLm55Yy5nb3YvcHJvZmlsZQ&fromKiosk=false&tab=email&client_id=piQBWIKc2ZJpuup6mVjJbNSU). Go to the [Create Account](https://www1.nyc.gov/account/register.htm?target=aHR0cHM6Ly9wb3J0YWwuMzExLm55Yy5nb3YvcHJvZmlsZQ&fromKiosk=false&client_id=piQBWIKc2ZJpuup6mVjJbNSU)   page.  Complete the form. If you are linking your 311 Account, make sure to enter the same email address you’ve used for your 311 Account to link it with NYC.ID.  Submit the form.  Confirm your email address.  Complete your 311 profile.
Password Reset Issues
On November 13, 2025, 311’s website accounts system was converted to NYC.ID. NYC.ID is the single sign-in system for many City websites, including ACCESS HRA, Notify NYC, and NYC Housing Connect. If you had an account before November 13 and have not yet registered for an NYC.ID through 311: Usernames and passwords from 311’s former accounts system have been deactivated. Your account history has been retained.  To access your 311 account, you’ll need to [register for NYC.ID](https://www1.nyc.gov/account/register.htm?target=aHR0cHM6Ly9wb3J0YWwuMzExLm55Yy5nb3YvcHJvZmlsZQ&fromKiosk=false&client_id=piQBWIKc2ZJpuup6mVjJbNSU). If you use the same email address your former account had, your history will carry over automatically.  If you signed up for an account after November 13 or have an NYC.ID already: Use the [Forgot Password](https://www1.nyc.gov/account/forgotPassword.htm?target=aHR0cHM6Ly9wb3J0YWwuMzExLm55Yy5nb3YvcHJvZmlsZQ&fromKiosk=false&client_id=piQBWIKc2ZJpuup6mVjJbNSU) link on the NYC.ID sign in page.
NYC.ID False Link Issue
On November 13, 2025, NYC311’s online accounts transitioned to the NYC.ID platform. An email notification was sent out to account holders about this change. Some email platforms mistakenly converted the NYC.ID name into a hyperlink. Since the official name includes a period between the C and the I, a few systems interpreted it as a web address and created a link automatically. This made it seem like a valid link was there when it wasn’t.  If you’ve already completed your 311 profile on NYCID, there’s nothing further you need to do.   If you haven’t created yours yet, you can get started by using the Create an NYC.ID section above.
Report a Technical Problem
If you experience any technical issues with your: NYC.ID Account, please [submit this feedback form](https://www1.nyc.gov/account/feedback.htm?client_id=piQBWIKc2ZJpuup6mVjJbNSU). 311 profile , please use the [NYC311 Feedback Form](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/submit-feedback/). Do not use these feedback forms to file service requests or ask questions that are not related to accounts.
NYC311 Privacy Policy
Your privacy is important to us.  NYC311 only collects identifying information needed to work on your service request. This can include your name, address, phone number, and other identifying information, although some requests may be filed anonymously. We do not collect any information for commercial or marketing purposes.  NYC311 only shares identifying information with City agencies, City workers, and vendors handling your request. We do not share identifying information with third parties unless required by law. The NYC311 Privacy Policy details how we handle identifying information. [Read it here.](https://www.nyc.gov/html/misc/html/NYC311-privacy-policy.html)

title: Parking Ticket or Camera Violation Advocate
body:
Need something else? [Parking Ticket or Camera Violation Payment](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02036) to pay a parking ticket or camera violation The Office of the Parking Summons Advocate can help if you’ve tried to resolve certain parking ticket or camera violation issues with the Department of Finance (DOF) through the normal process, but you’ve been unsuccessful or haven’t received a timely response. The Advocate can help if: You don’t get a timely response from DOF to requests for hearings, appeals, or refunds You keep getting notices about tickets you’ve already paid or had a hearing on You had a valid defense but were found guilty anyway Depending on the issue, the Advocate may be able to help you better prepare for a hearing or appeal or advocate on your behalf with other DOF units. Regardless of the assistance, the Advocate can’t: Extend any deadlines Guarantee any specific outcome Have sole authority to change an outcome Reverse an administrative law judge’s decision Dismiss a ticket Waive penalties If you wish to appeal a guilty decision, you should do so, even if you want to ask the Advocate for help.
When to Get Help from the Advocate
The Parking Summons Advocate will only help with certain parking or camera violation issues. Issues Addressed by the Advocate Guilty Decisions The Parking Summons Advocate can help if you disputed a ticket or filed an appeal but you were found guilty even though: You never owned the vehicle or it was transferred before the date and time you were ticketed The license plate was lost or stolen before the date and time you were ticketed and you immediately filed a police report and replaced the registration plates and stickers The vehicle wasn’t in New York City on the date you were ticketed The parking ticket inaccurately described your car’s license plate number, state of registration, plate type, make or model, or body type The ticket is missing information, such as the date and time, address where the ticket was issued, or issuer’s signature The registered owner of the vehicle died before or within 90 days of when the ticket was issued Department of Finance Response You can get help from the Advocate if you don’t get a timely response from the Department of Finance to requests for hearings, appeals, or refunds. You can contact the Parking Summons Advocate for help if: You submitted a dispute to your ticket and haven’t received a decision within 20 days You submitted a Parking or Camera Violation Appeal Application and haven’t received a decision within 60 days You submitted a Parking or Camera Violation Refund Form and haven’t received a decision within 60 days Notice for Violation Already Paid or Dismissed You can contact the Parking Summons Advocate for help if you keep receiving notices from the Department of Finance or a collection agency about a ticket that you already paid or already had a hearing on but for which you never received a decision. Issues Not Addressed by the Advocate The Advocate can’t help you if: You need help with a traffic ticket (moving violation) You are represented by an attorney or broker You are asking for legal advice You’re claiming that a NYC parking law, rule, or regulation violates the New York State or U.S. Constitution
Getting Help from the Advocate
You can contact the Parking Summons Advocate online or by mail. You can also meet with staff virtually or in person at a DOF Business Center. After reviewing your help request, the Advocate will call, email, or mail you with more information within 14 days. Depending on the issue, the Advocate may be able to help you better prepare for a hearing or appeal or advocate on your behalf with other DOF units. [Learn more about the Parking Summons Advocate.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/vehicles/opsa.page) Online [Contact the Parking Summons Advocate.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-by-email/contact-opsa.page) By Fax You can fax your help request to (646) 500-6541. By Mail You can request assistance by completing and mailing a help request form. Mail to: Parking Summons Advocate 66 John Street, 3rd Floor New York, NY 10038 You can get the help request form by mail.
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Virtual You can schedule a video appointment with staff from the Parking Summons Advocate’s office.   [Schedule a video appointment online.](https://outlook.office365.com/owa/calendar/OfficeoftheParkingSummonsAdvocateDOF@nyco365.onmicrosoft.com/bookings/) In Person Staff from the Parking Advocate's office are available at Department of Finance Business Centers on specific days in each borough. All DOF Business Centers are open Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM. Bronx Business Center : Tuesday and Friday Brooklyn Business Center : Monday and Thursday Queens Business Center : Monday and Friday Manhattan Business Center : Tuesday and Thursday Staten Island Business Center : 1st and 3rd Friday of each month [Get DOF Business Center locations.](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01015) Schedule an Appointment You can schedule an appointment to ensure social distancing at DOF Business Centers. Walk-in customers are still accepted. [Schedule an appointment.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/make-an-appointment.page)

title: Specialized High Schools
body:
New York City public high schools include nine Specialized High Schools for students who excel academically or artistically. These schools are: Bronx High School of Science Brooklyn Latin School Brooklyn Technical High School Fiorello H. LaGuardia High School of Music and Art and Performing Arts High School for Math, Science and Engineering at City College High School of American Studies at Lehman College Queens High School for the Sciences at York College Staten Island Technical High School Stuyvesant High School Under New York State law, admission to these schools is based on the results of a competitive test or audition. Students must be residents of New York City and be current 8th or first-time 9th graders to apply. Onine [Learn more about Specialized High Schools.](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/enrollment/enroll-grade-by-grade/specialized-high-schools) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Specialized High School Admissions Test (SHSAT)
To apply to a specialized high school other than LaGuardia High School, you must take the Specialized High School Admissions Test (SHSAT). Students currently in the 8th grade and first time 9th grade students are eligible to register. Students who are in the 10th, 11th, and 12th grades are not eligible to take the exam. NYC public school students who want to take the fall exam must register with their guidance counselor. After registering, your school counselor will give you an SHSAT Test Ticket with the specific date, time, and location for your test. Students attending non-public schools should speak to their schools directly about registering for the SHSAT. Key Dates Thursday, March 6, 2025: High School Offer Release  You can [sign up to receive emails](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/connect) with the latest updates on specialized high school admissions. Summer SHSAT For eligible students who did not participate in the Fall Specialized High Schools Admissions Test (SHSAT), a summer SHSAT is offered in August. You can register for the summer SHSAT in July and August at a [Family Welcome Center](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03128). Learn More You can get more information and assistance online and by phone. Information about testing locations is also available. Online [Learn more about the specialized high school admissions test (SHSAT).](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/school-life/learning/testing/specialized-high-school-admissions-test) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) if you need more help.
LaGuardia High School Auditions
Admission to LaGuardia High School of Music and Art and Performing Arts is based in part on a competitive audition. The SHSAT is not considered for admission to LaGuardia High School. During the application period, students can register for an audition to LaGuardia High School through their school counselor.  After registering, your school counselor will give you an Audition Ticket with the specific date, time, and location for your test. All auditions are held at LaGuardia High School. The application period for the 2025-2026 school year is closed. You can [sign up to receive emails](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/connect) with the latest updates on specialized high school admissions.
DREAM Program
The DREAM program helps eligible students get ready for the Specialized High Schools Admissions Test (SHSAT). There are two DREAM programs. The Specialized High Schools Institute (DREAM-SHSI) is an extracurricular program of rigorous coursework. To be accepted into the Institute, the student must commit to participating for the full program, which spans 6th grade, 7th grade, and 8th grade. The Summer/Fall Intensive test-prep program runs during the summer and fall before students plan to take the SHSAT. If your child is eligible, an invitation letter and a pre-populated application will be delivered to your child’s school. You can get more information about DREAM online or by email. Online [Get information about preparing for the SHSAT through the DREAM program.](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/about-us/programs/dream-program) By Email [SHSI@schools.nyc.gov](mailto:SHSI@schools.nyc.gov)
High School Fairs
At High School Admissions Fairs, you can speak with representatives from all of the City's public high schools, including specialized schools, and participate in workshops related to the high school admissions process. You can also get copies of publications, including the Directory of the New York City Public High Schools.
