[Smoke Free Air Act](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03007) [Construction Site No Smoking Sign Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02241) The Smoke Free Air Act (SFAA) protects the health of New Yorkers against the harmful effects of secondhand smoke by banning smoking and the use of e-cigarettes in public spaces. Public spaces include: Businesses Child or day care centers Convention halls Gym, health clubs, and other membership associations Health care facilities Libraries Museums and galleries Office buildings, factories, and warehouses Parks Public and private schools Restaurants and bars (including outdoor dining areas) Residential building common areas Shopping malls and retail stores (other than retail tobacco stores) Sports and recreational arenas Theaters, concert halls, and auditoriums Zoos You can report: Ashtray in a smoke free area Smoking or vaping signage missing or inadequate Workplace policy not provided or inadequate To report smoking or vaping in a smoke free area, refer to [Smoking or Vaping Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02295).
Ashtray in a Smoke Free Area
You can report an ashtray in a smoke free area at a location covered by the SFAA.
Report an ashtray in a smoke free area.
Smoking or Vaping Signage Missing or Inadequate
Business operators and residential property managers must post smoking or vaping signage at their establishment or in common areas of residential buildings. You can report smoking or vaping signage that is not posted or easily visible.
Report smoking or vaping signage missing or inadequate.
Workplace Policy Not Provided or Inadequate
Business owners and employers are required to create a smoking and e-cigarette use policy. It should be posted for all employees and shared with new hires. In most cases, the policy should prohibit any smoking and e-cigarette use in indoor workplace spaces.

title: Building Planting Regulations
body:
The Department of Buildings (DOB) enforces planting regulations for buildings throughout the City. Planted areas: Have front yard minimums ranging from 20% for narrow lots to 50% for wide lots. Can be a combination of grass, groundcover, shrubs, trees, or other living plant material. Planted areas within a driveway or parking space do not qualify towards the minimum planting requirements. The minimum requirements for Residential Districts in New York City are: R1 through R5 Districts: Front Yard Planting Street frontage of zoning lot Percentage of front yard (min) Less than 20 feet 20 20 to 34 feet 25 35 to 59 feet 30 60 feet or greater 50
Report a planting violation.
Zoning Districts
The Department of City Planning (DCP) has zoning district guides. [Get more information from DCP Zoning District Guides.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/planning/zoning/districts-tools/residence-districts-r1-r10.page) Medium and High Density Zoned Districts Planting regulations also apply to medium- and high-density contextual R6 through R10 districts and where the optional [Quality Housing Program](https://www.nyc.gov/site/planning/zoning/glossary.page#quality) is utilized in R6 through R10 districts. title: Bird Flu Information
body:
A type of bird flu (avian influenza), called H5N1, has been detected in birds in New York City. People exposed to sick or dead birds with H5N1 are asked to call the NYC Health Department if they develop flu-like symptoms. There have been no human cases of bird flu in New York. The current risk to New Yorkers remains low. People who work with animals may be at higher risk of exposure to bird flu. No human-to-human transmission of H5N1 has been detected to date. The NYC Health Department recommends New Yorkers report groups of sick or dead birds or animals through NYC311. Avoid contact with birds that look sick or have died and surfaces that have bird feces. Do not consume raw milk or raw milk products. Continue safe food handling practices at home to reduce the risk of food-borne illnesses. [Get more information about bird flu from the NYC Health Department.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/avian-flu.page)
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to report the problem.

title: Broker Fees
body:
The NYC Fairness in Apartment Rental Expenses (FARE) Act went into effect on June 11, 2025. This law prohibits brokers who represent landlords from charging broker fees to tenants. This includes brokers who publish listings with the landlord’s permission. Landlords or their agents must disclose other fees that the tenant must pay in their listings and rental agreements. The Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) enforces this law. You can file a complaint against a landlord or real estate agent that: Charges prospective tenants a broker fee when not hired by the tenant Requires prospective tenants to use an agent Lists a broker fee Does not disclose fees or surcharges [Learn more about the FARE Act.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/about/FAQ-Broker-Fees.page)
Report a problem with a landlord or real estate agent.
What Happens Next If you don't include your address or email with your service request, you won't receive follow up. The Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) will consider your complaint a tip. If you include your address, DCWP will mail you a complaint form. You must complete and return it to DCWP. If you provide your email address, you'll get the form by email instead. Check your spam folder if you don't see it in your inbox.

title: Saturday Night Lights
body:
Saturday Night Lights (SNL) is a citywide program that provides young people with year-round free, exceptional sports programs on Saturday nights. The SNL program provides basketball, soccer, dance, and other sports at select gyms, community centers, and schools. Some sites may offer additional activities beyond sports, such as mentorship and workshops. Sessions take place every Saturday from 5 PM to 9 PM at various locations in all five boroughs. The program is open to all New York City youth ages 11 through 18 at no cost. No prior registration is required. Youth can walk in and sign up on-site at participating locations in any borough. You can get more information online, including a map of locations and site-specific offerings. [Learn more about Saturday Night Lights.](https://saturdaynightlights.cityofnewyork.us/) [View a map of Saturday Night Lights program locations.](https://saturdaynightlights.cityofnewyork.us/locations/)

title: Hotel License
body:
As of May 3, 2025, you must have a license to operate a hotel in New York City. A hotel license is required if your business operates, owns, leases, or manages a hotel and controls its day-to-day operations. This includes the employment of the people who work at the hotel, by virtue of your ownership, management agreement, lease, or other legal construct. You must have a separate license for each hotel you operate. [Download the hotel license application and other forms.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/businesses/licenses-apply.page) Fee The fee for the full two-year license term is $350. title: NYPD Quality of Life Division
body:
The NYPD and the Mayor’s office announced a new citywide public safety initiative that: Focuses on enhancing trust between communities and the police Addresses everyday issues that impact New Yorkers' sense of safety and well-being The new Quality of Life Division will unite specially-trained officers from various existing community-oriented roles, including: Neighborhood coordination officers Youth coordination officers Traffic safety officers This restructuring creates a more flexible and responsive deployment model, allowing the NYPD to direct resources to specific needs within their communities. These "Q-Teams" will focus on non-emergency 311 and 911 concerns, such as [abandoned vehicles](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02130), [noise complaints](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02125), and [illegal parking](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01986). Teams will also continue to nurture the relationships that were built with businesses and local community. The pilot program began on April 14, 2025 in the 13th, 40th, 60th, 75th and 101st Precincts and Police Service Area (PSA) 1. The initiative will be evaluated and refined before expanding citywide. [Learn more about the NYPD Quality of Life Division.](https://www.nyc.gov/mayors-office/news/2025/04/mayor-adams-nypd-commissioner-tisch-launch-new-quality-life-division-enhance-public-safety#/0)

title: Natural Gas Detectors
body:
Call 911 If you smell gas, leave the area immediately . Once you are safe, call 911 to report gas odors or other potential gas leaks.
Natural Gas Detector Requirements Building owners are required to install natural gas detectors (alarms) in: Apartment buildings Hotels, motels, and lodging or rooming houses Single room occupancy buildings Private dwellings – one and two-family homes For multiple dwellings and one- and two-family homes, you must install detectors within 15 feet of the primary entrance to each sleeping room if there is gas piping in the building. Natural gas detectors are required to be replaced as their useful life expires, according to the manufacturer's instructions and based on the original date of installation. The replacement device must be a model that has an end-of-life alarm. While owners are required to install and replace natural gas detectors, tenants are responsible for maintaining them and changing the batteries. Tenants must pay the owner $25 when the owner installs a new natural gas detector, replaces a natural gas  detector that has reached the end of its useful life, or replaces one that the tenant lost or damaged. Tenants have up to 1 year to make the payment. [Learn more about HPD's natural gas detector requirements.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/detectors.page)
Signs of a Gas Leak
If you smell gas, leave the area immediately . Once you are safe, call 911 to report gas odors or other potential gas leaks. Natural gas can leak from any gas piping when there is a break or crack in the pipes that transport natural gas to homes. Natural gas is mostly made up of methane, a colorless and odorless gas. To help detect leaks, gas suppliers add a distinctive odorant called mercaptan, which gives it a smell similar to rotten eggs. A natural gas leak can happen because of aging infrastructure, physical damage to pipes, or improper installation or maintenance of gas appliances. Gas leaks can range from small, undetectable leaks to major leaks that present significant dangers. Signs of a gas leak: Distinctive sulfur or rotten egg smell, hissing or whistling sounds; or Physical symptoms like dizziness, headaches, nausea, or respiratory difficulties.
Exempt Buildings
If your building has no gas piping, it may be exempt from natural gas detector rules. HPD will have a process for filing an exemption from some requirements.  More information will be available later this year. A building can be exempt from providing carbon monoxide detecting devices and posting notices related to carbon monoxide if it has no fossil fuel burning devices and no enclosed parking spaces Note:  If the residential portion of your building does not have any fossil fuel burning devices but does have enclosed parking spaces in a space attached to the residential building, you are required to provide carbon monoxide detecting devices in the apartments only on those floors with the enclosed parking spaces, and on those floors immediately above and immediately below the enclosed parking spaces. In this case, you may file for a partial exemption.  A building can be exempt from providing natural gas detecting devices and posting notices related to natural gas If the building has no gas piping
Installation and Types of Detectors
Owners are required to provide and install at least one natural gas detector in each apartment in applicable buildings. Natural gas alarms that are powered either by battery or by plug-in AC receptacle may be installed by anyone, including but not limited to the: Building owner Building maintenance personnel Dwelling unit occupant  The devices must be replaced upon expiration of its useful life, or if stolen, removed, missing, or rendered inoperable within 30 calendar days after receiving written notice that such device is inoperable.  “Central System” Natural gas alarms must be installed by a New York City Licensed electrical contractor who obtains all required permits from the Department of Buildings (DOB). [Learn about DOB’s standards for installation and location of natural gas alarms.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/natural-gas-detector-faqs.page)
Costs
Tenants who live in a Class A multiple dwelling or private dwelling (permanent residence dwelling) must reimburse the building owner $25 for each smoke detector, each carbon monoxide detector, and each natural gas detector or $50 for each joint smoke/carbon monoxide detector or joint smoke/natural gas detector or joint carbon monoxide/natural gas detector, or $75 for a combined carbon, smoke and natural gas detecting device that is newly installed or installed as a result of the occupant’s failure to maintain the detector, or where the detector has been lost or damaged by the occupant. The occupant has one year from the date of installation to make a payment. Tenants who live in a Class B multiple dwelling building (legal short-term occupancies like a hotel, dorm, lodge, or rooming/boarding house) are not required to reimburse property owners for any detector device.
Notice to Tenants
Owners are also required to install signage and provide tenants with notice about the natural gas detector legal requirements and manufacturer’s recommendations, as well as to keep records regarding natural gas detector installation. [Learn more about HPD's natural gas detector requirements.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/detectors.page) For more information about HPD Code Enforcement borough offices use the, [HPD Code Enforcement Borough Service Centers](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01073) page.
Get Help
You can get more information from your HPD Code Enforcement borough office. Use the [HPD Code Enforcement Borough Service Centers](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01073) page. Property owners can also email questions to HPD at [codevios@hpd.nyc.gov](mailto:codevios@hpd.nyc.gov).

title: Traffic Lane Separator Complaint
body:
Traffic lane separators are located on city streets to improve roadway safety and manage the flow of different types of roadway users. The Department of Transportation (DOT) installs and maintains traffic lane separators, including: Plastic flexible delineators which are used to protect on-street pedestrian zones and bike lanes on streets. They can be yellow or white.             ​​     Plastic bollards ("Quick Kurbs")  look like an upside-down baseball bat.  They are attached to a rubber curb or plastic cone-like base with reflective coverings. These are used to separate traffic lanes and protect pedestrian zones, bikes, and contra-flow bus lanes.                  Rubber speed bumps are installed on the roadway or at corners to slow vehicles down and help enforce safe driving. These can be found at left and right turns, indicating bike and bus lanes, roundabouts and curb extensions known as chicanes.                   File a Complaint You can report damaged, flattened, or missing traffic lane separators to DOT. [Report a problem with a traffic lane separator located on a city street.](https://www1.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/contact/contact-form.shtml?routing=ts)

title: Mobile Behavioral Health Treatment and Care Coordination Services
body:
The Single Point of Access (SPOA) program helps providers connect people with serious mental illness to mental health services that can accommodate them. Through these services, people with serious mental illness can connect to treatment, communicate with providers and get help finding benefits. In addition, Children's Single Point of Access (CSPOA) is a centralized referral system for youth (21 or under) with serious emotional disturbance who need intensive mental health services to remain at home or in their community.  After receiving a referral request, CSPOA will conduct an assessment and interview the family and referrer to determine the child’s needs.  Providers who refer clients for these services must include in the referral application the following: A recent psychiatric evaluation A recent psychosocial evaluation A client consent form The NYC Health Department reviews eligibility and makes referrals to the appropriate services.  More detailed information, including referral applications and consent forms, are available online. [Learn more about referring an adult to mental health services through SPOA.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/providers/resources/mental-illness-single-point-of-access.page) [Learn more about referring a youth (21 or under) to mental health services through CSPOA.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/providers/resources/mental-illness-childrens-single-point-of-access.page)

title: Inflation Refund
body:
As part of the 2025-2026 state budget, the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance will be sending out inflation refunds to eligible New Yorkers.  There is no application process as residents that are eligible will automatically receive a check in the mail. Checks will be mailed out over a period of several weeks starting  at the end of September of 2025. You may receive your check sooner or later than your neighbors, as mailings are not based on zip code or region. This is not a program being administered by the City of New York. NYC311 is not able to provide the status of your check. [Learn more about the inflation refund check.](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pit/inflation-refund-checks.htm)
Eligibility
You are eligible for a refund check if, for tax year 2023, you: filed Form IT-201, New York State Resident Income Tax Return reported income within the qualifying thresholds below, and were not claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer’s return Your inflation refund check will be based on your income and filing status. Filing status 2023 New York Adjusted Gross Income (Form IT-201 line 33) Refund amount Single $75,000 or less more than $75,000, but not more than $150,000  $200 $150 Married filing joint $150,000 or less more than $150,000, but not more than $300,000 $400 $300 Married filing separate $75,000 or less more than $75,000, but not more than $150,000 $200 $150 Head of household $75,000 or less more than $75,000, but not more than $150,000 $200 $150 Qualified surviving spouse $150,000 or less more than $150,000, but not more than $300,000 $400 $300
Inflation Refund Scam
New York State Tax Department is not contacting individuals about the New York State inflation refund check. If you are contacted about the inflation refund check by someone claiming to be from the Tax Department, do not provide any personal information. You can report any scams to the State by email or by phone. By Email [dtfoia@tax.ny.gov](mailto:dtfoia@tax.ny.gov) By Phone
Agency: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
Division: Fraud Line
Phone Number: (518) 457-0578
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8:30 AM - 4:30 PM
Get Help
If you need more help, contact the NYS Department of Taxation and Finance for assistance with cashing your check or reporting lost or destroyed checks. They will not be able to provide you information regarding the delivery or status of your check. [Learn more about lost, stolen, or destroyed refund checks.](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pit/file/replacement-check.htm)
Agency: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
Phone Number: (518) 457-5181
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8:30 AM - 4:30 PM
Staff is available through the automated phone system during business hours. Automated assistance is also available in Cantonese, Mandarin, Russian, and Spanish.

title: Essential Plan Cooling Program
body:
Need something else? [HEAP Cooling Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02552) The Essential Plan Cooling Program provides a free air conditioner to eligible New Yorkers to help keep their homes cool. To be eligible, you must be enrolled in the NY State of Health’s Essential Plan and apply. If your application is approved, you may receive one cooling unit per applicant household every five years.   If an air conditioner cannot be safely installed, a fan will be provided.   Installation cannot exceed $900 for a window or portable air conditioner or $500 for a standing floor fan. For an existing wall sleeve unit replacement, installation cannot exceed $1,100. Cash benefits are not available. [Learn more about the Essential Plan Cooling Program.](https://info.nystateofhealth.ny.gov/CoolingProgram)
Eligibility
You may qualify if you: Are enrolled in NY State of Health’s Essential Plan Have persistent asthma Have not received a cooling unit in the past five years through the Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP) Cooling Program. Request installation at the permanent residential address on file with NY State of Health If you are unsure whether you are an Essential Plan enrollee, you can contact NY State of Health by phone or download the NYSOH Mobile Upload App from the [Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/ebtedge/id1398046228) or [Google Play Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.fis.ebtedge) and log in to your account to confirm you are enrolled in the Essential Plan.
Agency: New York State Department of Health
Phone Number: (855) 355-5777
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 8 PM; Saturday : 9 AM - 1 PM
Automated Assistance is available in English and Spanish 24 hours, 7 days a week. Staff is available through the automated phone system during business hours, except on City Holidays. Most languages are available through a staff person.
Apply
New Yorkers who are enrolled in the Essential Plan must complete the [online application](https://healthresearchinc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/requests/new). Applications will be accepted until August 31, 2026 or until funds run out. Once an application is submitted, you will receive an email within two to three weeks letting you know if you’ve been approved. If approved, the email will include information about the vendor you should contact to schedule installation of your device.
Maintenance
You are responsible for maintaining the air conditioner.  This includes: Removing, covering, and storing the unit Reinstalling the unit or sleeve seasonally The vendor will help you sign up for the manufacturer’s warranty when they install the unit.
Get Help
For general questions about the program, you can contact the NY State of Health Customer Service Center.
Agency: New York State Department of Health

Automated Assistance is available in English and Spanish 24 hours, 7 days a week. Staff is available through the automated phone system during business hours, except on City Holidays. Most languages are available through a staff person.
If you have submitted an application, have been approved and are having trouble reaching an approved vendor or need help with this program, please contact NY State at [NYSoHCoolingProgram@health.ny.gov](mailto:NYSoHCoolingProgram@health.ny.gov).

title: Credit Card Surcharge
body:
Need something else? [Restaurant Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03516) to report restaurant surcharges Under a New York State law, businesses charging additional fees for credit card purchases must display the highest total price for each purchase (excluding sales tax). This means that if a purchase with a credit card would be higher than a cash purchase, the credit card purchase price must be displayed to customers. Business cannot: Put a sign on the wall or at the register that notifies a fee is applied to all credit card sales Advertise a cash discount without including the higher credit card price Charge separate line items to credit card users on a customer receipt without clearly posting the total price prior to purchase Include a credit card surcharge warning on the item price tag Business can: Clearly display both the credit card and the cash price for items List the higher credit card price and advertise a discount for cash purchases This law does not apply to debit cards. [Learn more about the credit card surcharge.](https://dos.ny.gov/business-resources) To report a business violating the credit surcharge law, go to the [Store Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02153) page.

title: Social Care Networks (SCNs)
body:
New York Medicaid members with social and health needs may qualify for support to access services like food, housing, home safety modifications, rent or utility assistance, and transportation. title: Bin Reimbursement
body:
Need something else? [Trash, Recycling, and Compost Bins](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01303) to learn more about buying an official NYC Bin [Residential Waste Containerization](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03602) to learn more about the residential trash containerization rules Owners of 1- and 2-family homes who receive the STAR or ESTAR in 2024 or 2025 exemption or credit are eligible to receive a one-time reimbursement check of $59.30 to pay for the cost of one 45 gallon official NYC Bin.  The Department of Finance (DOF) sent letters in October 2025 notifying homeowners of this refund.   Homeowners who have:  Already purchased their NYC Bin online or by phone from the City's vendorwill automatically receive a reimbursement check for $59.30. Purchased or will purchase their NYC Bin in person from Home Depot will use the voucher code at the top of the DOF letter and proof of purchase to request their reimbursement check. Request reimbursement with your voucher code online at [www.nyc.gov/freetrashbins](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/property/free-trash-bins.page). The deadline to request a reimbursement check is June 1, 2026. Reimbursement checks must be cashed or deposited within 90 days of the date on the check.
Request a Reimbursement Check or Credit
If you purchase or will purchase a NYC Bin in person from Home Depot you will need to apply for a reimbursement. You will need to submit your voucher code and proof of purchase to DOF.   Acceptable forms of proof of purchase are: A receipt A copy of a credit card bill or bank statement showing the purchase A photo of your bin with either the bin serial number or your home address in the picture The deadline to request a reimbursement is June 1, 2026. You will receive a reimbursement check or credit on your property tax account within six weeks of submitting your request. You can apply online, by mail, or in person. Online Request reimbursement with your voucher code online at [www.nyc.gov/freetrashbins](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/property/free-trash-bins.page). By Mail Completed applications can be mailed to: NYC Department of Finance 66 John Street, 18th Floor New York, NY 10038 You can get a paper application online or by mail. Online [Download the Trash Bin Reimbursement Form.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/finance/downloads/pdf/25pdf/trash_bin_reimbursement_form.pdf) By Mail
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to request a copy.
In Person You can deliver a completed application to any [DOF Business Center](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01015). To find a DOF Business Center, go to the [DOF Business Center](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01015) page.
Reimbursement Check Issues
Damaged Check   If the check you receive is damaged, please send it to the mailing address below. Rather than send you a new check, DOF will add the reimbursement as a credit to your property tax account. NYC Trash Bin Reimbursements Attn: Damaged Review P.O. Box 5528 Wrong Owner If you received a check that was addressed to someone else, please send it to: NYC Trash Bin Reimbursements Attn: Mailing Error P.O. Box 5528 Binghamton, NY 13902-5528 Deceased Homeowner If you received a check that was addressed to a deceased homeowner, please send it to: NYC Trash Bin Reimbursements Attn: Mailing Error P.O. Box 5528 Binghamton, NY 13902-5528 DOF will add the reimbursement as a credit to the property tax account. Lost or Misplaced Check If you lose your check, contact DOF at [nyc.gov/dofcustomerservice](https://nyc.gov/dofcustomerservice). Be sure to include your full name along with the address of the property. Allow up to four weeks for DOF to review your claim and reissue a reimbursement as a credit to your property tax account. Expired Check Reimbursement checks are valid for 90 days. If you have a check that is more than 90 days old, do not attempt to deposit or cash the check. Instead, you should contact DOF at [nyc.gov/dofcustomerservice](https://nyc.gov/dofcustomerservice). Provide DOF with your full name, borough, and address where your property is located, and the check number. Allow up to four weeks for DOF to review your claim.
Get Help
For more information on the program, visit [www.nyc.gov/freetrashbins](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/property/free-trash-bins.page). If you have additional questions, or lost your voucher code, you can contact DOF online or in person. Online [Contact the Department of Finance.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/about/contact-by-email/contact-us-general-correspondence.page) In Person To find a DOF Business Center, go to the [DOF Business Center](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01015) page.

title: Early Voting
body:
You don’t have to wait until Election Day to vote in NYC. The ballot is the same, no matter when you choose to vote. There are two ways to vote early: Vote at your early voting poll site Vote by early mail ballot
Early Voting at Poll Sites
Your early voting poll site is based on your home address that’s currently registered with the New York City Board of Elections (BOE). Poll sites and hours can change from election to election, so always check before you go. Your early voting poll site may also be different than your Election Day site. [Find your poll site.](https://findmypollsite.vote.nyc/) [Learn more about voting at poll sites.](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03691)
Early Voting by Mail Ballot
Any registered voter can vote by mail. You don't need to give a reason. You can request an early mail ballot online or apply by mail, email, or in person. If you are blind, have low vision, or have a disability that requires you to use an accessible version that can be read by a screen reader, you may request an accessible ballot. If you cannot affirm that you are blind or low vision, you must request a regular early mail ballot. Request a Ballot Online [Request an early mail ballot.](https://requestballot.vote.nyc/) Request a Ballot Application Ballot applications are available in multiple languages. Online [Download an application.](https://vote.nyc/page/absentee-voting-0) In Person Pick up a copy at a [BOE office](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03689). By Mail Call BOE to request an application and a postage-paid return envelope.
Agency: Board of Elections
Division: Vote Phone Bank
Phone Number: (866) 868-3692
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available through the automated phone system during business hours. Automated assistance is also available in Cantonese, Korean, Mandarin, and Spanish. Call volume is often high. If you receive a busy signal or can't get through, call back later.
Return an Early Mail Ballot You can return your completed ballot to the Board of Elections (BOE) by mail or in person. By Mail Mail your ballot to your [BOE borough office](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03689). To be counted, your ballot must be: Postmarked no later than Election Day Received by the borough office no later than 7 days after Election Day The Postal Service recommends mailing your ballot at least 7 days before Election Day to ensure it is received on time. In Person You can drop off your ballot at a [BOE office](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03689) or any [poll site](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03691) during voting hours. Note that not all early voting sites will be available for drop-off on Election Day. You must deliver your ballot no later than 9 PM on Election Day. Track Ballot Status You can check the status of your ballot or ballot application. [Track your ballot.](https://requestballot.vote.nyc/tracking)

title: Absentee Voting
body:
You can vote by absentee ballot if you can’t vote on Election Day or at an early voting poll site because of: Business Studies Travel Imprisonment (not including convicted felons) Illness Disability Hospitalization Residency in a long-term care facility Accessible absentee ballots are available if you have a condition or disability that requires a ballot that can be read by a screen reader. Note: You don't need a reason to vote by mail with an [early mail ballot](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03687). Voting in Person After Requesting an Absentee Ballot If you change your mind and want to vote in person instead of by absentee ballot, you can. But you can't cast your vote on a voting machine. Instead, a poll worker will give you an affidavit ballot to complete. After they get your affidavit ballot, the Board of Elections (BOE) will check if your absentee ballot has been received. If it’s been received, the affidavit ballot won’t be counted. If it hasn’t been received, the affidavit ballot will be counted.
Request an Absentee Ballot
You can request an absentee ballot online or submit an application by mail, email, or in person. If you are blind, have low vision, or have a disability that requires you to use an accessible version that can be read by a screen reader, you may request an accessible ballot. If you cannot affirm that you are blind or low vision, you must request a regular absentee ballot. Request a Ballot Online [Request an absentee ballot.](https://requestballot.vote.nyc/) After submitting your request, you can check the status of your application online. [Track your ballot request.](https://requestballot.vote.nyc/tracking) Request a Ballot Application Ballot applications are available in multiple languages. Online [Download an application.](https://vote.nyc/page/absentee-voting-0) In Person Pick up a copy at a [BOE office](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03689). By Mail Call BOE to request an application and a postage-paid return envelope.
Agency: Board of Elections
Division: Vote Phone Bank
Phone Number: (866) 868-3692
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available through the automated phone system during business hours. Automated assistance is also available in Cantonese, Korean, Mandarin, and Spanish. Call volume is often high. If you receive a busy signal or can't get through, call back later.
Submit a Ballot Application You can mail or drop off your completed application to your borough [Board of Elections Office](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03689) or email [Apply4Absentee@boe.nyc](mailto:Apply4Absentee@boe.nyc). After submitting your request, you can check the status of your application online. [Track your ballot request.](https://requestballot.vote.nyc/tracking)
Return an Absentee Ballot
You can return your completed ballot to the Board of Elections (BOE) by mail or in person. By Mail Mail your ballot to your [BOE borough office](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03689). To be counted, your absentee ballot must be: Postmarked no later than Election Day Received by the borough office no later than 7 days after Election Day The Postal Service recommends mailing your ballot at least 7 days before Election Day to ensure it is received on time. In Person Absentee voting in person starts as soon as the ballots are available (at least 32 days before an election) and ends on Election Day. You can drop off your ballot at a [BOE office](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03689) or any [poll site](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03691) during voting hours. Note that not all early voting sites will be available for drop-off on Election Day. You must deliver your ballot no later than 9 PM on Election Day.
Track Ballot
You can check the status of your ballot or ballot application. [Track your ballot.](https://requestballot.vote.nyc/tracking)
Get Help
You can get help with an absentee ballot or application. You can also make a complaint or report a concern about the voting process. By Email [AbsenteeHelp@boe.nyc](mailto:AbsenteeHelp@boe.nyc) By Phone

title: Poll Sites
body:
Poll sites provide voters with ballots and scanners to record their votes. Your poll site is based on your home address that’s currently registered with the NYC Board of Elections (BOE). Always check your poll site before you go. Locations can change between elections. Your early voting poll site may also be different than your Election Day site.
[Find your poll site.](https://findmypollsite.vote.nyc/)
How to Vote
Step 1: Check in at the poll site for your registered home address. A poll worker will look up your name on the list of registered voters or scan your Fast Pass. If you’re a first-time voter who didn’t provide identification when you registered, you need to show ID. Then sign your name in the poll book. Step 2: Go to the voting booth . You'll be given a paper ballot and directed to a privacy booth with a pen to mark your ballot. If you need disability assistance, just ask a poll worker. Step 3:  Mark the ballot with your choices . Step 4: Insert your ballot into the scanner to cast your vote. The scanner will record your vote. When polls close, the scanners will be used to count all votes cast.
What to Bring
For easy check-in, bring your Fast Pass tag or card. It's not required, but your Fast Pass has all your voting information, including districts. A poll site worker can scan it and check you in quickly. BOE will include the card and tag in the NYC Information Mailer before the election. Only first-time voters who did not provide identification when they registered to vote must show ID at the poll site. Acceptable forms of ID include: Valid photo ID A recent copy of a utility bill A recent copy of a bank statement A recent copy of a paycheck A recent copy of a government check or document
Accessibility
Every poll site has Accessibility Clerks. These are ADA-focused poll workers who help voters with disabilities upon request. You can also bring anyone with you into the voting booth to help you vote, except your employer or union representative. Accessible Entrances Every poll site has an entrance that is accessible to voters with disabilities. This entrance may have temporary equipment, such as mats and ramps, to ensure voters can safely access the site. Ballot Marking Devices To ensure all voters can mark and cast their ballot privately and independently, every poll site has at least one Ballot Marking Device (BMD) and one ADA Privacy Booth, as well as other aids such as magnifying sheets. The BMD is an electronic device that gives voters the ability to access and mark a ballot using a: Audio headset Touch screen Keypad Sip and puff device Rocker paddle
Language Assistance
You can bring anyone into the voting booth to interpret for you and help you vote, except your employer or union representative. As required by the Voting Rights Act, the Board of Elections (BOE) also provides interpretation services at certain poll sites in: Bengali Cantonese Korean Mandarin Spanish To find out if your poll site offers language assistance, call the BOE.
Agency: Board of Elections
Division: Vote Phone Bank
Phone Number: (866) 868-3692
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available through the automated phone system during business hours. Automated assistance is also available in Cantonese, Korean, Mandarin, and Spanish. Call volume is often high. If you receive a busy signal or can't get through, call back later.

title: Ranked Choice Voting
body:
Ranked Choice Voting (RCV) allows you to choose up to five candidates and rank them in order of preference on your ballot, instead of casting a vote for just one. Ranking other candidates doesn't hurt your first-choice candidate. Your second, third, and other choices will be considered only if your first choice doesn't win. You don't have to rank candidates on your ballot if you don't want to; you can still vote for just one candidate. But if you prefer some candidates over others, it can help the other choices on your list win if your first choice doesn't. [Learn more about RCV.](https://www.nycvotes.org/how-to-vote/ranked-choice-voting/) [Practice ranking candidates.](https://www.nycvotes.org/how-to-vote/ranked-choice-voting/practice-ballot/) Elections That Use Ranked Choice Voting RCV is used in primary and special elections in NYC. Voters can rank candidates for: Mayor Public Advocate Comptroller Borough President City Council RCV isn't used in general elections or for candidates for state or federal offices. How Votes Are Counted If a candidate gets a majority of first-choice votes (at least 50%), they are declared the winner. If no candidate gets a majority, the counting continues in rounds. In each round, the candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated. If your top-choice is eliminated, the next choice on your ballot is counted. The process is repeated until a candidate has at least 50% of the vote and is declared the winner. [Learn more about how votes are counted.](https://www.nycvotes.org/how-to-vote/ranked-choice-voting/how-votes-are-counted/#/)

title: Voter Rights
body:
You have the right to register to vote in New York City if you: Are a U.S. Citizen Have been a New York City resident for at least 30 days Are at least 18 years old (you may pre-register at 16 or 17, but can't vote until you're 18) Aren’t in prison for a felony conviction Haven't been judged mentally incompetent by a court Don’t claim the right to vote elsewhere You have the right to vote if you are registered to vote and meet age, citizenship, and residency requirements. You also have rights at poll sites and when voting. [Learn more about your rights as a voter.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/civicengagement/voting/know-your-rights.page)
Person in Custody
If you are in Department of Correction (DOC) custody, you can register to vote. You can also vote by absentee ballot unless you are in prison or jail for a felony. You are eligible to vote if you are awaiting arraignment, trial, or sentencing. You can get registration forms and absentee ballot applications in law libraries, counseling units, chaplains’ offices, and program wagons. When you register, use your permanent home address as your residence. Do not provide the address of the jail, except as your mailing address. Online [Learn about voting rights and registration for people in custody.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/probation/services/adult-court-voting-rights.page) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.
Person With a Criminal Record
All voters must meet age, citizenship, and residency requirements. You must also be registered to vote. If you have a criminal record, you may need to meet additional requirements. If you were in prison for a felony, the Board of Elections (BOE) was notified, and your name was removed from the voting rolls. If you completed your maximum sentence or were discharged from parole, you need to register again to vote. If you are on parole, you must get a Certificate of Relief or a Certificate of Conduct to restore your voting rights. You must also register again. To learn how to get these certificates, visit the [Certificate of Conduct](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02614) page. There are no additional requirements if you: Were convicted of a misdemeanor Are on probation Completed your maximum prison sentence Were discharged from parole on any charge Online [Learn about voting rights and registration for people with a criminal record.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/probation/services/adult-court-voting-rights.page) By Phone
Call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) for help.

title: Political Campaign Complaint
body:
NYC311 is part of New York City government and does not provide information or take complaints about political candidates or their election campaigns. The NYC Board of Elections and other City agencies also don’t take these complaints. Election campaigns and other non-profit organizations are not covered by the National Do Not Call Registry. You may contact the candidate's campaign office to make a complaint about the candidate, campaign workers, or the use of campaign tactics, such as robo-calls, direct mail, or television ads. To report political signs on public property, visit the [Poster or Sticker Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02140) page.
Electioneering
Electioneering is prohibited within 100 feet of a polling site entrance during an election. Electioneering includes: Distributing, wearing, or carrying political literature, posters, banners, or buttons Soliciting votes If you see or are made aware of anyone electioneering, you can report it to the Poll Site or call the borough [Board of Elections office](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03689). If posters are illegally placed on public property, you can file a report using the [Poster or Sticker Complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02140) page.

title: Mandatory Downspout Disconnection
body:
New York City property owners must ensure their downspouts (rain gutters) are not connected to the City’s sanitary sewer system. These connections are not allowed under [New York City’s Rules](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/newyorkcity/latest/NYCrules/0-0-0-26985) because they can overwhelm the sewer with rainwater and cause sewer back-ups in basements and flooding in neighborhoods. The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) plans to start enforcing this rule. If your downspouts are currently connected to the City’s sanitary sewer system, you must disconnect them. You can disconnect them yourself, or you can hire a contractor. [Get more information and guidance for DEP's Mandatory Downspout Disconnection.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/whats-new/downspout-disconnection.page) Tips For Redirecting Rainwater: Water should flow away from a building’s foundation. Water should not be directed onto neighboring properties or the sidewalk. Water can be captured in rain barrel for reuse, to water plants or wash cars. Downspouts can be extended to direct water under a deck, patio, or to a grassed or garden area. Rain gardens can be created and hard surfaces, like cement or patios, can be removed to allow water to infiltrate.
Certify Your Disconnection
You can certify your downspout disconnection from the sanitary sewer with the NYC Downspout Disconnection Certification Form. All submissions are subject to audit. [Access the NYC Downspout Disconnection Certification Form.](https://outreached.wufoo.com/forms/zj9t23i1150ftb/)

title: Income Savings Plan (ISP)
body:
The DHS Income Savings Plan (ISP) Program was created to help homeless clients build savings, transition out of shelters, and achieve self-sufficiency. Individuals who lived in a Department of Homeless Services shelter may have been required to participate in this program.  This program has ended.   Where you submit the request to reclaim the funds depends on how the funds were deposited.
Reclaim Funds Deposited to a Shelter ISP
If you deposited funds directly with a shelter through their ISP, please contact that shelter directly to reclaim the funds.  If you don’t remember the name or address of the shelter, you can request this information by email or by phone.  By Email Send an email to [RecordsAccess@dhs.nyc.gov](mailto:RecordsAccess@dhs.nyc.gov). Attach a completed DHS Record Release Authorization Form to your email. If you need to submit other supporting documents, include them in your email.  [Learn more and download the DHS Record Release Authorization Form on the DHS website.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dhs/about/contact.page#:~:text=Requests%20for%20Client%20Records) By Phone
Agency: Department of Homeless Services
Division: Office of the Ombudsman
Phone Number: (800) 994-6494
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available through the automated phone system during business hours.
Reclaim Funds Deposited to a DHS ISP
If you deposited the funds by mailing a check or money order to a DHS/DSS ISP, savings that were not claimed by program participants were transferred to the NYS Office of Unclaimed Funds.    If you meet the following criteria, you can submit a claim to request your savings:   You were enrolled in the program  You have exited the shelter   Have not yet claimed your savings  Did not receive a refund from DHS  [Learn more on the NYS Office of Unclaimed Funds website.](https://www.osc.ny.gov/unclaimed-funds)

title: Pharmacy Home Delivery Program
body:
Gotham Health patients can get prescriptions delivered directly to their home through the Pharmacy Home Delivery Program. To be eligible, you must have an active prescription from a Gotham Health provider. Patients will receive their medications within one business day, with helpful tracking details via text, and they will be required to sign for their medications upon arrival. The program delivers all prescription medications except for controlled substances and refrigerated medications. Patients can contact their health care provider to learn more.

title: Access NYC311 as a Person with a Disability
body:
Disability Access Survey Thank you for visiting our site. NYC311 is offering a survey to understand how people with disabilities experience our services. Our goal is to ensure NYC311 is accessible for all. It usually takes just a few minutes.  [Click here](https://nam.dcv.ms/zGlp4OSdc3) to take the Disability Access Survey.
Need something else? [Access City Agencies as a Person with Disability](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02321) for help accessing City services or programs [People with Disabilities Services](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02386) for information about Citywide programs for people with disabilities NYC311 is committed to providing the best customer service to all New Yorkers. We work to make our services accessible to everyone, including people with disabilities. Find the support that’s right for you. Select a category below that best describes your needs to see how NYC311 can help.
Blind or Low Vision
Our website supports screen readers. If you experience any issues, you can leave us [feedback](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02419) - it helps us improve! If you prefer assistance, an NYC311 representative can help by phone or text. You can dial 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) or text us at [311-692](sms:311692).
Deaf or Hard of Hearing
You can text us directly to reach a live NYC311 representative at [311-692](sms:311692). The NYC311 Text Team is trained to provide information and handle most NYC311 reports based on complexity. If you’re being asked to call 311 but are unable to, let the representative know. We’ll do our best to assist you by text. If you use 711, video relay services, or another relay provider, your relay operator can connect you with 311 by dialing 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675).
Speech Disabilities
You can text us directly to reach a live NYC311 representative at [311-692](sms:311692). The NYC311 Text Team is trained to provide information and handle most NYC311 reports based on complexity. If you’re being asked to call 311 but are unable to, let the representative know. We’ll do our best to assist you by text. If you use 711, video relay services, or another relay provider, your relay operator can connect you with 311 by dialing 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675).
Learning or Cognitive Disabilities
For those who prefer to use NYC311 online or the [NYC311 App](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01025), our content is intentionally written to be easy to understand. If there’s an area you think we could improve, let us know by providing [feedback](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02419). If self-service is challenging, a live NYC311 representative is here to assist with guided support 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.  Just text [311-692](sms:311692) and a representative will reply shortly. Our representatives are trained to communicate clearly, repeat information, and guide you at your pace.  Or call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to connect with us.
Mobility-Related Disabilities
NYC311 doesn’t have an in-person location, but we can be reached by: Calling us at [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) if you’re calling from outside of the five boroughs Texting us at [311-692](sms:311692) Sending us a direct message @nyc311 via [X](https://x.com/nyc311) or [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/nyc311/) Contacting us on [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/NYC311/) at NYC311 We are here for you 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year! If you have limited hand mobility, a voice assistant like Siri may help you place a call. When using a voice assistant to contact us, please be sure to say or enter our full number: 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) .
Request a Disability Accommodation
We understand access looks different for everyone. You can request help if you are a person with a disability trying to access a City service provided by NYC311 and need additional assistance. Ask for a disability-related accommodation by: Calling us at [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) Texting us at [311-692](sms:311692) Emailing us at [DisabilityAccess@311.nyc.gov](mailto:DisabilityAccess@311.nyc.gov)

title: Warming Centers
body:
Call 911 Call 911   to report a medical or health-related emergency, or a person in need of medical assistance.
During periods of extreme cold, warming centers may be activated across all boroughs, using both fixed sites and warming vehicles.  When the Department of Social Services (DSS)/Department of Homeless Services (DHS) activate [Code Blue](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01037), resources and outreach are available. When a Code Blue is in effect, over 50 NYC hospitals (including [public hospitals](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02793)), as well as DHS [drop-in centers](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02528) and [shelters](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02501), operate with a full open-door policy. This ensures every New Yorker has a safe, warm place to go. New Yorkers who see individuals they believe to be experiencing homelessness and in need should request [homeless outreach assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01037).

title: NYC Affordability Resources
body:
Life in New York City is full of possibilities, but everyday costs can add up quickly. This page brings together housing, food, health, transportation, and child care resources to help you lower your bills, meet essential needs, and make life more affordable. Other ways to get help Screen for over 30 programs on [ACCESS NYC](https://access.nyc.gov/eligibility/) to check which benefits you may be eligible for. [Reach out](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/about-nyc-311/#contact-us) if you can’t find what you need or have questions about a program—we’re here to help!
Housing + − Find an affordable place to live Finding housing that fits your budget can be challenging. Housing is generally defined as affordable if it costs one-third or less of your income. If you pay more, you’re not alone. Here’s where to look for affordable units with rents and maintenance costs that stay stable over time. [Housing lotteries Enter lotteries to rent or buy below market rate apartments. ›](https://housingconnect.nyc.gov/PublicWeb/) [Public housing Apply for a NYCHA apartment with rent based on your income. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01963) [Middle income housing developments Join waiting lists or enter lotteries for affordable rentals or co-ops. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/mitchell-lama-program.page) [Help buying your first home Receive up to $100,000 toward a down payment or closing costs of a new home. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/homefirst-down-payment-assistance-program.page) + − Pay rent and housing expenses Rising rents and housing costs can make it hard to keep up with bills. You may qualify for programs that help pay rent, utilities, and other housing expenses. Renters [Support to stay in your home Navigate your options and apply for rental assistance with a housing specialist. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01041) [Ongoing cash help Get monthly cash benefits for low-income tenants to pay for rent, utilities, and other basic needs. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03115) [Rent increase help Know your rights and what to do if your rent is going up. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/main/services/rent-increase-guide) [Rent freeze for seniors Stop future rent increases if you're 62 or older and live in a rent regulated apartment. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02289) [Rent freeze for people with disabilities Stop future rent increases if you have a disability and live in a rent regulated apartment. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02290) Homeowners [Financial assistance for homeowners Manage debt, apply for low-cost loans, and create a plan to keep your home. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03437) [Property tax savings Lower your property tax bill with exemptions and credits. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01795) [Property tax payment plan Pay your property taxes over time instead of all at once. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01248) + − Keep your housing Facing the loss of your home can be stressful, but you don’t have to navigate this alone. If you are at risk of eviction or foreclosure, there are programs and legal protections that may help you stay in your home and find a path forward.     Facing an immediate housing crisis? If you’re being evicted, contact [Homebase](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01041) for alternatives to shelter. If your home is unsafe due to domestic violence, contact [Safe Horizon](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01217) for emergency housing. [Support to stay in your home Navigate your options and apply for rental assistance with a housing specialist. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01041) [Emergency cash help Apply for a one-time grant to pay back rent, stop utility shutoff, or meet an unexpected expense. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01104)[Legal help for tenants Get referrals to free legal services and help to understand your rights from the Tenant Helpline. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/site/mayorspeu/programs/contact-the-tenant-support-unit.page) [Property tax pause Defer property tax payments if you're experiencing hardship. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03188) [Foreclosure and loan assistance Access financial and legal services if you’re at risk of losing your home. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01401)
Food + − Get help to pay for groceries You can get help paying for groceries by enrolling in a food benefits program. [Money to buy food Get monthly SNAP benefits loaded onto a card that you can use to buy groceries at many stores and markets. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01018) [Nutrition support for families Get help buying healthy food and formula if you’re pregnant, a new parent, or caring for a child under 5. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01702) [Extra money for fruits and vegetables Earn a dollar-for-dollar match to spend on produce when you use SNAP. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03564) + − Pick up free food Free food is available to all New Yorkers who need it. [Food for your household Pick up groceries to use at home from a neighborhood food pantry. ›](https://finder.nyc.gov/foodhelp/) [Food packages for older adults Pick up healthy foods to supplement your diet from distribution sites if you’re 60 or older. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01477) + − Find free meals You can learn about programs that provide free prepared meals to eligible New Yorkers. For everyone [Community meals Sit down for a free hot or ready-to-eat meal at soup kitchens and mobile meal vans. ›](https://finder.nyc.gov/foodhelp/) For children [Free breakfast and lunch at school Enjoy free, nutritious meals every school day. ›](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/school-life/food/school-meals) [Summer meals Pick up free meals during the summer at schools, pools, parks, and other places. No sign-up required. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01374) For older adults [Group meals Share a meal with others who are 60 or older at an older adult center. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02760) [Meal delivery Get meals delivered to your home if you’re 60 or older and can’t go out to shop or cook at home. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02252)
Health + − Find health insurance Health insurance plans Health insurance can help cover doctor’s visits, medications, and assistive devices like hearing aids or glasses. If you don’t qualify for coverage through your workplace, there are other options that may fit your budget. [Free or low-cost Sign up for Medicaid if you have a low income or a specific health need, like a disability. ›](https://access.nyc.gov/programs/medicaid/) [For children Sign up for Child Health Plus if your child needs health insurance and doesn’t qualify for Medicaid. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02093) [For seniors or people with disabilities Sign up for Medicare if you're 65 or older or have a qualifying disability. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01674) Navigating your options Choosing a health plan can feel overwhelming. Trained specialists can help you find a plan, check your eligibility, or renew your coverage. [Enrollment support Connect with a health insurance specialist to explore public and private health coverage options. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03167) [Medicare plan counseling Get help to find the right Medicare plan for you. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dfta/services/health-insurance-assistance.page) [Veteran health care Connect with organizations that support the health needs of veterans, service members, and their families. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/site/veterans/services/health.page)   + − Access free or low-cost health services Medical debt isn’t the only option for uninsured New Yorkers who need health care. If you don’t qualify for health insurance or missed the enrollment deadline, you may still be able to get affordable care with transparent pricing. [Health care if you have no insurance Access free or low-cost care if you can’t afford or don’t qualify for public or private health insurance. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03317) [Health screenings Get screened for chronic conditions such as asthma, cancer, diabetes, heart disease, and mental illness. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02769) [Sexual and reproductive health Get sexual health services, including STI testing, vaccines, and contraception. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02998) [Dental care Find clinics that offer low-cost dental and oral health services. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02903) [Mental health support Get free, 24/7 confidential mental health support by text, chat, or phone for anxiety, depression, or substance use. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01682)
Transportation + − Save on public transit Save money on your commute and other everyday trips by subway, bus, ferry, or paratransit. [50% off subway, bus, or paratransit fares Ride for half-price on subways, buses, and Access-A-Ride if you have a low income. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03181) [50% off for riders 65 or older or with disabilities Ride for half-price if you're 65 or older or have a qualifying disability. ›](https://www.mta.info/fares-tolls/subway-bus/reduced-fare) [Free rides for paratransit customers Get up to four free subway or bus rides per day if you're enrolled in Access-A-Ride. ›](https://www.mta.info/accessibility/access-a-ride/four-free-rides) [Discounted ferry tickets Ride NYC Ferry for $1.45 if you're eligible for a reduced fare. ›](https://www.ferry.nyc/discount/) [Ferry discounts for high school students Get discounts on NYC Ferry when traveling to school. ›](https://www.ferry.nyc/student-discount/) [Pre-tax transit benefits Use pre-tax income to pay for transit if your employer offers commuter benefits. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/workers/workersrights/commuter-benefits-law-for-workers.page) + − Get free rides for essential trips You may qualify for free transportation to access health care, older adult services, and other essential needs. [Rides for older adults Get free rides to older adult centers, medical appointments, grocery stores, and more. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02307) [Non-emergency medical transportation Get free rides to medical appointments if you receive Medicaid. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01583) + − Reduce driving costs Driving can be expensive. These options can help reduce the cost of owning and using a car.   [Discounts on bridge and tunnel tolls Use E-ZPass and enroll in a discount plan to pay less on tolls. ›](https://www.panynj.gov/bridges-tunnels/en/e-zpass.html#plansDiscounts) [Discount on congestion toll Get a reduced toll or tax credit if you have a low income. ›](https://www.mta.info/fares-tolls/tolls/congestion-relief-zone/discounts-exemptions)[Disability exemption from congestion toll Avoid the Congestion Relief Zone toll if you have a disability and can't use public transit. ›](https://www.mta.info/fares-tolls/tolls/congestion-relief-zone/discounts-exemptions) [No fees at parking meters Park without paying the meter if you have a disability parking permit. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01243) [Carsharing Use carshare instead of owning a car to save on insurance, maintenance, and storage. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02610) [Carpool ride matching Share your ride with others and split gas and toll costs. ›](https://511nyrideshare.org/carpool) [Free car seat Get a free child's car seat if your family can't afford one. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03532) + − Save on biking and e-scooters Bikes and e-scooters are low-cost ways to get around the city. You can find discounts and free gear to make riding easier, safer, and more affordable. [Free bike helmets and lights Pick up a free helmet or bike light at a giveaway event. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/bicyclists/bike-events.shtml) [$5 a month Citi Bike membership Sign up for a discounted membership if you get SNAP, live in NYCHA, or belong to a select credit union. ›](https://citibikenyc.com/community-programs/reducedfare) [E-scooter share discount Get a discounted e-scooter share membership for rides in select neighborhoods. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03442)
Child Care + − Find affordable child care Learn about free or low-cost child care and early education programs. [Free or low-cost infant care Apply for child care for infants 6 weeks to 2 years old for free or a small fee. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/content/childcarehub/pages/discover-child-care/infant-extended-day-and-year) [Free child care for low-income families Apply for free, full-day child care and early education for children from birth to age 5. ›](https://headstart.gov/) [Free or low-cost toddler care and 2-K Apply for child care for toddlers 13 months to 3 years old for free or a small fee. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/content/childcarehub/pages/discover-child-care/toddler-2-k-programs) [Free or low-cost 3-K Apply for early childhood education programs the year your child turns 3 for free or a small fee. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/content/childcarehub/pages/discover-child-care/3-k) [Free or low-cost pre-K Apply for early childhood education programs the year your child turns 4 for free or a small fee. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/content/childcarehub/pages/discover-child-care/pre-k) [Child care for student parents Get free child care and support while finishing high school. ›](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/school-life/special-situations/services-for-student-parents) + − Get help paying for child care A child care voucher can cover some or all your child care costs. If you qualify, you can use it year-round for up to 24 hours a day with a provider you choose. [Child care voucher with Cash Assistance Cover the full cost of child care if you receive Cash Assistance. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/child-care-benefits.page) [Child care voucher waitlist Join the waitlist to receive full or partial help paying for child care. ›](https://mycity.nyc.gov/s/childcarelanding?language=en_US&LanguageCode=en_US) + − Find after school and summer programs You can sign up for free or low-cost programs outside of school hours. These programs help kids learn, have fun, build skills, and stay active.   [Free after school programs Get homework help, sports, and enrichment through school-based programs for kids 4 and up. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02550) [Free after school parks program Enroll in after school programs at parks and recreation centers for kids 6 and up. ›](https://www.nycgovparks.org/programs/recreation/afterschool)[Free, full-day summer learning Enroll in academic and enrichment programs for students in grades K-8. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03035) [Lower-cost summer camp at NYC Parks Enroll in sports, arts and crafts, nature exploration, and more at summer camp for kids 6 and up. ›](https://www.nycgovparks.org/events/summer-camp) + − Claim tax credits for child care You may qualify for tax credits that help offset the cost of child care. To claim them, you’ll need to file a tax return. [NYC Tax Prep](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02303) offers free tax filing help. [Federal child care credit Get up to $3,000 back in child care expenses for one child under 13, or up to $6,000 for two or more. ›](https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/child-and-dependent-care-credit-information) [NY State child care credit Get a credit for child care expenses for children under 13. ›](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pit/credits/child_and_dependent_care_credit.htm) [NYC child care credit Get a credit for child care expenses if you earn under $30,000 and have a child under 4. ›](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pit/credits/new_york_city_credits.htm) + − Use paid leave to care for your child If you work in New York City, you may have the right to job-protected, paid time off to care for your child. Learn your rights and how to use paid leave. [Paid leave to care for your child Take up to 56 hours of paid time off from work each year to care for your child. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02909) [Paid leave to bond with a new child Take up to 12 weeks of paid time off from work to care for a child under 1. ›](https://paidfamilyleave.ny.gov/paid-family-leave-bonding)

title: Snow or Ice on Building
body:
Call 911 Call 911   to report immediate danger including: Falling ice or snow that is an immediate hazard An accident that just occurred and caused injury
New York City property owners and construction site managers are responsible for securing their properties from hazardous conditions, including melting or falling ice and snow. The Department of Buildings (DOB) will take enforcement action if a building or site is not safely secured. Residential and Commercial Buildings Property owners should take all precautionary measures including, but not limited to: Securing and clearing roofs, awnings, umbrellas and overhangs of melting snow and ice. Removing ice and snow from tree limbs and other structures. Ensuring gutters are clear of debris to allow drainage. Construction Sites Builders, contractors, and developers should take all precautionary measures to secure construction sites, including but not limited to: Clearing icicles and snow masses from sidewalk sheds and supported and suspended scaffolds. Clearing melting snow and ice from roofs, overhangs, and gutters. Clearing debris from gutters and spouts to allow proper drainage. Clearing snow and ice from sidewalks, walkways and public areas surrounding a construction site. Call 911 if there is an emergency on a construction site. You can report snow or ice on a building or construction site. Include in your report:  What is falling Which side of the building it's falling from What part of the structure it's falling from

title: Open Grid Security Gates
body:
New York City street-level stores and businesses must comply with new storefront security grille (gate) regulations outlined in the City's code. A storefront security-grille or security gate allows for: 24-hour visibility into a store or business Greater visual access for security Brighter, safer, and more welcoming NYC By July 1, 2026 , all existing and new security gates in the City in buildings must comply with the [NYC Local Law 75 of 2009](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/local_laws/ll75of2009.pdf) requirement where 70 percent of the area covered by the security gate must be visible from the sidewalk. This applies to buildings with occupancies designated as: Occupancy Group B (Business) Occupancy Group M (Mercantile) Buildings in Historic districts and those designated as Landmark are exempt.
