title: SNAP Benefit Management
body:
You can learn how to use and keep your SNAP benefits. New to SNAP? [Learn how to apply](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01018). Time to recertify for SNAP? [Learn how to recertify and where to get help](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03718). Need help with your EBT card? [Find EBT card services](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02340).
Use SNAP to Buy Food
You access SNAP benefits through an Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card. Activating Your EBT Card You need to activate the card before using it. Learn how to activate and manage your card on the [EBT Card Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02340) page. Where to Shop You can use your EBT card to buy food at participating stores and farmers markets. Some online stores also accept SNAP for delivery orders. Benefits may be used to pay for approved items, but not for delivery fees. [Find stores, markets, and websites that accept SNAP.](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/retailer-locator) What You Can Buy You can use SNAP benefits to buy most food items. You can’t use SNAP to buy: Alcoholic beverages or tobacco products Pet supplies Cleaning products, paper products, toiletries, or cooking utensils Items for food preservation, freezer containers, or food wrapping paper Medicine, vitamins, or minerals [Learn more about eligible purchases.](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/eligible-food-items) How to Pay Once you’ve activated your new EBT card, you can use it to buy groceries. This works like a debit card. Just swipe the card and then enter your PIN in the machine at the checkout line. After making your purchase, you should put a freeze on your card. Freezing your card when you’re not using it can help protect you from electronic benefit fraud. Learn more on the [EBT Card Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02340) page. Unused Benefits SNAP benefits carry over from month to month with one exception. If you haven't used your SNAP benefits for 274 consecutive days, any remaining SNAP benefits will be removed from your EBT card. If this happens, your SNAP benefits cannot be reissued.
Manage Your EBT Card and SNAP Case
EBT Card Services Your EBT card works a lot like a debit card. Like a bank account, you can: Track spending Check your balance Get a replacement card Update settings [ebtEDGE](https://www.ebtedge.com/gov/portal/PortalHome.do) is a free and easy way to manage your EBT card. Learn more about EBT card services on the [EBT Card Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02340) page. Keeping Your SNAP Case Up-to-Date When you apply for SNAP, you’re assigned a case number. Your case links your household information, your applications, and actions taken when you’re in the program, like recertification. Part of managing your SNAP benefits is updating your case when your situation changes. It’s also important that HRA has your current contact information. The easiest way to view and update your case details is online, but you can also do this by fax, mail, or in person. Online Use the [ACCESS HRA website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/) or the [ACCESS HRA mobile app.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page) By Phone
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Division: DSS OneNumber
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.
In Person
Go to any [SNAP center](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/locations/snap-locations.page).
By Mail SNAP P.O. Box 29008 Brooklyn, NY 11202 By Fax (917) 639-2544
Benefit Deposit Schedule SNAP benefits are added to your account at around the same time each month. The day money is deposited into your account is called your benefit schedule. This day may change from month to month and from year to year. You can check your current schedule and past deposits online or by phone. You’ll need your 19-digit EBT card number. Online [Visit the ebtEDGE website.](https://www.ebtedge.com/gov/portal/PortalHome.do) Download the ebtEDGE mobile app for free through the [Google Play Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.fis.ebtedge) or [Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/ebtedge/id1398046228). By Phone
Agency: New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance
Division: Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) Customer Service
Phone Number: (888) 328-6399
Business Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week
Staff is available at all times through the automated phone system.
Protect Your Benefits
EBT scams are common. Some people will try to steal your benefits or trick you into giving your personal information. Personal information includes your Social Security number, bank information, EBT card number, or PIN number. Follow these tips to keep your card secure. Freeze your card when you’re not using it with ebtEDGE. Only unfreeze it right before you buy something. [Learn how to freeze your card](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02340). Check card readers for credit card skimmers. Keep your PIN safe. Only you should enter it. Always check and keep your receipts. Learn more about benefit theft on the [Electronic Benefit Theft and Scams](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03716) page.
Report Changes
If your situation changes during your certification period, you may be required to report changes to your household. This is called a Case Change request. This includes changes to: Income Savings Address Who lives in your household Employment You will need to submit proof of your reported changes. If you are due to recertify your SNAP benefits in the next 75 days, report the change as part of your recertification instead. Some SNAP participants will also receive a Periodic Report in the mail halfway through their certification period. This is usually every six months. If you do not report changes or return your Periodic Report form, your benefits will stop, and your case will close. [Learn more about reporting changes.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/snap-faq.page) Report Online Use the [ACCESS HRA website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/). After you submit the form, upload your required documents using the [ACCESS HRA Mobile App](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page). Report by Mail SNAP P.O. Box 29008 Brooklyn, NY 11202 Report in Person
Go to any [SNAP center](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/locations/snap-locations.page).
Work Requirements
To receive SNAP, you might need to work, volunteer, do job training, or participate in other activities. There are two types of work requirements: General requirements apply if you’re age 16 to 59 and able to work. ABAWD requirements may also apply if you’re age 18 to 64 and don’t have dependents. General Work Requirements Most people ages 16 to 59 must meet general work requirements to keep their benefits. You may be exempt if you're doing one of the following: Working at least 30 hours per week or earning at least $217.50 per week Studying at least half-time Getting unemployment benefits Participating in addiction treatment Meeting TANF (Cash Assistance) work requirements Getting SSI (Supplemental Security Income) [Learn more about general work requirements for SNAP.](https://otda.ny.gov/programs/snap/work-requirements.asp) Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) Requirements As of March 1, 2026, some SNAP recipients must comply with new ABAWD work requirements to keep their benefits. Generally, you’re considered an ABAWD if you: Are age 18 through 64, and Don’t live with a child under 14, and Don’t have a physical or mental barrier that prevents you from working HRA will inform you if you or anyone in your household needs to meet SNAP work requirements. You can submit proof that you meet the SNAP work requirements on the [ACCESS HRA website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/). [Learn more about ABAWD work rules.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/able-bodied-adults-without-dependents.page) [Read FAQs about SNAP work requirements.](https://access.nyc.gov/snap-work-requirements/)
Get Help
Help with Your EBT Card For EBT card services, go to the [EBT Card Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02340) page.
Case-Specific Questions Online You can track applications, get case details, and learn about next steps you need to take through the [ACCESS HRA website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/) or the [ACCESS HRA Mobile App](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page). By Phone

title: Electronic Benefit Theft and Scams
body:
Some people will try to steal your SNAP and Cash Assistance benefits or scam you into giving your account and personal information. They use tactics like pretending to be from a government agency or tampering with devices to copy your EBT card details. This is called electronic benefit theft or fraud.
Types of Electronic Theft or Scams
Skimming  is when someone puts an overlay on a store’s card-swiping machine to copy EBT, credit, and debit card account information. The stolen information is used to make fake cards called “clones.” The scammers will then steal money from the accounts. Skimming can happen anywhere you swipe your EBT card. Your benefits can be stolen through skimming even if you always have possession of your EBT card. Imposter scams  happen when thieves pretend to be from a government agency, such as the Department of Social Services (DSS) or the Human Resources Administration (HRA). This is sometimes called “third-party misrepresentation.” A caller or recorded message will ask for your account information, such as an EBT number or PIN. They may say you’re at risk of losing your benefits if you don’t. If you don’t currently receive SNAP, you might also get contacted by imposters that say you were chosen to receive SNAP. Spoofing  refers to the tactic of falsifying data to gain access to your personal information. Scammers may forge their caller ID or email in order to impersonate DSS or HRA. Never give out personal information over the phone. Hang up and contact the organization through a verified number.   Phishing  is when thieves trick people into clicking on a link that allows them to access your account information. This usually happens through text or email. [Learn more about EBT scams.](https://otda.ny.gov/workingfamilies/EBT-scam-alert.asp)
How to Protect Yourself
Freeze your card using [ebtEDGE](https://login5.fisglobal.com/idp/EBTEdge_NCH/?client_id) when you’re not using it. Only unfreeze it right before you buy something. Learn more on the [EBT Card Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02340) page. Check store machines for credit card skimmers before you use them. Keep your EBT card and account information private. Personal information includes your Social Security number, bank information, EBT card number, and/or PIN. Never share this with anyone over the phone or by text. Track your account history and keep your receipts. If you think you received a scam call, hang up. If you think you received a scam text, do not reply. Just delete the message. Contact HRA directly if you don’t know if a request for information was real.

Report Theft or Scams
Contact EBT Customer Service immediately if you know or suspect: Your benefits have been stolen Your card or card number has been stolen Someone you didn’t authorize has access to your PIN Someone accessed information about your identity If you think you gave away your personal information to a scammer, you should also file an [identity theft](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02533) report. Cargo drones will transport non-hazardous, non-sensitive, and non-biological cargo between the Downtown Skyport (Pier 6) in Manhattan and the Brooklyn Marine Terminal (Pier 7). The focus of the pilot is to test whether drones can be used to deliver goods in the future. The pilot program will run on weekdays from 9 AM to 5 PM through April 2027. title: SNAP Recertification
body:
To keep getting SNAP benefits, you must recertify to confirm you’re still eligible. Usually, you must recertify once a year. You’ll receive a notice in the mail or an alert on ACCESS HRA when it’s time to recertify.  It’s important to recertify as early as possible so you don’t miss a SNAP payment. You can recertify as early as 60 days before the end of your current recertification period. [Recertify for SNAP on ACCESS HRA.](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/) Already get SNAP? [Manage your benefits](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03714) Steps to Recertify Fill out a recertification form . Answer questions about your household, income, and expenses. The fastest, easiest way is on the [ACCESS HRA website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/). Complete an interview by phone or in person. No appointment is needed. A SNAP eligibility worker will review your form with you to ensure that it’s ready for processing. They will also help you figure out which documents you need to provide. Submit required documents . You’ll find out during your interview which ones you need. Wait for a decision . This can take up to 30 days. You can check status on [ACCESS HRA](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/).
Recertify for SNAP
Ready to recertify? The first step is to submit a recertification form. The fastest way to recertify is online using [ACCESS HRA](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/). Recertification forms are available in many languages. A simplified form is available if no one in the household has earned income and all adults have a disability or are age 60 and older.  Online [Recertify for SNAP on ACCESS HRA](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/). After you submit the recertification, upload your required documents using the [ACCESS HRA Mobile App](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page). In Person
Go to any [SNAP center](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/locations/snap-locations.page).
By Mail or Fax If you prefer to fill out a paper form, you can get it in three ways: [Download and print a recertification form](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/snap-application-documents.page). Pick up a recertification form at any [SNAP center](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/locations/snap-locations.page). Request a recertification form by phone.
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Division: DSS OneNumber
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.
Mail Your Recertification Mail the completed recertification form and copies of required documents to: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program P.O. Box 29008 Brooklyn, NY 11202 Fax Your Recertification Fax your completed recertification form and required documents to (917) 639-2544.
Eligibility Interview
After you submit your recertification, you must have an eligibility interview. You can do this by phone or at a SNAP center. SNAP interviews take about 30 minutes. During the interview, a SNAP eligibility worker will review your recertification with you to ensure that it’s complete, correct, and ready for processing. They will also help you figure out which documents you need to provide. No appointment is necessary. When you’re ready, just call or visit a SNAP center to have the interview. By Phone The fastest way to get your benefits is to call for your interview. [Get tips for calling HRA.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/ondemandinfo.page)
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Division: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Interview Phone Line
Phone Number: (718) 762-7669
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8:30 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages.
In Person Go to any [SNAP center](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/locations/snap-locations.page) and tell them you need an in-person interview.
Required Documents
To complete your recertification, you need to submit proof that you’re eligible for SNAP. The easiest way is to take photos of your documents and upload files using the [ACCESS HRA Mobile App](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page). You can do this at any time, but it’s best to wait until after your eligibility interview with HRA. Sometimes, HRA can check your information without needing documents. Your interviewer will help you figure out which documents you need to submit. Eligibility Factor Document Examples Identity Driver license Photo ID Address Lease Utility bill Rent receipt Mortgage statement Social Security Social Security numbers for all applicants Proof of application for a Social Security number Income Pay stubs Employer wage statement Government benefit letters Expenses Utility bills Rent and mortgage Child care or child support payments Out-of-pocket medical expenses, if you're 60 or older or get federal disability benefits [Download a full list of required documents.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hra/downloads/pdf/services/snap/eligibility_factors_and_suggested_documentation_guide.pdf)
Recertification Status and Processing
After your interview is finished and you’ve submitted your documents, HRA will start to process your recertification. It can take up to 30 days for HRA to review it and make a decision. Getting a Decision If your recertification is approved, HRA will mail you a letter to tell you. If you signed up for notifications, you will also get an email and text message. If your recertification is rejected , HRA will mail you a letter to tell you why. You can reapply at any time. If your recertification wasn’t approved because you’re ineligible and your situation hasn’t changed, look into [other food help programs](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03304). If you think HRA’s decision was wrong, you can: Visit a [SNAP center](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/locations/snap-locations.page) and request an informal conference Request a [Fair Hearing](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02943) Check Status You can track your recertification and get notifications through the [ACCESS HRA website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/) or the [ACCESS HRA mobile app](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page). If you can’t use ACCESS HRA, you can call for status.  Please note: Processing only starts after you finish your interview and send all documents. It can take up to 30 days to process your case. If it’s been less than 30 days since you recertified, HRA’s phone line won’t have more information than you see on ACCESS HRA.
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Division: DSS OneNumber
Phone Number: (718) 557-1399
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
Staff is available during business hours (except on City holidays). You can get help in most languages. The automated phone system is always available.
Get Help
Help with Your EBT Card For EBT card services, go to the [EBT Card Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02340) page.
Help to Recertify Hunger Free NYC The Hunger Free NYC Benefits Access Call Center (BACC) can screen you for SNAP eligibility. They can also help you file a SNAP recertification.
Agency: Human Resources Administration
Division: Hunger Free NYC Benefits Access Call Center
Phone Number: (646) 355-1475
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
SNAP Centers SNAP centers offer walk-in customer service. All centers are accessible to people who use wheelchairs. [Find a SNAP center near you.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/locations/snap-locations.page)
Community Organizations Community Based Organizations (CBOs) can help you complete SNAP recertifications and screen you for eligibility. Some locations can also help you submit your documents electronically. [Find a Community Based Organization.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/partners/find-a-partner-organization.page)
People with Disabilities If you have a disability, medical condition, or mental health condition that makes it hard for you to recertify for SNAP benefits, you can request a reasonable accommodation. Learn more on the [Access City Agencies as a Person with a Disability](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02321) page.
Case-Specific Questions Online You can track recertifications, get case details, and learn about next steps you need to take through the [ACCESS HRA website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/) or the [ACCESS HRA Mobile App](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page). By Phone

title: Hantavirus Information
body:
Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome is a rare but potentially serious disease. People exposed to rodents-infested environments are at the greatest risk for infections. The best way to prevent hantavirus is to [control rodents both inside and outside the home](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/rats.page). You should take precautions when exposed to rodent infested environments. There are no reported cases of Hantavirus in NYC. [Learn more about the Hantavirus, including prevention and symptoms.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/hantavirus-infection.page)

title: FIFA World Cup 2026
body:
New York and New Jersey are hosting eight FIFA World Cup 2026 matches, including the Final. The New York New Jersey Host Committee is the official organizing body working alongside FIFA. [Learn more about the FIFA World Cup 2026.](https://nynjfwc26.com/) Free, official NYNJ Fan Events will take place across all five boroughs. These events will bring live match viewings, cultural programming, local businesses and interactive experiences directly to New Yorkers at no cost.   Bronx NYNJ World Cup 26 Bronx Fan Zone Bronx Terminal Market June 13–14 Matchday programming and local cultural programming Brooklyn NYNJ World Cup 26 Brooklyn Fan Zone Brooklyn Bridge Park June 13 - July 19 Daily programming and match viewings Manhattan NYNJ World Cup 26 & Telemundo Fan Village at Rockefeller Center Rockefeller Center July 6–19 Daily programming; extended hours during Finals Week Queens NYNJ World Cup 26 Queens Group Stage HQ USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, Flushing Meadows June 11–27 Daily programming and match viewings Staten Island NYNJ World Cup 26 Staten Island Fan Zone Staten Island University Hospital Community Park June 29–July 2 Daily programming and evening match viewings   Additional details on programming, partners and talent will be announced in the coming weeks. For more information, visit [nynjfwc26.com](https://nynjfwc26.com/).   [Read the official press release announcing the citywide Fan Events.](https://www.nyc.gov/mayors-office/news/2026/04/mayor-mamdani--governor-hochul-and-fifa-world-cup-2026-nynj-host)
Ticket Lottery for NYC Residents
The City of New York, in partnership with the NYNJ Host Committee, has secured 1,000 affordable tickets to the FIFA World Cup 2026 for New Yorkers. The tickets are $50 per seat and include free round-trip bus transportation to MetLife Stadium. The program covers the five group stage matches and two knockout round matches. Approximately 150 tickets will be allocated per game. All current New York City residents over 15 years of age may enter the lottery for the chance to purchase tickets. Winners will be selected randomly. Entry opens at [www.regnyctix.com](https://www.regnyctix.com) on Monday, May 25 at 10 AM and closes Saturday, May 30 at midnight. New Yorkers may enter once per day, with a daily cap of 50,000 entries. Winners will be notified Wednesday, June 3, and may purchase up to two tickets each. To prevent scalping, tickets will be nontransferable and distributed directly to winners at the official boarding location on the day of each match. Free round-trip transportation from the pickup location to the NYNJ Stadium will be included for every winner.

title: NYC Grocery Stores
body:
NYC Grocery Stores are City-owned stores designed to deliver affordable, high-quality, culturally relevant, and accessible groceries that provide meaningful savings for New Yorkers and strengthen neighborhood food access citywide. One location is planned for each borough as part of this initiative. All five are expected to open by 2029. The Peninsula will be the Bronx location and is anticipated to open in 2027. La Marqueta will be the Manhattan location and is expected to open in 2029. [Get updates and learn more about NYC Grocery Stores.](https://edc.nyc/program/nyc-groceries)

title: Enhanced Energy Affordability Program (EEAP)
body:
Need something else? [Electric Service and Billing](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02425) [Gas Service and Billing](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02446) The New York Enhanced Energy Affordability Program (EEAP) is a 2-year pilot program that provides monthly discounts for income-qualified households across New York State. Eligible customers can receive assistance based on their household size, income level, and utility provider. The EEAP application is available to customers of Central Hudson Gas & Electric, Con Edison, National Fuel, National Grid, NYSEG, Orange & Rockland and RG&E.
Eligibility
You may be eligible if: Have an active residential electric or natural gas account with a participating New York utility Have a household income below the maximum, which varies by location and household size Provide complete documentation of your entire household’s income for the prior month [Learn more about eligibility.](https://nyeeap.com/faq)
How to Apply
You can apply for the EEAP online, by phone, by mail or through fax. Online Applying online is the fastest method. [Apply online.](https://nyeeap.com/program) By Phone You must speak to an agent during business hours to apply by phone.
Agency: New York Department of Public Service
Phone Number: (877) 400-2501
Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 8 AM - 5 PM
By Mail and Fax You can download a paper application to send in by mail or fax. Applications are currently available in: [English](https://nyeeap.com/static/customer/ny_eeap/paper_application_20260128.pdf) [Spanish](https://nyeeap.com/static/customer/ny_eeap/paper_application_20260128_spanish.pdf) [Portuguese](https://nyeeap.com/static/customer/ny_eeap/paper_application_20260128_portuguese.pdf) You can mail your completed application to: CLEAResult – NY EEAP 16350 Felton Rd. Lansing, MI 48906 You can fax your completed application to 517-580-5123.

title: 2026 Primary Election
body:
▲Top
A Primary Election is being held on Tuesday, June 23 . [Early Voting](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03687) runs from Saturday, June 13 to Sunday, June 21 .   [Find your poll site](https://findmypollsite.vote.nyc/)
On This Page Key Dates and Deadlines Ways to Vote Poll Site Information What's on Your Ballot Voter Resources
Key Dates and Deadlines Election Day Election Day is Tuesday, June 23. Poll sites are open from 6 AM to 9 PM. If you are in line by 9 PM, you can stay in line to cast a ballot. Early Voting Early Voting runs from June 13 to June 21. Date Voting Hours Saturday, June 13 9 AM to 5 PM Sunday, June 14 9 AM to 5 PM Monday, June 15 9 AM to 5 PM Tuesday, June 16 10 AM to 8 PM Wednesday, June 17 10 AM to 8 PM Thursday, June 18 8 AM to 4 PM Friday, June 19 9 AM to 5 PM Saturday, June 20 9 AM to 5 PM Sunday, June 21 9 AM to 5 PM Early Mail and Absentee Voting Deadlines Date Deadline June 13 Last day for the Board of Elections to receive an application or letter of application by mail, online portal, email, or fax for a ballot. June 22 Last day to apply in person for an absentee or early mail ballot. June 23 Last day to postmark an absentee or early mail ballot. It must be received no later than June 30. June 23 Last day to deliver the ballot in person. Voter Registration Deadlines Date Deadline June 8 Last day to request a change of address on your voter registration. The Board of Elections must receive your application by this date. June 13 Last day a mail application must be received by the Board of Elections to be eligible to vote in the Primary Election. June 13 Last day to register to vote in person to be eligible to vote in the Primary Election. Election Timeline   June 8 Last day to update your address on your voter registration [Learn how to update your registration](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03252)   June 13 Last day to register to vote [Learn how to register](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03252)   June 13 Early Voting begins [Learn how to vote early](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03687)   June 21 Last day of Early Voting   June 22 Last day to apply for an early mail or absentee ballot [Learn about early mail voting](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03687) [Learn about absentee voting](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03688)   June 23 Election Day   June 23 Last day to drop off or postmark your early mail or absentee ballot
Ways to Vote In New York City, registered voters have three ways to cast their ballot. 1. Vote at a Poll Site During Early Voting (June 13 to June 21) On Election Day (June 23) You must vote at the specific poll site assigned to our home address. Your Early Voting poll site may be different than your Election Day poll site. [Learn more about voting at poll sites.](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03691) 2. Vote by Early Mail Ballot You can request an early mail ballot for any reason. The Board of Elections (BOE) will mail you the ballot and a pre-paid envelope. Then you can return the ballot by mail or drop it off at a poll site during voting hours or at a BOE office. [Learn more and request an early mail ballot.](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03687) 3. Vote by Absentee Ballot If you can’t make it to the polls in person for a specific reason, like illness or travel, you can request an absentee ballot. The Board of Elections (BOE) will mail you the ballot and a pre-paid envelope. Then you can return the ballot by mail or drop it off at a poll site during voting hours or at a BOE office. [Learn more and request an absentee ballot.](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03688)
Poll Site Information Always look up your poll site before you go—your poll site may change from election to election. Your early voting poll site can also be different than your Election Day site..   [Find your poll site](https://findmypollsite.vote.nyc/)   What to Bring For easy check-in, bring your Fast Pass tag or card. It's not required, but your Fast Pass has all your voting information, including districts. BOE will mail them to you before the election. You only have to bring ID if you are a first-time voter who didn't give your identification when you registered to vote. Acceptable forms of ID include: Valid photo ID A recent copy of a utility bill A recent copy of a bank statement A recent copy of a paycheck A recent copy of a government check or document How to Vote at a Poll Site   Check in A poll worker will look up your name on the list of registered voters or scan your Fast Pass. If you’re a first-time voter who didn’t provide identification when you registered, you need to show ID. Then sign your name in the poll book. 1 Go to the voting booth You'll get a paper ballot and be directed to a privacy booth with a pen to mark your ballot. If you need disability assistance, just ask a poll worker. 2 Mark the ballot with your choices 3 Insert your ballot into the scanner You're done! The scanner will record your vote. When polls close, the scanners will be used to count all votes cast. Don't forget to pick up an official "I Voted" sticker before you leave! 4 Disability and Language Acccess All poll sites have: An accessible entrance ADA booth Ballot Marking Device Ask a poll worker if you need help. Ballots are translated into some languages at select poll sites. Interpretation is also offered at some poll sites. [Learn more about accessibility and language assistance at poll sites.](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03691)
What's on Your Ballot Candidates In this Primary Election, you can vote in various contests, including: Governor and Lieutenant Governor State Attorney General State Comptroller State Senate State Assembly Some voters may also see these on their ballot, depending on where they live:  U.S. House of Representatives  City Council (Council District 3 only) After the complete contest list is approved, you can preview the list of candidates on a sample ballot. [See who's on your ballot.](https://findmypollsite.vote.nyc/)
Voter Resources ​ [Check Registration Confirm your voter status, registered home address, and political party.](https://amiregistered.vote.nyc/) ​ [Poll Site Complaint Report a problem with a poll site or worker.](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02926) ​ [Stay Connected Sign up for text or email updates and reminders about upcoming elections.](https://www.nycvotes.org/get-involved/stay-informed/)
